providers.description: Cradle is a Dutch–Swiss biotechnology software company founded in 2021 with headquarters in Amsterdam and an office in Zurich, building an AI-powered protein engineering platform for industrial biotech and biopharma R&D teams. The platform combines proprietary generative AI models — trained on billions of natural protein sequences and on data produced in Cradle's own Amsterdam wet lab — with a web application and REST API/Python SDK so that scientists can design, simulate, and co-optimize amino-acid sequence variants across multiple measurable properties such as activity, binding affinity, stability, expression, and developability. Core platform capabilities include AI candidate generation, multi-property co-optimization, virtual plate design, experimental data management with full versioning and audit trails, task orchestration (analyze data, diversify, engineer, select, search, train) across modalities including antibodies/mAbs, enzymes, vaccines, therapeutic peptides, and food ingredients, plus a Custom Predictors framework letting customers plug in their own ML models. Cradle is sold as enterprise SaaS to R&D organizations — disclosed customers and partners include Johnson & Johnson Janssen, Bayer, Novozymes/Novonesis, and Twist Bioscience, with the platform serving six of the top 25 global pharma companies and over 50 active R&D programs. The company has raised approximately $115M to date across a seed round (Index Ventures, 2022), a $24M Series A (Index Ventures, 2023), and a $73M Series B (IVP, 2024). Co-founders are Stef van Grieken (CEO), Jelle Prins, Elise de Reus, Eli Bixby, and Harmen van Rossum.

providers.name: Paradromics
providers.description: Paradromics is a clinical-stage neurotechnology company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with a machine-learning and data-science office in Oakland, California, developing high-data-rate implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCI). Founded in 2019 by Matt Angle, the company builds the Connexus BCI, an investigational fully implantable system that records high-resolution intracortical neural activity and transmits it through the skin to an external system that decodes intended speech, text and digital device control for people with severe motor impairment. Connexus holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designations for speech decoding (2023) and digital device control (2024), was accepted into the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program, and received an Investigational Device Exemption in November 2025 for the Connect-One Early Feasibility Study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07357428). Tempo BCI is a pre-clinical-trial pipeline product. Paradromics publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its only machine-readable public surface is an llms.txt AI-context file at paradromics.com/llms.txt.

providers.name: Unlearn
providers.description: Unlearn is a San Francisco AI company that builds digital twin generators for clinical trials — machine learning models trained on patient-level historical data that forecast an individual participant's clinical outcomes under control or standard of care. Sponsors use these AI-generated digital twins to plan trials, monitor clinical data, and run smaller, more powerful studies; the approach is qualified by the EMA and aligned with current FDA guidance. Unlearn is backed by 8VC and DCVC and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Briya
providers.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Generation Lab
providers.description: Generation Lab is a longevity science company founded in 2023 by Alina Su, UC Berkeley bioengineer Dr. Irina Conboy, and Michael Suswal, and backed by an $11M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first longevity bet). Its flagship SystemAge test measures biological age across roughly 460 biomarkers spanning 19 to 21 physiological systems and organs from an at-home, needle-free blood collection, returning a personalized aging report and science-backed action plan that ranges from lifestyle and supplement guidance to clinical interventions. The test is distributed through 300+ clinic partners across 18 countries and via a patient/provider portal. Generation Lab publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public web, product, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: i-Brain Tech
providers.description: i-Brain Tech is a neuroscience company building a brain-controlled training platform for sports performance. Its core product is a video game driven exclusively by an athlete's brain impulses through motor-imagery and neurofeedback, requiring no physical movement. The platform is applied to three areas: post-injury neuromuscular recovery and return-to-play readiness, player development through cognitive and tactical training without physical strain, and cognitive assessment that surfaces mental resilience, attention, and endurance from real brain data. Elite football clubs including Real Sociedad, Juventus FC, CD Leganes, Olympique Lyonnais, S.L. Benfica, and Seattle Reign FC use the platform. i-Brain Tech is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Zageno
providers.description: ZAGENO is a multi-supplier e-commerce marketplace and procurement platform for pharma and life-science R&D labs. It lets scientists search, compare, and order more than 50 million SKUs from over 6,000 global suppliers through a single consolidated catalog and checkout, with real-time availability, spend visibility, and automated approval workflows. ZAGENO connects into enterprise procure-to-pay and ERP systems (Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer, Procurify, NetSuite, QuickBooks and more) through a single PunchOut/cXML catalog integration rather than a public developer API. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, it is backed by General Catalyst, Grazia Equity, and Capnamic Ventures.

providers.name: AstraZeneca
providers.description: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company focused on oncology, cardiovascular, renal, metabolism, and respiratory therapies. AstraZeneca does not publish a general developer portal or commercial public APIs; technology integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, clinical trial data portals such as clinicaltrials.gov and the Vivli platform, and EDI/x12 channels used by distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Outpost Bio
providers.description: Outpost Bio builds frontier AI foundation models for the human microbiome. Its "lab-in-the-loop" platform pairs high-throughput wet-lab experiments with machine learning in a continuous cycle to predict how drugs and ingredients interact with microbial ecosystems, helping de-risk drug and ingredient R&D decisions around metabolism, toxicity, and efficacy. The company's public developer surface is the open-source Waypoint Python library and CLI (published to PyPI as waypoint-bio) plus gated Waypoint model checkpoints, the Atlas pretraining dataset, and the Compass benchmark suite on the Hugging Face Hub. Outpost Bio is a Seedcamp portfolio company and does not currently publish a hosted web API.

providers.name: Kymera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kymera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 500 North Beacon Street in Watertown, Massachusetts, pioneering targeted protein degradation as a way to build oral small-molecule medicines against targets that conventional inhibitors cannot reach. Rather than blocking a protein's activity, Kymera's degraders recruit the body's own protein-disposal machinery so that a binding event alone is sufficient to eliminate the disease-driving protein, an approach the company describes as a disease-agnostic modality. Its wholly-owned pipeline is led by KT-621, a once-daily oral STAT6 degrader in Phase 2 for Type 2 inflammatory diseases including atopic dermatitis, asthma, COPD and chronic spontaneous urticaria, and KT-579, a first-in-class oral IRF5 degrader in Phase 1 for lupus, Sjogren's syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis. Partnered programs include the oral IRAK4 degrader KT-485/SAR447971 with Sanofi and the CDK2 molecular glue degrader KT-200 with Gilead Sciences. Kymera publishes no public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web, investor, patient and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Massive Bio
providers.description: Massive Bio is an AI-powered healthcare company that matches cancer patients with clinical trials. Its platform analyzes 500+ medical data elements — diagnosis, genomic profile, and clinical history — to deliver personalized trial-match reports within 24 hours, connecting patients, physicians, pharmaceutical sponsors, and research institutions. Products include a patient-facing matching service, the Trial Relay physician screening and referral tool, and iOS/Android mobile apps. The company reports 200,000+ registered patients and coverage of 19,000+ active oncology and hematology trials across multiple international markets. Massive Bio does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Pi Health
providers.description: Pi Health is an AI-native clinical trial technology company and contract research organization (CRO) building FICS, a unified operating system for oncology and global clinical trials. Its platform consolidates traditionally fragmented systems — Electronic Data Capture (EDC), Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), electronic Trial Master File (eTMF), electronic Investigator Site File (eISF), and an EMR-to-EDC Orchestrator — into a single AI-validated master record spanning study startup through closeout. Pi Health pairs the platform with CRO services and a global research network with oncology sites across the US, Brazil, Australia, and India. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this remains an identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API.

providers.name: Antheia
providers.description: Antheia, Inc. is a Menlo Park, California synthetic-biology company that manufactures biosynthetic key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for essential medicines. Founded on Christina Smolke's Stanford research, Antheia engineers yeast strains that reconstruct long, complex plant biosynthetic pathways and ferment sugar into molecules previously obtainable only through agricultural cultivation, compressing production timelines from years to weeks. Commercial products include fermentation-derived thebaine, oripavine and scopolamine, with a development pipeline of 70+ KSMs and APIs spanning neurology, gastrointestinal and oncology programs. NOTE FOR THE CATALOG: Antheia's "APIs" are Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not web APIs — the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Apnimed
providers.description: Apnimed is a late-stage clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing novel oral drug therapies for sleep-related breathing disorders. Its lead candidate AD109 (Oxnimbi) is a fixed-dose combination of an anti-muscarinic and a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, designed to improve upper-airway muscle activity and treat an underlying neuromuscular cause of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) rather than manage it mechanically. The company was founded in 2017, partners with Shionogi through the Shionogi-Apnimed Sleep Science (SASS) joint venture, and had a New Drug Application for AD109 accepted by the FDA in 2026. Apnimed is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: AusperBio
providers.description: AusperBio — AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. in the United States and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (杭州浩博医药有限公司) in Hangzhou, China — is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 that develops oligonucleotide and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B infection. Its proprietary Med-Oligo antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) platform pairs novel ASO design and optimization with targeted delivery conjugation chemistry, and its Au-HALO hepatocyte-targeting delivery technology extends the same modular approach to siRNA. The lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO that completed enrollment in two Phase II trials and received China CDE clearance to enter Phase III; a second clinical candidate, AHB-171, is a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA. The company has raised more than $200M across Series B, B+ and B2 rounds from investors including Qiming Venture Partners, HanKang Capital, CDH Investments, Sherpa Capital, YuanBio Venture Capital and Genesis Capital. AusperBio sells therapeutics, not software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable surface is the private Spring Boot CMS backend that renders ausperbio.com, whose springdoc API description is correctly locked behind authentication.

providers.name: ClearNote Health
providers.description: ClearNote Health (formerly Bluestar Genomics) is a US cancer detection company with offices in San Diego and San Mateo, California. Its proprietary 5hmC epigenomic platform combines cell-free DNA sequencing from a standard blood draw with machine learning to identify DNA-based alterations as cancer develops. The company commercializes Avantect, a suite of early-detection liquid biopsy tests for pancreatic and ovarian cancer that clinicians order through its laboratory, and Virtuoso, a research-use-only epigenomics platform sold to biopharma for drug discovery, therapy response and resistance research. ClearNote Health publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification: the clinician ordering path is a hosted intake form, and its public GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source bioinformatics tooling.

providers.name: Eureka Therapeutics
providers.description: Eureka Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Emeryville, California, developing T-cell therapies for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. The company was founded by Dr. Cheng Liu and is built on two proprietary platforms: E-ALPHA, a high-throughput human antibody discovery engine used to find binders against cancer-specific targets, and ARTEMIS, an engineered T-cell receptor platform (AbTCR) designed to deliver CAR-T-level potency with a reduced cytokine-release profile. Its clinical programs include ET140203 (ARYA-1 in adults, ARYA-2 in pediatrics) and ECT204 (ARYA-3) in advanced liver cancer, alongside a GPC2 ARTEMIS T-cell program for neuroblastoma licensed from the National Cancer Institute. Eureka publishes a corporate website, pipeline and technology overviews, a press-release archive with an RSS feed, and patient-facing trial information; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Galvanize Therapeutics
providers.description: Galvanize Therapeutics, Inc. is a Redwood City, California medical device company founded in 2015 by Jonathan Waldstreicher, MD and William Krimsky, MD, and created and incubated by Apple Tree Partners (ATP). Galvanize develops pulsed electric field (PEF) therapies that deliver high-voltage, short-duration energy locally to alter the transmembrane potential of targeted cells, inducing non-thermal regulated cell death without denaturing cellular proteins or the extracellular matrix. Its Aliya PEF System is cleared for surgical ablation of soft tissue and is being studied in non-small cell lung cancer, while RheOx addresses chronic bronchitis in the airway. The company received FDA 510(k) clearance for the Aliya EX Generator in May 2026. Galvanize is a privately held, clinically-focused device manufacturer and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Geltor
providers.description: Geltor is a biodesign company founded in 2015 by Alex Lorestani and Nick Ouzounov that engineers animal-free designer proteins, peptides and polypeptides and manufactures them through precision fermentation. Its Biodesigner AI computational biology platform is used to imagine, screen and optimize novel protein sequences, which are then scaled commercially as ingredients for beauty and personal care, specialty nutrition and medical/life-science applications. The portfolio includes HumaColl 21 (biomimetic human collagen), HumaColl 21 Select (a matrikine peptide complex), Elastapure (biomimetic human elastin), Collume and Caviance (vegan collagens) and PrimaColl, a Type XXI signaling collagen and the first biotech-derived collagen to receive an FDA GRAS "no questions" letter for ingestible use. Geltor sells business-to-business to brand formulators and manufacturers; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Grail
providers.description: GRAIL, Inc. is a healthcare company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, focused on detecting cancer early, when it can be cured. Its flagship product, the Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, uses a single blood draw and methylation-based genomic sequencing to screen for a signal shared across more than 50 types of cancer, many of which lack any recommended screening today. GRAIL runs large clinical programs including the PATHFINDER, PATHFINDER 2, and NHS-Galleri studies, and distributes Galleri through health plans, employers, and partners such as Quest Diagnostics and Junction. GRAIL is a portfolio company of investors including GV and SV Angel. It does not publish a first-party public developer API; programmatic access to Galleri ordering is offered through third-party diagnostic infrastructure partners.

providers.name: LabGenius Therapeutics
providers.description: LabGenius Therapeutics is a London-based drug discovery company that combines machine learning, high-throughput robotic experimentation and synthetic biology to discover and co-optimise next-generation therapeutic antibodies for solid tumours. Its EVA (Experimental Vector Automation) platform is a closed-loop, modality-agnostic discovery engine that runs a design-build-test-learn cycle in under six weeks — computationally designing multispecific antibodies in the dry lab, then cloning, expressing, purifying and functionally screening up to 2,300 multispecifics per cycle in an automated wet lab, and feeding the resulting proprietary data back into multi-objective ML models. The company operates a wholly-owned pipeline of selectivity-enhanced T-cell engagers alongside partnered antibody-optimisation programmes with Sanofi. LabGenius is a pre-clinical therapeutics company and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public web and machine-readable surface only.

providers.name: Nautilus Biotechnology
providers.description: Nautilus Biotechnology is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: NAUT) life-sciences company developing a single-molecule protein analysis platform aimed at unlocking the proteome for basic biology, medicine, and drug discovery. Its Voyager platform pairs a novel single-molecule proteomics instrument with reagents and software to quantify and map proteoforms at scale. The company partners with academic and pharmaceutical researchers on applications spanning biomarker discovery and the drug-development process. Nautilus operates as a research-tools and instrument company; it publishes a corporate site, blog, resource library, and investor relations pages, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Onco.com
providers.description: Onco.com is a comprehensive cancer care platform operated by Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd that connects cancer patients across India with oncologists and treatment services. The platform offers priority expert oncology consultations, pan-India cancer medicine delivery at discounted rates, diagnostic testing and imaging, curated treatment packages with negotiated hospital rates, and the CanWin peer support group for survivors and caregivers. Onco.com reports a network of 400+ oncologists and 23+ treatment centers, having served more than 100,000 patients. It also publishes extensive patient-education content covering many cancer types (breast, lung, blood, prostate, colon, and others) through its About Cancer library and blog. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company; the platform is consumer/patient facing and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Opna Bio
providers.description: Opna Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology, developing novel small-molecule and targeted-degrader therapeutics against key regulators of cancer, including the Hallmarks of Cancer. Its pipeline features OPN-6602 (an EP300/CBP inhibitor in Phase 1 for multiple myeloma, granted FDA Fast Track designation), zavabresib (OPN-2853, a BET inhibitor with Orphan Drug designation for myelofibrosis), multi-functional protein degraders, and additional programs targeting hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. The company operates from South San Francisco and San Diego, California, and Lausanne, Switzerland.

providers.name: Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE)
providers.description: Pedestal Health, formerly Target RWE (and NoviSci), is a Durham, North Carolina real-world evidence and health-data company serving life sciences organizations and health systems. It generates regulatory-grade real-world evidence from large-scale observational data and longitudinal patient cohorts across hepatology, dermatology, and gastroenterology (including the TARGET-NASH, TARGET-Derm, and TARGET-Gastro registries), supporting clinical development, regulatory strategy, and care delivery. The company operates as a data, research, and services provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched from the company's public website (targetrwe.com now redirects to pedestalhealth.com).

providers.name: QurAlis
providers.description: QurAlis Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded on December 12, 2016 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Drs. Kasper Roet, Kevin Eggan and Clifford Woolf together with Q-State Biosciences, and staffed by neurodegenerative biologists out of Harvard Medical School and Harvard University. The company develops precision medicines for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and other neurodegenerative and neurological diseases, built on the discovery — published in Nature Neuroscience by co-founder Kevin Eggan's lab — that loss of normal TDP-43 function drives a decrease in STATHMIN-2 (STMN2) expression and impairs neuronal repair. Its lead candidates are QRL-201, a first-in-class molecule intended to restore STMN2 expression in ALS (ANQUR trial), and QRL-101, a potentially best-in-class selective Kv7.2/7.3 ion channel opener for hyperexcitability-induced disease progression in ALS as well as epilepsy and pain; a third program targets UNC13A cryptic-exon mis-splicing. Therapies are built on the proprietary FlexASO® anti-sense oligonucleotide splice-modulator platform. QurAlis publishes a corporate site covering its story, pipeline, platform, people, patient resources, presentations and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Repertoire Immune Medicines
providers.description: Repertoire Immune Medicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company (with a site in Schlieren, Switzerland) building immune medicines grounded in the human T cell repertoire. Its proprietary DECODE platform characterizes the immune synapse by identifying T cell receptor (TCR) and antigen (peptide-MHC) pairs together with T cell function and HLA presentation, and uses that map to rationally design treatments across oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease. Backed by Flagship Pioneering and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It publishes no public developer API; its only public technical surface is a small research GitHub organization.

providers.name: Xaira
providers.description: Xaira Therapeutics is a South San Francisco-based biotechnology company building the transformative artificial intelligence that discovers and develops the next generation of medicines. Founded in 2023 and launched publicly in 2024 out of ARCH Venture Partners and Foresight Labs, Xaira couples large-scale generative and predictive AI models with in-house wet-lab data generation to design novel therapeutics, shorten development timelines, and lower the cost of bringing medicines to patients. The company's research spans protein design, molecular machine learning, and genome-scale perturbation modeling (its open X-Cell diffusion language model). Xaira does not currently operate a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web, security, and open-source research surface.

providers.name: Beacon Biosignals
providers.description: Beacon Biosignals develops AI-powered neurotechnology for brain health, applying machine learning to EEG (electroencephalography) data at scale. Its platform serves two markets: precision neuroscience for drug development, where it collects and analyzes EEG across the clinical trial lifecycle (2M+ hours of EEG analyzed across 40+ trials), and home sleep testing diagnostics through the SleepView Monitor and SleepView Direct products (500K+ home sleep tests completed). Beacon is also a prolific open-source contributor in the Julia ecosystem, publishing signal-data and modeling libraries such as Onda.jl, Legolas.jl, EDF.jl, Effects.jl, and Lighthouse.jl. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a life-sciences / neurotech provider; Beacon does not publish a public developer API, so this profile centers on its open-source software surface and company identity.

providers.name: Ring Therapeutics
providers.description: Ring Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering that develops targeted vector conjugate medicines built on the human commensal virome. Its Anellogy platform harnesses anelloviruses — commensal viruses that co-exist with the human immune system — to generate gene delivery vectors with tissue-specific tropism and the potential to be redosed. Ring has sequenced thousands of anelloviruses into what it describes as the largest anellovirus database assembled to date, and has raised more than $250 million across Series A, B and C financings. The company is a therapeutics developer rather than a software provider: it publishes a corporate site, a press release stream and a scientific publications list, and operates no public API, developer portal or SDK.

providers.name: Terray Therapeutics
providers.description: Terray Therapeutics is an AI-native, chemistry-first biotechnology company building an integrated full-stack platform for small molecule drug discovery. Its EMMI platform (Experimentation Meets Machine Intelligence) pairs a proprietary ultra-miniaturized microarray assay system and fully automated lab with a family of machine learning models: COATI, a chemistry foundation model trained on roughly a billion molecules that encodes molecules into a latent space; reinforcement-learning generative models for synthesizable de novo design; TerraBind for potency prediction; and EMMI Select for uncertainty-aware molecule selection. Terray reports a proprietary target-molecule interaction dataset of more than 17 billion measurements growing by about a billion per quarter, and runs multi-target discovery collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Gilead, Calico and Odyssey Therapeutics, with investment from NVIDIA. Terray publishes several of its research code libraries as open source on GitHub (COATI, COATI-LDM, TerraMax) but operates no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Aculys
providers.description: Aculys Pharma, Inc. is a Japanese clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on neurological and psychiatric diseases where there is high unmet medical need. The company works to eliminate Japan's drug lag and drug loss by bringing innovative medicines already approved in Western markets to Japanese patients as early as possible. Its lead product is Spydia (diazepam nasal spray), Japan's first domestically developed intranasal anti-seizure agent, approved in June 2025 and administrable outside medical facilities. Originally funded by SoftBank Vision Fund (Series C, March 2025), Aculys was acquired by and became part of the Viatris Group in October 2025. Aculys publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained for network completeness and identity.

providers.name: Calviri
providers.description: Calviri is a Phoenix, Arizona biotechnology company, founded in 2017, that develops multi-cancer diagnostic tests and therapeutic and preventative cancer vaccines for dogs and people. Its science rests on RNA-Error Derived Neoantigens (REDNs) — abnormal proteins thrown off by the error-prone RNA processing of tumor cells — which Calviri builds as peptides on semiconductor chips and then queries against an individual's blood for antibody responses, using those antibodies as sensitive biomarkers of cancer. Its lead product, StageOne Plus, is a canine multi-cancer blood test designed to detect stage 1 disease before signs appear, alongside a pipeline of canine and human therapeutic and preventative vaccines and a preventative-vaccine trial (VACCS) that enrolled 800+ dogs. Calviri is a life-sciences company with no developer program, no product API and no developer portal; the only machine-readable surface on calviri.com is the Wix-platform-generated llms.txt and the anonymous site MCP endpoint it advertises.

providers.name: Biosplice Therapeutics
providers.description: Biosplice Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2008 by Osman Kibar and known until its 2020 rename as Samumed, LLC (samumed.com still redirects to biosplice.com). The company develops first-in-class small-molecule therapeutics that act on novel components of the Wnt signaling pathway and on the regulation of alternative pre-mRNA splicing. Its lead program is lorecivivint, an investigational intra-articular knee injection for osteoarthritis, positioned against a stated unmet need of "over 50 million US patients suffer from osteoarthritis, with no drugs available to arrest the disease"; the candidate has completed Phase 3 study and a New Drug Application has been submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Programs outside lorecivivint — neurology, diabetes and oncology — are developed by the company's affiliate TenaRx, Inc. The company is led by Erich Horsley (Chief Executive Officer) with Osman Kibar as Founder and Executive Chairman, Yusuf Yazici as Chief Medical Officer, Phil Wilson as Chief Financial Officer and Scott W. Bulcao as Chief Legal Officer. Biosplice is a drug-discovery and clinical-development organization, not a software vendor: biosplice.com is a small ASP.NET corporate site covering mission, board, management, advisors, programs, publications, news and careers, and the company publishes no developer program of any kind — no API, no SDK, no developer portal, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.description: Foundation Medicine is a molecular information and precision cancer diagnostics company that develops comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) tests for solid tumors, blood cancers, and sarcomas, including its FoundationOne family of assays. Its testing analyzes patient tumor and liquid-biopsy samples to identify genomic alterations that can inform targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and clinical-trial matching, and it partners with biopharma on companion diagnostics and clinical-trial enrollment. A Roche company, it has delivered more than 1.5 million patient CGP reports and supports 950+ clinical trials. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead (gv, kleiner-perkins) and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public developer API or portal, so this record captures its public web, legal, and security-disclosure surface.

providers.name: 1910 Genetics
providers.description: 1910 Genetics (now branded 1910) is an AI-native biotechnology company advancing small and large molecule drug discovery with a multimodal AI platform powered by high-throughput laboratory automation. Its ITO platform integrates computational data, wet-lab proxy biological data, and wet-lab ground-truth biological data to pursue "modality agnostic" drug discovery, alongside named AI models including PEGASUS (macrocyclic peptide discovery) and CANDID-CNS (CNS-penetration prediction). The company partners with pharma and technology organizations and offers co-engineering collaborations at the data, AI-model, compute, and interactive-tool levels. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Playground Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Attovia Therapeutics
providers.description: Attovia Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in San Carlos, California, founded in 2022 and developing next-generation precision biologics for immune-mediated diseases. Its proprietary ATTOBODY platform is a modular protein design technology built on biparatopic nanobody scaffolds, used to engineer multispecific biologics that inhibit two, three, or four disease-driving pathways from a single molecule while targeting improved selectivity, stability, and less frequent dosing than existing therapies. The lead program ATTO-1310 is an anti-IL-31 candidate in Phase 1 for chronic pruritus and high-itch atopic dermatitis; ATTO-2306 (IL-31 x IL-13) and ATTO-1091 (TL1A x IL-23p19 x integrin alpha-4-beta-7, for inflammatory bowel disease) are in IND-enabling studies, alongside discovery-stage programs in rheumatology, IBD, and respiratory disease. The company raised a $105M Series B led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives and listed on Nasdaq as ATTO in August 2026, raising $289M. Attovia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification — its product is therapeutics, not software.

providers.name: Attralus
providers.description: Attralus is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Francisco, California, developing transformative medicines for patients with systemic amyloidosis. Its proprietary pan-amyloid removal (PAR) platform pairs a pan-amyloid binding peptide with a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody so the resulting fusion protein binds amyloid deposits across every amyloidosis type and stage and recruits the immune system to clear them. The lead candidate, zamubafusp alfa (AT-02), is a pan-amyloid depleter in a Phase 1/2 open-label extension study and has received U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of AL amyloidosis; a next-generation PAR program (IV and subcutaneous) and a research-stage neurodegeneration program targeting Abeta, tau and alpha-synuclein aggregates follow behind it. Attralus' molecular imaging agents AT-01 (124-iodine evuzamitide) and AT-05 (99mTc-p5+14) were acquired by Bayer in January 2026. The company was launched in 2020 with a Series A from venBio Partners and has since raised additional rounds including a $56 million financing led by Alpha Wave Ventures with participation from Bristol Myers Squibb. Attralus is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract of any kind (every OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A and /.well-known/ path probed on its hosts returns 404, and no api/developer/docs subdomain resolves).

providers.name: Day One Biopharmaceuticals
providers.description: Day One Biopharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing targeted therapies for people of all ages living with life-threatening diseases, with an initial focus on pediatric and rare cancers. Its lead product OJEMDA (tovorafenib) is an FDA-approved treatment for relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma, and its pipeline includes DAY301 and the antibody-drug conjugate Emi-Le. Headquartered in Brisbane, California, the company was acquired by and is now part of the Servier Group as of March 2026. Day One was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it maintains a corporate and investor-relations web presence but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Liquidia
providers.description: Liquidia Corporation (NASDAQ: LQDA) is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of inhaled therapies for cardiopulmonary disease, specifically pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD). Its proprietary PRINT technology produces drug particles of uniform size and shape engineered for deep-lung deposition, and underpins YUTREPIA, its inhaled treprostinil dry powder product. Liquidia is also developing L606, a sustained-release liposomal treprostinil inhalation suspension partnered with Pharmosa Biopharm. Liquidia publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable interface; this profile is catalogued for network identity, corporate transparency, and domain-security coverage only.

providers.name: Aardvark Therapeutics
providers.description: Aardvark Therapeutics, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed (AARD) clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel small-molecule therapies designed to inhibit hunger and treat metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, ARD-101, is an oral, gut-restricted agonist of bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) on the luminal side of the intestine, which triggers the release of satiety hormones to suppress hunger signaling; it has been evaluated for hyperphagia associated with Prader-Willi Syndrome, including the Phase 3 HERO trial, as well as in obesity and hypothalamic obesity. The company operates purely as a drug-development organization: its public web presence consists of science, programs, team, news and investor-relations material, and it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Ensoma
providers.description: Ensoma is a privately held, clinical-stage genomic medicines company developing in vivo hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) engineering. Its platform pairs an off-the-shelf in vivo delivery system built on high-capacity virus-like particles that preferentially bind HSCs with a gene engineering toolkit spanning base editing and high-efficiency gene integration, carrying payloads of roughly 35 kilobases so that changes from single-base edits through multi-gene insertions can be made without ex vivo cell collection, manipulation, or transplant conditioning. The company is pursuing programs across genetic disease, immune disorders, and oncology, including EN-374 for X-linked chronic granulomatous disease, and is backed by 5AM Ventures, F-Prime Capital, RTW Investments, Alexandria Venture Investments, Cormorant Asset Management, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Enrichment found no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI contract, MCP server, or agent card — this is a therapeutics R&D company, not an API provider. Its only public machine-readable output is open-source computational genomics and sequencing-pipeline code published under its GitHub organization.

providers.name: Lila Sciences
providers.description: Lila Sciences is an AI company founded in 2023 that is building what it calls Scientific Superintelligence: an autonomous system that runs the scientific method end to end by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, executing them in physical AI Science Factories (autonomous robotic laboratory networks), and learning from the resulting experimental data. Rather than training on internet text, Lila trains a scientific reasoning model on experimental data, coupling it to scalable verifiers and instruments such as molecular dynamics simulators, protein structure predictors, quantum chemistry solvers, and gene editors, then optimizing the policy with reinforcement learning. The company packages this as two commercial offerings: Catalyst, positioned as an operating system for science that accelerates an organization's existing research, and Creation, a partnership model for generating new discoveries, launching products, and founding new companies. Lila works across therapeutics (mRNA, proteins, antibodies, cell therapies, small molecules), advanced materials, chemicals, energy and environment, oil and gas, aerospace and defense, and biotech. It has raised roughly $550M ($200M seed announced March 2025 and a $350M Series A closed in October 2025) from investors including General Catalyst and NVIDIA, at a reported valuation above $1.3B, and collaborates with NVIDIA on the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit. Lila operates from Cambridge MA, San Francisco CA, and London UK. As of this profile Lila publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this entry is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AbelZeta Pharma
providers.description: AbelZeta Pharma is a global clinical-stage cell therapy company discovering, developing, and manufacturing T-cell-based immunotherapeutics for cancer and immunological diseases. Its pipeline centers on Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T cell technology across hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, and inflammatory and immunological conditions. Backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China), AbelZeta develops personalized immune cell therapies that empower patients' own immune systems to address unmet medical needs, with operations in the United States (Maryland) and China. AbelZeta does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate web presence and identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Abogen Biosciences
providers.description: Abogen Biosciences (Suzhou Abogen Biosciences, 苏州艾博生物科技有限公司) is an industry-leading clinical-stage biotech company founded in January 2019 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, dedicated to developing transformative medicines through messenger RNA (mRNA) innovation. The company has built full-scale in-house capabilities spanning the entire mRNA drug-development cycle — protein engineering, mRNA sequence design and synthesis, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, formulation, and commercial-scale manufacturing — underpinned by proprietary mRNA and nano-delivery technology platforms. Its pipeline covers infectious-disease prevention and tumor immunology, including an EUA-authorized product and multiple clinical-stage candidates. Abogen is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced through the API Evangelist VC-portfolio enrichment pipeline; the company publishes a corporate website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Acclinate
providers.description: Acclinate is a health-equity technology company that improves clinical trial diversity by building trust with historically underrepresented communities. Its NOWINCLUDED community platform engages 250,000+ members with culturally relevant content and in-person events, while its proprietary e-DICT AI/ML engine transforms community trust signals into predictive enrollment intelligence — participation-probability scoring, demographic forecasting, and real-time dashboards for pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs. Acclinate operates as a managed service across a three-stage trust model (Access, Engage, Mobilize) rather than a self-service developer platform; no public API, developer portal, or API documentation is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Affinia Therapeutics
providers.description: Affinia Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in Waltham, Massachusetts pioneering next-generation adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapies. Using AI and structural modeling to rationally design novel capsids that better target tissues for improved safety and effectiveness, Affinia develops therapeutic cargoes for devastating rare and prevalent diseases of the heart and the nervous system. Its lead program, AFTX-201, targets BAG3-associated dilated cardiomyopathy and is being evaluated in the UPBEAT trial. Affinia Therapeutics is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This company profile carries no public API surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network for identity and demand signal.

providers.name: AgNovos Bioscience
providers.description: AgNovos Bioscience is a privately held medical technology company developing novel treatments for bone disease, founded in 2012 with offices in New York, Rockville (Maryland), Frankfurt and Dallas. Its lead technology is AGN1, a proprietary triphasic, calcium-based, osteoconductive implant material delivered through the OSSURE Local Osteo-Enhancement Procedure (LOEP) — a minimally invasive procedure intended to immediately, substantially and durably increase the density and strength of osteoporotic bone at sites of highest fracture risk. The company runs an active clinical program (CONFIRM, RECONFIRM, RESTORE and GRACE trials) and sponsors the ESCEO-AgNovos Young Investigator Award. AgNovos ships a physical implant and surgical kit, not software: its public web presence is a corporate and clinical-communications site with no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Alcresta Therapeutics
providers.description: Alcresta Therapeutics is a specialty pharmaceutical company developing enzyme-based products that improve fat absorption and digestive health for people with rare and chronic conditions. Its lead product, the RELiZORB (immobilized lipase) cartridge, uses the company's patented iLipase microbead technology to mimic pancreatic lipase and hydrolyze fats in enteral (tube) feeding formulas, helping patients with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, cystic fibrosis, short bowel syndrome, and critical-care nutrition needs absorb fatty acids they otherwise could not. Alcresta is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The company operates a corporate and product marketing website but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Alector
providers.description: Alector is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing immuno-neurology therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, including frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Alzheimer's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Combining human genetics, neuroscience, and immunology, the company designs potential first- and best-in-class medicines that remove toxic proteins, replace deficient proteins, and restore immune and nerve cell function. Alector was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile captures corporate and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Alloy Therapeutics
providers.description: Alloy Therapeutics is a biotechnology ecosystem company operating as a Product Development Organization that partners across discovery, preclinical, and clinical development. It combines proprietary AI/ML, real-world data, and tech-enabled scientific services across multiple therapeutic modalities, including monoclonal and bispecific antibodies, TCR mimics, genetic medicines (cyclic RNA and oligonucleotide design), and cell-therapy pharmacology. Alloy is known for its transgenic antibody-discovery platforms (the ATX-Gx mouse series) and licenses reagents, platforms, and services to pharmaceutical and biotech partners rather than exposing a public developer API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Alpha-9 Oncology
providers.description: Alpha-9 Oncology is a clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company that spun out of the University of British Columbia and BC Cancer in 2019 to develop a portfolio of targeted cancer therapies. Alpha-9 engineers bespoke radiopharmaceutical molecules — optimizing the binder, linker, chelator, and radioisotope — to deliver radiation directly to tumor cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. The company operates purpose-built research facilities in Vancouver, BC and Boston, MA, and in October 2024 raised an oversubscribed $175M Series C led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Ascenta Capital to advance its clinical pipeline. Alpha-9 is a drug developer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and public-web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ancora Heart
providers.description: Ancora Heart, Inc. is a privately held medical device company headquartered at 4001 Burton Drive, Santa Clara, California, developing transcatheter therapies for people living with heart failure. Its lead product is the AccuCinch Ventricular Restoration System, a completely transcatheter implant designed to reduce the size of an enlarged left ventricle and restore cardiac structure and function in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) who remain symptomatic on guideline-directed medical therapy. The device is investigational and is being evaluated in the CORCINCH-HF study (NCT04331769), a prospective randomized international trial enrolling up to 400 patients across as many as 80 centers, alongside the CORCINCH-EU program in Europe. Ancora Heart is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes a marketing and clinical-information website for patients and physicians, and operates no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Apollomics, Inc.
providers.description: Apollomics, Inc. (Nasdaq: APLM) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Foster City, California, focused on the discovery and development of oncology therapies designed to be combined with other treatments to harness the immune system and target specific molecular pathways that inhibit cancer. Operating since 2016, Apollomics has a pipeline of nine drug candidates spanning small-molecule targeted drugs and biologics, including late-stage programs such as vebreltinib (Phase 2, NSCLC and solid tumors with cMet dysregulation) and uproleselan (Phase 3 in China for relapsed/refractory AML). The company became publicly traded via a business combination with Maxpro Capital Acquisition Corp. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; as a biopharmaceutical company it publishes no public developer API surface — this profile carries its corporate identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: asieris
providers.description: Asieris Pharmaceuticals is a China-based biopharmaceutical company developing innovative therapies in genitourinary tumors and women's health. Its focus areas span urologic oncology (bladder cancer diagnosis and treatment), women's health, and breast and gynecologic oncology, with marquee assets Vesique (APL-1202) for bladder cancer and Cevira (APL-1702), a non-invasive photodynamic therapy for cervical precancerous lesions. The company runs three proprietary R&D platforms (TIMN, TAIDD, DDC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; as a biopharma company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Carbon Health
providers.description: Carbon Health is a technology-enabled healthcare provider offering primary, urgent, virtual, and pediatric care through in-person clinics and telemedicine across the United States. It operates on its own clinical technology platform (CarbyOS) and offers services including same-day appointments, cold/flu/COVID testing, STI/STD testing, sports physicals, occupational and workplace health, and clinical research for sponsors. Carbon Health was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or FHIR patient-access surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on transforming the treatment of cardiovascular disease and heart failure. Its research and development pipeline centers on novel small-molecule programs including PDE9 inhibition for chronic heart failure (HFrEF and HFpEF) and CaMKII inhibition for cardiac diseases such as catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). Cardurion combines target discovery, adaptive clinical trial design, and precision-medicine approaches, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). The company publishes a corporate and R&D website but does not expose a public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cerevance
providers.description: Cerevance is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Its proprietary NETSseq platform profiles gene expression across specific human brain cell types from post-mortem tissue to identify previously undiscovered, cell-type-specific drug targets, powering a pipeline of small-molecule candidates for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, epilepsy, and other neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Cerevance publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Cirsium Biosciences
providers.description: Cirsium Biosciences is a biotechnology company democratizing gene therapy through transformative manufacturing methods. It develops viral vector production systems that use whole plants as bioreactors, offering a highly scalable, linear scale-out platform for producing recombinant AAV (adeno-associated virus) vectors. The plant-based, controlled-environment agriculture approach targets the industry's core production bottlenecks - inadequate global capacity, poor scalability, high clinical-grade manufacturing costs, and standardization challenges - claiming up to a 70% reduction in manufacturing lead times. Cirsium is a private, venture-backed therapeutics-manufacturing firm and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Condorsoftware
providers.description: Condor Software builds AI-powered financial intelligence software for life sciences R&D organizations, unifying clinical, operational, and financial data to manage complex clinical trial finances. The platform connects data from existing systems (CROs, ERP, CTMS, EDC, procurement), automates AI-powered accruals, invoice reconciliation, and financial close, and delivers board-ready forecasts, scenario planning, and portfolio dashboards for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. Condor advertises 90%+ forecast accuracy, faster month-end close versus spreadsheets, and a compliance-by-design architecture co-developed with Big 4 accounting firms. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; integrations with systems such as Veeva, Medidata, SAP, and Oracle NetSuite are delivered through the product. Backed by Felicis; raised a $24M Series A.

providers.name: Connect Biopharma
providers.description: Connect Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, dedicated to transforming care for patients with inflammatory diseases such as asthma and COPD. Its lead drug candidate, rademikibart (CBP-201), is an antibody targeting IL-4Ra in Phase 2 clinical development for acute asthma and COPD exacerbations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network, the company operates in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sector and publishes no public developer portal, API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: crownbio
providers.description: Crown Bioscience (CrownBio) is a global contract research organization (CRO) specializing in translational oncology and immuno-oncology drug discovery. It provides preclinical and translational services to biotech and pharmaceutical companies, including in vitro drug screening (cell lines, organoids, panels), in vivo studies (PDX, CDX, syngeneic and humanized models), DMPK/toxicology, preclinical imaging, and biomarker analysis spanning genomics (NGS, single-cell sequencing), proteomics, spatial biology, and flow cytometry. CrownBio also operates public web-browsable cancer-model databases — a PDX Model Database (2,500+ models), an Organoid Models Database (600+ models), an IO Murine Models Database, and a Cell Line / CDX Database — searchable through a Multi-Model Search interface. There is no public developer API or programmatic data access; the databases are web interfaces. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Delfi Diagnostics
providers.description: DELFI Diagnostics is a precision oncology company, founded in 2019 and built on research from the Johns Hopkins Kimmel Cancer Center, that combines machine learning with genome-wide analysis of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns (an approach it calls DNA fragmentomics, or "fragmentomes") to develop accessible, blood-based cancer screening and treatment-monitoring tests. Its first commercial product, FirstLook Lung, is a laboratory-developed liquid biopsy screening test for lung cancer that runs from a simple blood draw and reports a high negative predictive value; the company also offers DELFI-TF for treatment monitoring and partners with health systems and pharmaceutical researchers. DELFI operates a CLIA laboratory and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network; DELFI publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Editas Medicine
providers.description: Editas Medicine is a clinical-stage genome editing company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing durable, precision CRISPR-based gene editing medicines for people with serious diseases. The company works across in vivo and ex vivo approaches and holds foundational CRISPR/Cas9 and Cas12a intellectual property, advancing a pipeline that has included programs in sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia and inherited retinal disorders. Editas Medicine trades on Nasdaq under the ticker EDIT and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). As a life-sciences research and therapeutics organization it publishes a corporate and investor-relations web presence rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: eGenesis
providers.description: eGenesis is a biotechnology company working at the intersection of genome engineering and transplantation to make organ transplants accessible to all. Using a multiplex CRISPR gene-editing and genome-engineering platform, eGenesis engineers porcine (pig) donor organs that are immunologically and molecularly compatible with human recipients and free of porcine endogenous retroviruses, aiming to end waitlist mortality by removing donor-organ scarcity as a barrier to transplantation. Its pipeline spans kidney, liver, and heart xenotransplantation programs; the U.S. FDA has cleared its IND for EGEN-2784, a genetically engineered porcine kidney, to begin a Phase 1/2/3 trial in patients with end-stage kidney disease. eGenesis is a private, venture-backed company (investors include Lux Capital). This API Evangelist profile tracks the company for network discovery; eGenesis publishes a corporate and scientific web presence but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: eGenesis
providers.description: eGenesis is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing human-compatible, genetically engineered organs to address the global organ shortage. Using a proprietary CRISPR-based multiplex genome-editing platform, eGenesis modifies the porcine genome to inactivate endogenous retroviruses and add protective human transgenes, producing pig kidneys, livers, and hearts intended for xenotransplantation. Its lead program, EGEN-2784, is a genetically engineered porcine kidney being evaluated in an expanded-access study. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; eGenesis publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Enveda
providers.description: Enveda is a Boulder, Colorado based drug discovery company that combines artificial intelligence with the chemistry of nature to accelerate the development of new medicines. Its platform mines the vast chemical diversity of plants and other natural sources, using machine learning to decode complex natural compounds, identify their chemical structures and biological activity, and surface novel drug candidates faster than traditional approaches. Enveda was surfaced as a portfolio company of True Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private biotechnology and drug discovery firm it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, security posture, and web properties.

providers.name: Erasca
providers.description: Erasca is a clinical-stage precision oncology company (NASDAQ: ERAS) headquartered in San Diego, California, whose name is its mission: to erase cancer. The company is singularly focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing therapies for RAS- and MAPK pathway-driven cancers. RAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene and the MAPK pathway one of the most frequently altered signaling pathways in cancer, together accounting for roughly five million newly diagnosed patients globally each year. Erasca pursues three complementary therapeutic strategies intended to comprehensively shut down the RAS/MAPK pathway by targeting multiple nodes and cooperative mechanisms in parallel. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio-linked lead; as a therapeutics company Erasca publishes a corporate and investor web presence rather than a developer API surface, so this record captures verified company identity, legal, and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Escient Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Escient Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class, oral small-molecule therapeutics targeting Mas-related G protein-coupled receptors (MRGPRs) along the neurosensory-inflammatory axis. Its lead programs are EP262, an MRGPRX2 antagonist for mast-cell-mediated diseases such as chronic spontaneous and inducible urticaria and atopic dermatitis, and EP547, an MRGPRX4 antagonist for cholestatic and uremic pruritus. The company was backed by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and was acquired by Incyte Corporation on May 30, 2024. Escient operates a corporate marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API specification; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: Frontage Laboratories
providers.description: Frontage Laboratories is a global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated, science-driven drug discovery and development services across the pharmaceutical and biotechnology lifecycle. Its services span drug discovery (chemistry, biology, ADME/toxicology screening, pharmacology), drug development (DMPK, preclinical safety and toxicology, clinical trial support), laboratory testing (bioanalysis, genomics, central lab, biomarkers), CMC (product development, formulation, analytical services, manufacturing), and agrochemical support. Frontage operates roughly 28 sites across North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe with about 2,200 employees. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Frontage publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface, so this profile captures company identity and web properties only.

providers.name: Ideaya Biosciences
providers.description: IDEAYA Biosciences is a clinical-stage precision medicine oncology company headquartered in South San Francisco, California (NASDAQ IDYA), focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing targeted therapeutics for genetically defined cancer patient populations. Its research spans PKC inhibition in uveal melanoma, antibody-drug conjugate and DNA-damage-response combinations, synthetic-lethal MTAP-pathway programs, and KAT6/7 epigenetic inhibition, led by the investigational candidate darovasertib in registrational uveal melanoma trials. The company maintains a corporate and investor-relations web presence and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Impelpharma
providers.description: Impel Pharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company developing first-in-class intranasal drug treatments for central nervous system (CNS) disorders with high unmet medical needs. Its proprietary Precision Olfactory Delivery (POD) technology targets the vascular-rich upper nasal cavity to achieve more rapid and consistent bioavailability than conventional delivery. Its lead product, Trudhesa (dihydroergotamine mesylate) nasal spray, is approved for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Impel was backed by Norwest Venture Partners (co-led its 2018 Series D) and later filed for bankruptcy in December 2023. This is a patient- and science-facing pharma company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Iterative Health (fka Iterative Scopes)
providers.description: Iterative Health (formerly Iterative Scopes) is a healthcare and life-sciences company that operates an AI-enabled clinical research network, connecting pharmaceutical sponsors and contract research organizations (CROs) with community-based medical sites across gastroenterology (GI), hepatology, obesity, and cardiology. Its SKOUT product applies artificial intelligence to streamline site operations and patient enrollment, and the company runs a global site network embedded in community care practices through partnerships with GI Alliance, One GI, and US Heart & Vascular. Backed by Insight Partners, the company closed a $77M Series C in April 2026. Iterative Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kailera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kailera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the next generation of obesity and cardiometabolic care through a diversified pipeline of GLP-1 based therapies. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, its lead candidate ribupatide (KAI-9531) is a once-weekly injectable GLP-1/GIP receptor dual agonist in a global Phase 3 program, alongside oral small-molecule GLP-1 candidates and tri-agonist programs licensed in part from Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals. Kailera has raised a $400M Series A and a $600M Series B led by Bain Capital, and priced its IPO in April 2026 (NASDAQ: KLRA). This is a corporate/portfolio company profile in the API Evangelist network; Kailera publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Kirilys Therapeutics
providers.description: Kirilys Therapeutics is a multi-asset precision oncology company developing targeted therapeutic treatments for cancer patients. Led by co-founder and CEO BT Slingsby, MD, PhD, MPH, the company is building a pipeline of precision medicines and is backed by Catalys Pacific, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and UBE. Kirilys was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage biotech, Kirilys publishes a corporate marketing website (company, news, and contact pages) but exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or machine discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Mirvie
providers.description: Mirvie is a clinical-stage women's health company founded in 2018 and based in South San Francisco, California, pioneering the early prediction of pregnancy complications. Its proprietary RNA platform uses a simple maternal blood test and machine learning to read tens of thousands of molecular messages from mother, baby, and placenta, revealing the underlying biology of each pregnancy months before symptoms appear. Mirvie's first product, the Encompass preeclampsia test, pairs a novel blood test that predicts personalized preeclampsia risk with a preventive care plan and received FDA Breakthrough Device designation. The company is backed by General Catalyst, GV, Mayfield, Khosla Ventures, Foresite Capital, and Decheng Capital. Mirvie operates consumer and clinical web properties (mirvie.com and encompasstest.com) but publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mural Health
providers.description: Mural Health is a clinical research technology company whose Mural Link platform manages the clinical trial participant experience end to end. Founded by the team that created ClinCard, Mural Health provides integrated participant payments across 10+ global methods (Venmo, PayPal, Zelle, Revolut, bank transfer, virtual and physical prepaid debit cards, and check via mail), in-app travel and rideshare coordination (Uber, Lyft), participant messaging and calendar syncing, and real-time satisfaction analytics for research sites and sponsors. The company works with leading pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and site networks to reduce trial dropout and administrative burden across studies in 75+ countries, and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Mural Health does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integrations are delivered through partnerships (e.g., ClinOne, Clinical Ink).

providers.name: OriGene Technologies
providers.description: OriGene Technologies, Inc. is a life sciences company that develops and supplies validated research reagents and laboratory services for genomics and proteomics research. Its catalog spans cDNA clones, expression vectors, lentivirus and viral gene-delivery systems, RNAi and CRISPR tools, primary antibodies, recombinant proteins, ELISA and assay kits, and human tissue samples, alongside custom cloning, antibody and protein development, and lentivirus production services. The company operates in the United States and, through OriGene Technologies GmbH, in Europe. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass OriGene publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Ossium Health
providers.description: Ossium Health is a bioengineering company developing off-the-shelf cell therapies manufactured from stem cells recovered from deceased organ and tissue donors. The company operates a proprietary bone marrow and tissue recovery, banking, and manufacturing platform, and is advancing a clinical pipeline of allogeneic cellular therapies targeting hematologic diseases, organ transplant tolerance, and orthopedic conditions. Ossium Health is a private, venture-backed life sciences company; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record and was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst.

providers.name: Outcomes4Me
providers.description: Outcomes4Me is a digital health company providing a personalized cancer care navigation platform for patients. The consumer app delivers personalized treatment plans, symptom and medication management, and community support grounded in NCCN Guidelines, serving over 300,000 patients across 100+ cancer communities. Alongside the patient app, Outcomes4Me runs a For Life Sciences business that offers real-world outcomes data, precision content and marketing, and clinical-trial recruitment and patient-reported-outcomes support to pharmaceutical and diagnostics partners. Backed by Sierra Ventures. No public developer/API surface is published at this time; this profile has been enriched with the company identity and domain-security posture that are publicly available.

providers.name: POMS
providers.description: POMS Corporation develops POMSnet Aquila, a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) purpose-built for pharmaceutical, biotech, cell and gene therapy, and medical device manufacturers. The platform delivers FDA-compliant electronic batch records (EBR), production execution, review-by-exception, and plant-floor integration with ERP and equipment systems, deployed on-premise or in the cloud. POMS also offers the POMSnet Falcon EBR analytics dashboards. Founded around its first MES implementation in 1988 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, POMS sells enterprise software to regulated life-sciences manufacturers rather than publishing a public developer API. Surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, this profile is enriched from the company's public web presence; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found.

providers.name: Pretzel Therapeutics
providers.description: Pretzel Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class medicines that target mitochondrial biology and cellular energy regulation. Its pipeline spans neurological, muscular atrophy, metabolic, and rare disease indications, applying novel mitochondrial modulation approaches to conditions driven by dysfunctional cellular energy production. Backed by GV, the company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company record and life-sciences lead.

providers.name: Profluent
providers.description: Profluent is a Berkeley, California AI biology company building frontier protein language models and using them to design functional proteins for therapeutics, gene editing, agriculture, and industrial enzymes. Founded by Ali Madani — previously architect of the ProGen large language model for proteins at Salesforce AI Research — Profluent pairs in-house foundation models with a wet lab to author novel proteins from scratch and validate them experimentally. The company's research has been published in Nature Biotechnology and Nature, and it is best known for OpenCRISPR-1, which it describes as the world's first AI-designed gene editor, released freely for research and commercial use. Profluent also publishes the ProGen3 family of protein generation models, ProseLM for structure-conditioned protein design, the E1 family of protein encoder models, Protein2PAM for CRISPR-Cas PAM specificity prediction, and the CRISPR-Cas Atlas dataset. Commercial partnerships include a multi-target collaboration with Eli Lilly worth up to $2.25 billion, and deals with Ensoma, Corteva, Integrated DNA Technologies, and the Rett Syndrome Research Trust. Profluent is backed by Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, Altimeter, and Bezos Expeditions. The company does not publish a hosted developer REST API or commercial SDK; its surface area for external builders is the Profluent-AI GitHub organization (model weights and inference code), the Protein2PAM web tool, and partnership engagements.

providers.name: Rénibus Therapeutics
providers.description: Rénibus Therapeutics is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Southlake, Texas, developing treatments for cardio, renal and metabolic disease. Its pipeline is led by veverimer, a non-absorbed polymer in Phase 3 for metabolic acidosis in chronic kidney disease, and RBT-1 (stannic protoporfin / iron sucrose), a first-in-class intravenous pharmacologic preconditioning agent given 24-48 hours before non-emergent cardiac surgery to reduce post-operative complications, which holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations and completed the pivotal Phase 3 PROTECT trial.
