The company publishes a corporate marketing site, a news and events feed, an expanded access policy and patient information, but operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Sano
providers.description: Sano Genetics is a UK-based precision-medicine company operating a 360-degree platform that connects the workflows behind decentralized clinical trials and research studies. Its services span patient recruitment and outreach, protocol and study design, digital prescreening and consent, electronic medical record retrieval, at-home DNA testing with genetic counseling, participant engagement portals, and biomarker testing programs. The platform helps pharmaceutical sponsors and research teams find, engage, and retain the right participants for genetically-informed studies. Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: Science 37 *
providers.description: Science 37 operates a decentralized, direct-to-patient clinical research platform — the first and only FDA-inspected direct-to-patient site — that delivers clinical trials to participants wherever they are. Its Metasite and Agile Clinical Trial operating model combine patient recruitment, research-grade nursing, telemedicine, eConsent, ePRO, wearable/device integration, and EHR data capture into a single end-to-end SaaS platform used by sponsors and CROs. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company has supported 200+ trials across many therapeutic areas. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment (developer./api.science37.com do not resolve); this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Sidewinder Therapeutics
providers.description: Sidewinder Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Diego, developing a new generation of precision bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of solid tumors. Its engineered biologics bind two complexed targets simultaneously to increase tumor specificity, driving internalization of the antibody-receptor complex and its cytotoxic payload, with the goal of expanding the therapeutic window for hard-to-treat cancers such as colorectal, lung, and head-and-neck squamous cell carcinomas. The company raised an oversubscribed $137M Series B in 2026 (co-led by Frazier Life Sciences and Novartis Venture Fund, with DCVC Bio, OrbiMed, and others) and is advancing its bispecific ADC programs toward clinical development. Sidewinder is a biopharma research company and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: SPT Labtech
providers.description: SPT Labtech is a life-sciences laboratory-automation company headquartered near Cambridge, UK, that designs and manufactures instruments and consumables to accelerate drug discovery and life-science research. Its portfolio spans liquid handling (firefly, mosquito, dragonfly, apricot), sample preparation (chameleon for cryo-EM and Quantifoil supports), and sample management and storage (comPOUND, comPACT, arktic, lab2lab, and BioMicroLab). With 400+ employees across seven global locations and 30+ products, SPT Labtech serves pharmaceutical, biotech, and academic laboratories. It is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; SPT Labtech is a hardware and instrumentation vendor and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tenaya Therapeutics *
providers.description: Tenaya Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, focused on discovering, designing, developing, and delivering potentially curative gene therapies and precision medicines that address the underlying drivers of heart disease. Its clinical pipeline includes TN-201, an AAV-based gene therapy for MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), and TN-401 for PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), both in early clinical development. Publicly traded on Nasdaq as TNYA and backed by investors including GV, the company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer platform or API surface.

providers.name: Tigermed
providers.description: Tigermed (Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting Co., Ltd.) is a leading global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated drug and medical device development services across the full clinical lifecycle. Its capabilities span preclinical development (medicinal chemistry, compound screening, toxicology, and bioanalytical services), clinical development (medical writing, clinical monitoring, regulatory affairs, and data management), and integrated services including central laboratories, pharmacovigilance, medical imaging, quality assurance, and real-world and post-marketing studies. The company reports 11,000+ global employees, 180+ offices and locations, and 4,000+ customers, supporting the development of 170+ innovative drugs. Tigermed was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer, API, or technical platform surface.

providers.name: Vibe Bio
providers.description: Vibe Bio is a biopharma AI company whose VibeOne platform provides AI decision infrastructure for business development and licensing teams, accelerating therapeutic asset diligence by turning unstructured scientific and clinical data into decision-ready outputs across a source, prioritize, evaluate, and decide workflow. The company also operates a venture fund backing founders developing cures for rare and overlooked diseases. VibeOne is offered as a demo-request enterprise SaaS product; no public API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: Vilya
providers.description: Vilya is a computational drug-design biotechnology company pioneering the de novo design of macrocycles — entirely new therapeutic molecules that do not exist in nature. Spun out of the Institute for Protein Design and built on Nobel Prize-winning computational protein-design research from scientific founder Dr. David Baker, Vilya uses AI-driven generative models to generate, predict, and validate novel, chemically diverse macrocycles in silico. Its pipeline advances orally bioavailable macrocycles that aim to combine the target selectivity of biologics with the convenience of small- molecule pills, opening previously untreatable disease areas across oncology and immunology (including an integrin alpha4beta7 program for IBD). Vilya is a private therapeutics company; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Vividion Therapeutics
providers.description: Vividion Therapeutics is a San Diego-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that discovers and develops precision small-molecule medicines for previously undruggable disease targets. Its proprietary chemoproteomics platform pairs covalent chemistry with proteome-wide screening to map druggable pockets across the human proteome, driving a pipeline in oncology and immunology (including VVD-214, a WRN helicase inhibitor for MSI-high cancers). Vividion was acquired by Bayer in 2021 and operates as an independent subsidiary. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund; this profile has been enriched and carries no public developer or API surface (a corporate/scientific website only).

providers.name: VivorCare
providers.description: OncoveryCare (VivorCare) is the first virtual survivorship clinic for people living with and beyond cancer. Backed by Techstars, the company pairs survivorship-trained care teams with a virtual-first platform delivering physical and mental health support, personalized survivorship care planning, patient navigation to community resources and referrals, and survivor education. It partners with oncology providers such as New York Cancer & Blood Specialists (NYCBS) to extend post-treatment care. OncoveryCare operates a public website and blog but currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Zai Lab
providers.description: Zai Lab is an innovative, research-based, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in China and the United States, founded in 2014 with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Shanghai. The company discovers, develops, and commercializes transformative medicines for conditions with significant unmet patient needs across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, and infectious disease. As a fully integrated biopharma, Zai Lab spans early-stage discovery through development, regulatory approval, manufacturing, and commercialization. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HongShan and Qiming Venture Partners. Zai Lab publishes a corporate and investor web presence but exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Alleviant Medical
providers.description: Alleviant Medical, Inc. is a clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in Austin, Texas, founded in 2017 to develop minimally invasive, transcatheter therapies for heart failure. The Alleviant System is an investigational, no-implant approach that creates a small interatrial passageway to relieve elevated left atrial pressure without leaving a permanent device behind; it holds U.S. FDA Breakthrough Device designation for both preserved and reduced ejection fraction heart failure and is under study in the FDA-approved ALLAY-HF and ALLAY-HFrEF pivotal trials. The company has raised roughly $164M across a $75M round led by S3 Ventures and RiverVest Venture Partners and a $90M round led by Gilde Healthcare with Omega Funds, Vensana Capital, Longview Ventures, Gilmartin Capital and the TMC Venture Fund. Alleviant is a device and clinical-trial business, not a software business: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification, and its public web surface is limited to clinician, patient-education, investor and press material.

providers.name: Basking Biosciences
providers.description: Basking Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Research Triangle, North Carolina (with operations in Mitchelton, Queensland, Australia) developing novel therapies for life-threatening blood clots. Its lead program BB-031 is an investigational RNA aptamer that targets von Willebrand Factor (vWF) to deliver a rapid-onset, targeted, and reversible thrombolytic for acute ischemic stroke, paired with BB-025, a direct-acting reversal agent designed to rapidly neutralize BB-031. The company is running the RAISE Phase 2 clinical trial and is backed by Insight Partners. Surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: BlossomHill Therapeutics
providers.description: BlossomHill Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2020 by drug designer J. Jean Cui, Ph.D. and biotech operator Y. Peter Li, Ph.D., M.B.A. It develops intelligently designed small-molecule medicines for oncology and autoimmune disease, led by BH-30643, a first-in-class macrocyclic non-covalent mutant-selective OMNI-EGFR inhibitor for EGFR- and HER2-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, and BH-30236, a macrocyclic CLK inhibitor for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia and higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. The company is a drug discovery business, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Casma Therapeutics
providers.description: Casma Therapeutics is a privately held clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered at 201 Brookline Ave, Suite 1401, Boston, MA. Casma develops novel cellular degradation medicines built on the autophagy pathway — the conserved process cells use to clear damaged components. Its PHLYT (Phagosome-Lysosome Targeting) platform initiates target-specific autophagic degradation of disease targets independent of size or complexity, reaching beyond single proteins to organelles, protein aggregates and large signaling complexes, with programs spanning oncology, inflammation, neurodegeneration and metabolic disease. Casma was named to the Fierce 15 list in 2019. The company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API contract; it is catalogued here as a company profile only.

providers.name: Circular Genomics
providers.description: Circular Genomics is a San Diego, California precision-neurology diagnostics company that uses brain-derived circular RNA (circRNA) as a class of stable, blood-based biomarkers for psychiatric and neurological disease. Spun out of the University of New Mexico in 2021 and now resident at Lilly Gateway Labs in San Diego, the company builds CircPath, a proprietary molecular-intelligence platform that discovers, validates and translates circRNA signals into biological insight, and productizes it as research and clinical assays: Discover 1600+ (whole-transcriptome circRNA sequencing across 1,600+ brain-derived circRNAs with pathway-level analysis), AD Predict and AD Detect for Alzheimer's disease, and MindLight, an SSRI antidepressant response test for major depressive disorder. Test ordering and results delivery for licensed healthcare providers run through a login-gated provider portal at mindlight.circulargenomics.com, which is a white-labeled CrelioHealth laboratory information system rather than a first-party developer surface. Circular Genomics publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer documentation of any kind.

providers.name: City Therapeutics
providers.description: City Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 399 Binney Street in Kendall Square, Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2024 by pioneers of RNA interference including John Maraganore, Phillip Zamore, Kotaro Nakanishi, Yukihide Tomari and Mark Keating. The company engineers next-generation RNAi trigger molecules — including its proprietary cleavage-inducing tiny (city) RNAs — and pairs them with precision targeting ligands designed to deliver siRNAs beyond the liver into ocular, CNS and other extrahepatic tissues. Its pipeline includes CITY-FXI, a Factor XI-targeting candidate for thromboembolic disease, and CITY-RBP4 for Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, alongside undisclosed hepatic, ocular and CNS programs. City Therapeutics raised a $135M Series A in October 2024 and a $99.5M Series B in June 2026, and holds research collaborations with Biogen and Bausch + Lomb. City Therapeutics publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface; it is catalogued here as a company profile only.

providers.name: Electra Therapeutics
providers.description: Electra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2018 and pioneering first-in-class antibody therapies directed at signal regulatory proteins (SIRP) for immunological diseases and cancer. Its lead candidate, ELA026 (ipsoprubart), is a monoclonal antibody targeting SIRP-alpha/beta1/gamma on myeloid cells and T lymphocytes to selectively deplete the pathological immune cells that drive the cytokine storm in secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH); it is in the pivotal SURPASS Phase 2/3 study. A second SIRP-targeted program, ELA822, is directed at activated T lymphocytes for immunology and inflammation indications. The company has raised roughly $267M from investors including OrbiMed, Nextech Invest, EQT Life Sciences and Westlake Village BioPartners. Electra publishes a corporate website, pipeline, publications, clinical-trial and news pages, but no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Florence Healthcare
providers.description: Florence Healthcare provides eRegulatory and clinical-trial site enablement software for research sites, sponsors, and CROs. Its eBinders product is an electronic investigator site file (eISF) and participant binder platform that replaces paper regulatory binders with structured, compliant, 21 CFR Part 11 workflows; eTMF manages the sponsor-side trial master file; and SiteLink connects a network of 10,000+ investigator sites across 44+ countries to sponsors and CROs for remote site access, monitoring, document exchange, and source data verification. Florence describes an "open API" for eBinders, eTMF, and SiteLink that supports connected management of roles and permissions, inbound and outbound document exchange, and document status reporting across regulatory and source documents. Access to the API is partner- and customer-gated - it is granted through Florence's integration and partnership programs rather than a self-service public developer portal, and no public API reference, OpenAPI description, or base URL is published as of this writing.

providers.name: Lycia Therapeutics
providers.description: Lycia Therapeutics is a South San Francisco, California biotechnology company developing a new class of targeted protein degradation medicines built on its proprietary lysosomal targeting chimera (LYTAC) platform, which originated in the Stanford University laboratory of Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi, Ph.D. LYTAC molecules bind a disease-driving extracellular protein and shuttle it into the cell for destruction by the lysosome, allowing Lycia to pursue circulating and membrane-bound proteins that conventional small molecules and antibodies have been unable to drug. The company is led by President and Chief Executive Officer Aetna Wun Trombley, Ph.D., is backed by Versant Ventures, Redmile Group, Venrock, RTW and Blue Owl among others, and has partnered with Eli Lilly and Company to discover and develop LYTAC degraders. Lycia is a privately held, research-stage therapeutics company; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Nuvig Therapeutics
providers.description: Nuvig Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 3450 Hillview Avenue, Palo Alto, California, developing next-generation immunomodulators for chronic autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its lead investigational candidate, NVG-2089, is an engineered Fc fragment designed to selectively engage type II Fc receptors and harness an endogenous regulatory mechanism that resolves autoimmune dysregulation while preserving normal immune function; the first patient was dosed in a Phase 2 trial in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) in May 2025. The company announced a $161 million Series B financing in December 2024. Nuvig is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, GitHub organization, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its public web surface is a corporate WordPress site covering science, pipeline, team, news and careers, from which the only machine-readable artifact published is a Yoast-generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Triomics
providers.description: Triomics is an AI healthcare company focused on oncology workflows, using AI agents to transform unstructured electronic health records into structured, actionable datasets for cancer centers and life sciences organizations. Its products include PRISM (AI-powered clinical trial matching), Symphony (visit preparation), Harmony (registry data curation and abstraction), and OncoLLM, a language model that reads entire patient charts to answer oncology-specific questions. The platform ingests HL7, FHIR, CCDA, PDF, and image formats, integrates with Epic, OncoEMR, iKnowMed, and Cerner, and is approved on the Epic App Marketplace. Triomics is deployed at cancer centers including Memorial Sloan Kettering and Mount Sinai, and raised $22 million backed by Battery Ventures, Lightspeed, Nexus, Y Combinator, and Oncology Ventures. Triomics does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Triveni Bio
providers.description: Triveni Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing first-in-class antibody therapeutics for immunological and inflammatory (I&I) disorders, built on a genetics-informed approach to target discovery combined with advanced antibody engineering. Its lead program TRIV-509 is a dual-specific monoclonal antibody against kallikreins 5 and 7 (KLK5/7) for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, addressing barrier dysfunction, inflammation and itch; TRIV-573 is a half-life-extended, second-generation bispecific that pairs the KLK5/7 mechanism with anti-interleukin-13 (IL-13) and entered Phase 1 in 2026. The pipeline also includes an antibody inhibitor of trypsin 1 and 2 for hereditary pancreatitis driven by PRSS1 mutations. The company launched with a $92M Series A, raised a $115M Series B, and closed a $65M Series C in June 2026, and was named a Fierce 15 biotech of 2025. Triveni Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Valence Discovery
providers.description: Valence Discovery is an AI-first drug discovery company, now operating as Valence Labs, the AI research engine of Recursion. Formed from the merger of Datamol and InVivo AI, the team builds machine-learning methods and foundation models for molecular design, cellular perturbation prediction, and biological discovery, trained on petabyte-scale phenomics and transcriptomics data. Rather than a public REST API, Valence's developer surface is a suite of first-party open-source Python libraries - datamol, molfeat, graphium, SAFE and OpenQDC - published under the datamol-io and valence-labs GitHub organizations for cheminformatics, molecular featurization, graph neural networks and ML-ready quantum datasets.

providers.name: Valo Health
providers.description: Valo Health is a Boston-based drug discovery and development company that combines real-world human data, artificial intelligence, advanced causal inference and predictive chemistry to identify and validate therapeutic targets. Its work is organized around two stated capabilities: Human Causal Biology, which applies AI/ML and statistical genetics to large-scale human datasets and validates findings in human tissue, and Closed-Loop Chemistry, which pairs integrated computational modeling with laboratory work to engineer novel small molecules. The company, launched out of Flagship Pioneering and historically associated with its Opal Computational Platform, operates a shared risk-and-reward partnership model with pharmaceutical companies including Novo Nordisk, Merck KGaA, Pfizer and Lundbeck, advancing early-stage R&D while partners lead clinical development. Valo Health is a private biotechnology company that publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AbbVie
providers.description: AbbVie is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets advanced therapies in immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and other specialty areas. AbbVie's portfolio includes treatments for autoimmune diseases, various cancers, neurological disorders, and aesthetics through the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio.

providers.name: Ginkgo Bioworks
providers.description: Ginkgo Bioworks is a synthetic biology company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that builds a horizontal platform for programming biology. Through autonomous laboratories, foundry services, and AI-powered tools, Ginkgo automates the design-build-test cycle of biological engineering for customers across biopharma, agriculture, industrial biotech, and biosecurity. Its offerings include Build-Your-Own-Lab automation hardware and software, a remotely accessible Cloud Lab, Ginkgo Datapoints screening and data services, Foundry cell-engineering services, and the Catalyst autonomous lab agent. Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA) does not currently publish a public self-service developer API; this profile tracks the company's identity and web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Manus Bio
providers.description: Manus Bio Inc. (trading as "Manus", the BioAlternatives Company) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts industrial biotechnology company founded in 2011 out of MIT by Dr. Aji Parayil and Dr. Greg Stephanopoulos. Manus engineers microbial cell factories and precision-fermentation processes so that complex molecules normally obtained through petrochemical synthesis, agricultural extraction, or animal husbandry can be produced by fermentation instead - what the company calls bioalternatives. Its commercialized products include the first U.S. commercial-scale monk fruit sweetener (produced at its Augusta, Georgia BioFacility), the Yume M stevia Reb M sweetener co-developed with Tate & Lyle, citrus-derived aroma ingredients (Nootkatone 70, Valencene 80, BioNootkatone) for Givaudan, and an artemisinin antimalarial program funded by HHS/ASPR. It sells scale-up services through its BioAccelerator and BioManufacturing programs (protein engineering, strain development, bioprocess development from 250 ml to 3,000 L, pilot-scale and biomanufacturing). In April 2025 Manus merged with genome-engineering company Inscripta, adding whole-genome editing technology and the MAD7 CRISPR nuclease licensing program; inscripta.com is now a redirect notice. Manus is a manufacturer of physical ingredients and a contract development and manufacturing organization - it sells molecules and services, not software. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its computational and AI-driven enzyme-engineering tools are internal capabilities that support its services rather than a customer-facing platform.

providers.name: 3T Biosciences
providers.description: 3T Biosciences is a clinical-stage immunotherapy company based in South San Francisco, developing next-generation T-cell receptor (TCR) therapeutics for solid tumors and other immune-mediated diseases. Founded in 2017 on research from K. Christopher Garcia's lab at Stanford University, the company operates its proprietary 3T-TRACE (T-Cell Receptor Antigen and Cross-reactivity Evaluation) platform, which combines high-diversity yeast-display target libraries with active machine-learning to screen billions of protein fragments and identify novel shared TCR targets and specificities. 3T has raised a $40M Series A from Westlake Village BioPartners and Lightspeed Venture Partners and has struck cancer-immunotherapy collaborations with Boehringer Ingelheim worth up to $268M in milestones. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched into the API Evangelist network; 3T publishes no public developer API, SDK, or specification surface.

providers.name: Calysta
providers.description: Calysta, Inc. is a cellular agriculture company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with operations in Memphis, Tennessee (NouriTech), Wilton/Teesside in the United Kingdom (Calysta UK Ltd.) and Singapore (Calysta Asia Pte Ltd.). It produces protein ingredients through a patented gas-fermentation platform in which a naturally-occurring microorganism converts carbon and energy into a non-GMO single-cell protein, using no arable land and no plant or animal inputs. Its product family includes FeedKind for aquaculture and livestock, FeedKind Pet, FeedKind Net Zero and Positive Protein for human food ingredients; FeedKind Aqua is sold globally through Calysseo, a 50/50 joint venture with Adisseo whose first production plant in China manufactures thousands of tonnes per year. Calysta sells physical protein ingredients to feed and food manufacturers — its fermentation platform is industrial process technology, not commercial software — and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Checkerspot
providers.description: Checkerspot is an Alameda, California biotechnology company, founded in 2016 and incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation, that designs and produces functional fats and oils through precision fermentation of microalgae. Its biology-driven molecule licensing platform pairs algal strain development, an advanced analytical platform, bioinformatics, high-throughput screening, fermentation scale-up and downstream oil refining, built around the proprietary microbe Prototheca moriformis, which the company reports reaches over 80% oil content by dry cell weight. The commercial molecule portfolio includes a high sn-2 palmitate algal oil that mimics the triglyceride structure of human milk fat for infant nutrition, an Omega-7 (palmitoleic acid) algal oil, a designer high-oleic tropical-fat alternative to palm oil, and Algolein tG C18/80 for cosmetic formulation; earlier work commercialized algae-derived urethane composites through the WNDR Alpine outdoor brand. Checkerspot works through ingredient and manufacturing partners including AAK, Huvepharma and La Fabrique Vegetale, and closed a USD 55 million Series C led by ArrowMark Partners with participation from Cox Enterprises. It is a business-to-business ingredient and molecule licensing company rather than a software vendor: it operates a WordPress marketing site, publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and has no GitHub organization.

providers.name: Modern Meadow
providers.description: Modern Meadow is a bio-design and materials-science company founded in 2011 in Brooklyn by Andras Forgacs, Francoise Marga, Gabor Forgacs and Karoly Jakab, now headquartered in Nutley / Pine Brook, New Jersey, where it operates an innovation lab opened in 2017. The company applies synthetic biology and protein engineering to build animal-free, bio-fabricated alternatives to leather and other petrochemical-derived materials, through the Bio-Alloy technology platform (an alloy of engineered proteins and bio-based polymers), the BIO-VERA material launched in 2023, and its current flagship INNOVERA, a next-generation leather alternative made from plant proteins, biopolymers and recycled rubber with more than 80% renewable carbon content. It sells into interiors, fashion and accessories, footwear, and automotive, and has partnered with BASF, tannery HELLER-LEDER (a 2026 European joint venture) and Allbirds (the Terralux footwear line). Modern Meadow has raised roughly $236M. It is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: profiling on 2026-08-01 found no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no /.well-known/ documents, and no GitHub organization. Its corporate site (modernmeadow.com, Craft CMS) largely redirects to the product site innovera-world.com.

providers.name: Mytos
providers.description: Mytos is a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) for regenerative medicine and cell therapy. Its iDEM automation platform automates every unit operation of cell culture — coating, seeding, feeding, imaging, passaging and harvesting — in standard 2D T-flask formats, letting clinical-stage biotech companies transfer their manual protocols to automated GMP production at up to 50% lower batch cost, with 10x less labor and cleanroom footprint per batch. Mytos operates a CDMO facility within the Cell and Gene Therapy Catapult site and is backed by Wing Venture Capital. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment; the profile captures the company's verified security posture (trust center, SOC 2/SOC 3/21 CFR Part 11, domain security, vulnerability disclosure).

providers.name: UPSIDE Foods
providers.description: UPSIDE Foods is a cultivated meat company that grows real chicken directly from animal cells instead of raising and slaughtering animals. Starting from a master cell bank derived from a single heritage-breed chicken egg, cells are fed vitamins, minerals, and nutrients and grown in cultivator tanks, becoming cultivated chicken in about three weeks. The company supplies cultivated chicken to foodservice partners and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and Threshold Ventures. UPSIDE Foods publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interfaces as of July 2026.

providers.name: Aer Therapeutics
providers.description: Aer Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in the Research Triangle Park / Raleigh area of North Carolina, developing novel treatments for muco-obstructive lung diseases such as COPD, asthma, cystic fibrosis, and non-CF bronchiectasis. A spinout from Dr. John Fahy's laboratory at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), the company's lead candidate, AER-01 (fexlamose), is an inhaled small-molecule mucolytic designed to break down and liquefy the dense mucus plugs that obstruct airflow in the lungs. Aer closed a $36 million Series A backed by life-science investors including Canaan, OrbiMed, Hatteras Venture Partners, and Pappas Capital. Aer Therapeutics is a private, research-focused therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its corporate identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aktis Oncology
providers.description: Aktis Oncology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation precision radiopharmaceuticals for the treatment of cancer. The company has built a proprietary miniprotein radioconjugate platform that pairs tumor-targeting miniproteins with targeted alpha-particle emitters, aiming to reach solid-tumor types that have been difficult to address with existing radiopharmaceutical therapies. Aktis focuses on patient populations with significant unmet medical need, advancing a pipeline of targeted alpha-based therapeutic candidates. The company operates from Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional site in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. Aktis Oncology was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a biotechnology company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals
providers.description: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018, headquartered at 3027 Townsgate Road, Westlake Village, California, with research and development operations in Guangzhou, China. It discovers and develops biologic therapeutics for serious musculoskeletal diseases, including osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, bone metastasis, osteoarthritis and muscle disorders. Its clinical pipeline is led by AGA2118 and AGA2115, bispecific antibodies targeting sclerostin and DKK1, alongside AGA111 in lumbar interbody fusion. The company closed a $120 million Series C financing in December 2024 led by Bain Capital Life Sciences. Angitia is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, machine-readable specification, or technology platform of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is an XML sitemap and a robots.txt carrying Cloudflare-managed Content-Signal directives that reserve AI training rights.

providers.name: ArriVent
providers.description: ArriVent BioPharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the identification, development, and commercialization of differentiated medicines to address the unmet medical needs of patients with difficult-to-treat diseases, beginning with cancers. The company operates through three strategic pillars — Discover (identifying oncology programs with strong scientific rationale), Partner & Collaborate (licensing promising candidates and building partnerships), and Develop (designing development strategies leveraging regulatory expertise). Its lead candidate is firmonertinib, an EGFR inhibitor, alongside ARR-002, a tetravalent antibody-drug conjugate. ArriVent was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a corporate website and an investor relations site but exposes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Avalynpharma
providers.description: Avalyn Pharma is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing inhaled therapies for rare and serious respiratory diseases, with a focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and other interstitial lung diseases. Its inhaled-delivery pipeline includes AP01 (inhaled pirfenidone), AP02 (inhaled nintedanib), and AP03 (a fixed-dose combination), aiming to deliver antifibrotic medication directly to lung tissue to improve efficacy while reducing systemic side effects. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Beam Therapeutics *
providers.description: Beam Therapeutics is a biotechnology company pioneering precision genetic medicines through base editing, a technology that makes precise, predictable, and efficient single-base changes to the genome without cutting the DNA double helix. The company is developing a portfolio of investigational base editing programs across hematology, hepatology, and other therapeutic areas, using multiple delivery modalities including electroporation, nonviral lipid nanoparticles, and viral vectors. Publicly traded on Nasdaq as BEAM, Beam was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company in 2026. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and hongshan; it is a life-sciences company with no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Compass Therapeutics
providers.description: Compass Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics for the treatment of cancer. Its research is grounded in understanding the tumor microenvironment, designing candidates that optimize the components required for an effective anti-tumor immune response and bridge innate and adaptive immunity. Lead clinical programs include tovecimig and CTX-8371. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, this is a life-sciences company profile in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer, API, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
providers.description: CRISPR Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CRSP) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, with US operations in Boston, Massachusetts. Co-founded by CRISPR/Cas9 pioneer Emmanuelle Charpentier, the company develops transformative gene-based medicines for serious human diseases. Its programs span hemoglobinopathies, immuno-oncology, regenerative medicine, and in-vivo editing; its lead therapy CASGEVY (exagamglogene autotemcel), developed with Vertex Pharmaceuticals, is the first approved CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing treatment for sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia. This is a corporate/investor web presence with no public developer program or API surface.

providers.name: Curie.Bio
providers.description: Curie.Bio is a seed-stage biotech venture firm and drug-discovery co-pilot co-founded by Zach Weinberg (founder of Flatiron Health), Alexis Borisy, and Christoph Lengauer. It pairs seed investment — typically $5M-$7M initial checks, backed by a $380M pro-rata Series A follow-on fund — with hands-on scientific and operational support from a team of experienced drug hunters, helping therapeutics founders design their science and move programs into the clinic and toward a strong next round of financing. Curie.Bio has raised close to $1B and is backed by GV, a16z, and ARCH Venture Partners. It operates as a company/investor profile in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or platform, so most technical API artifacts are not applicable to this provider.

providers.name: Esperion Therapeutics
providers.description: Esperion Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ESPR) is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative medicines that lower LDL cholesterol and reduce cardiovascular risk. Its lead products are NEXLETOL (bempedoic acid) and NEXLIZET (bempedoic acid and ezetimibe), oral, once-daily, non-statin therapies indicated to lower elevated LDL-C in adults. As a life-sciences company, Esperion operates a corporate and scientific marketing web presence rather than a developer program; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable company identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Flex Pharma, Inc.
providers.description: Flex Pharma, Inc. entered the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio lead of bessemer-venture-partners. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable surface of any kind. The flex-pharma.com domain now resolves (via Cloudflare) to a consumer online-pharmacy storefront retailing generic and brand erectile-dysfunction medication (tadalafil, sildenafil), whose About page invokes Rockefeller University professor Dr. Rod MacKinnon — a founder associated with the original Flex Pharma biotech — while publishing no corporate entity name, address, or registration details. Treat the present site as unverified and distinct from the original venture-backed company. Only Terms, Privacy, and a Contact page were verified as live; every /.well-known/ path soft-404s to the homepage.

providers.name: Fractyl Health
providers.description: Fractyl Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GUTS) is a clinical-stage metabolic therapeutics company developing treatments that target the root causes of type 2 diabetes and obesity rather than managing symptoms. Its lead product, Revita, is an outpatient endoscopic procedure that resurfaces the duodenal lining to address a driver of metabolic disease, and Rejuva is an early-stage pancreatic islet-cell gene therapy platform designed for durable, one-time metabolic remission. The company is headquartered in Massachusetts and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst. Fractyl publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its corporate, product, and investor web presence.

providers.name: Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals (Shanghai Stock Exchange: 603087) is a Chinese biopharmaceutical company founded in 1998, specializing in the research, development, production, and commercialization of recombinant insulin analogs and injection devices for diabetes care, alongside a growing oncology pipeline and medical devices. Its products, including insulin glargine injections and prefilled pen injectors, are marketed across 23 countries with 19 products launched globally and clinical trials running in 10 countries. Gan & Lee does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web presence and domain security posture.

providers.name: Glyphic Biotechnologies
providers.description: Glyphic Biotechnologies is a Berkeley, California proteomics company founded in 2021 that is developing ProSE (Protein Sequencing by Expansion) — a de novo, high-throughput, single-molecule protein sequencing technology designed to discriminate all 20 amino acids and their post-translational modifications. The company aims to make massively parallel proteome sequencing broadly accessible for drug discovery and biological research, and is backed by Wing Venture Capital. Glyphic currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Insmed
providers.description: Insmed Incorporated is a NASDAQ-listed (INSM) global biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing therapies for people with serious and rare diseases. Its approved medicines include ARIKAYCE (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension) for refractory Mycobacterium avium complex lung disease and BRINSUPRI (brensocatib) for bronchiectasis. The company advances a pipeline across pulmonary, inflammatory, and rare-disease indications and runs early-innovation science platforms in gene therapy with targeted delivery, protein deimmunization, RNA end-joining, and synthetic rescue. Insmed operates patient-facing surfaces such as a clinical-trials portal and an investigator-initiated-research program, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Iterative Health
providers.description: Iterative Health is a Boston-based clinical research and healthcare technology company operating a global network of community-based clinical research sites that connect trial sponsors with providers to accelerate enrollment and expand patient access to investigational therapies. Its therapeutic focus spans gastroenterology, hepatology, obesity, and cardiology, and its SKOUT AI tooling (rooted in the company's computer-vision work in GI endoscopy) helps sites and sponsors run research more efficiently. Backed by GV and Obvious Ventures and funded through a $77M Series C, the company partners with provider networks including GI Alliance, One GI, and US Heart & Vascular. As of this enrichment pass Iterative Health publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Probably Genetic
providers.description: Probably Genetic is a healthcare company focused on rare disease diagnosis through genetic testing. It offers free targeted genetic testing programs for specific rare conditions (including alpha-mannosidosis, cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis, GRN-FTD, and SYNGAP1-related disorder), insurance-billed testing paired with genetic counselors, at-home saliva/cheek-swab collection kits, and physician-ordered genetic counseling. The platform has served more than 200,000 patients and partners with 50+ patient advocacy groups to advance rare disease research. This is a consumer-facing healthcare provider with no public API or developer program surface.

providers.name: Sana Biotechnology *
providers.description: Sana Biotechnology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company (NASDAQ: SANA) focused on engineering cells as medicines. Its platforms repair or control genes inside cells and replace missing or damaged cells to address the underlying causes of disease, with drug candidates spanning type 1 diabetes, B-cell cancers, and B-cell-mediated autoimmune disorders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass Sana publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Taxa
providers.description: Taxa Technologies is a San Francisco and Tokyo synthetic-biology startup engineering the human skin microbiome. Its debut consumer product is a shelf-stable probiotic deodorant cream: a single application of Taxa Probiotics (25.4 billion CFUs in a base of water, mango butter, and sunflower extract) lasts one week by swapping out the skin microbes responsible for body odor, with a line focused on Wakiga (severe underarm odor). The company frames the skin microbiome as a platform whose microbes drive body odor, UV absorption, and mosquito attraction. Backed by Matrix Partners, Taxa currently runs a product waitlist and publishes a consumer marketing site with People, Science, Terms, and Privacy pages, but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Transposon Therapeutics
providers.description: Transposon Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformational therapies for neurodegenerative and aging-related diseases driven by LINE-1 retrotransposon activity. Its lead asset, TPN-101 (censavudine), is a potent oral inhibitor of LINE-1 reverse transcriptase in late-stage development for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) / frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer's disease. The pipeline also includes follow-on novel nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and Protein Kinase R inhibitors (PKRi) targeting pathways activated by LINE-1 and implicated in cognitive impairment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a corporate marketing website only and no public API, developer, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Tyra Biosciences
providers.description: Tyra Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (NASDAQ: TYRA) based in Carlsbad, California, focused on developing next-generation precision medicines that address the emergence of tumor resistance and other challenges in existing treatment options. Tyra's proprietary in-house SNAP discovery platform combines advanced protein crystallography with structure-based drug design, producing full structural "SNAPshots" of the real-world interaction between a drug and its target in as little as seven days rather than weeks to months. This rapid, sequential structural iteration lets the team refine molecular designs to angstrom-level precision and design selective inhibitors intended to deliver deeper, more durable responses for patients, including in cancers where resistance mutations block first-generation drugs. Tyra was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Vir
providers.description: Vir Biotechnology, Inc. (NASDAQ: VIR) is a clinical-stage immunology company headquartered in San Francisco that combines immunologic insights with modern technology platforms to treat and prevent serious infectious diseases and, increasingly, cancer. Its pipeline spans chronic hepatitis B and D, respiratory infections, and dual-masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors, built on antibody, T-cell, innate-immunity, and small interfering RNA (siRNA) platforms. Vir is a research and corporate organization surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal — only its corporate and investor websites.

providers.name: Acepodia
providers.description: Acepodia is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2017 by Dr. Patrick Y. Yang and Dr. Sonny Hsiao, headquartered in Alameda, California with operations in Taipei, Taiwan. It develops off-the-shelf allogeneic cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease built on two proprietary platforms: Antibody-Cell Conjugation (ACC), which uses bioorthogonal click chemistry from Carolyn Bertozzi's Nobel Prize-winning work to attach tumor-targeting antibodies to gamma delta 2 T cells and natural killer cells without genetic engineering, and Antibody-Dual-Drugs Conjugation (AD2C). Its clinical pipeline includes ACE1831, an anti-CD20 gamma delta T cell therapy, and ACE2016, an anti-EGFR gamma delta T cell therapy. Acepodia is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Adimab
providers.description: Adimab is a private biotechnology company founded in 2007, headquartered in Lebanon, New Hampshire, with a west coast office in Mountain View, California. It operates a proprietary yeast-based antibody discovery and engineering platform that combines fully human synthetic and immune libraries to generate specific, stable and developable IgGs, heavy-chain antibodies (HCAbs), multispecifics, T-cell engagers and T-cell receptors. Adimab deliberately runs no internal therapeutic pipeline, instead partnering with biopharma companies through funded discovery programs, platform transfer and non-exclusive program deals. The company reports more than 140 industry partnerships since 2009, 675+ therapeutic programs initiated, 90+ clinical programs and 6 commercial products. Adimab publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its capabilities are delivered as laboratory discovery services and licensed platform transfer under partnership agreements.

providers.name: ARTBIO
providers.description: ARTBIO is a clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing a new class of targeted Alpha Radioligand Therapies (ARTs) built on the lead-212 (212Pb) isotope. Founded in 2021 out of research at the University of Oslo and Norway's Radium Hospital by Roy Larsen and Oyvind Bruland - the scientific co-founders behind Xofigo - the company pairs a differentiated oncology pipeline with its proprietary AlphaDirect isotope-production technology, a first-of-its-kind 212Pb isolation method intended to enable distributed manufacturing and reliable supply of alpha radioligand therapies. Its lead program AB001 (212Pb-NG001) is in first-in-human Phase 1 trials in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with additional preclinical and discovery programs across breast, head and neck, lung, pancreatic and other solid tumors. ARTBIO operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Oslo, is backed by F-Prime Capital, Third Rock Ventures, Omega Funds, Sofinnova Partners, B Capital, ARE and QIA, and is privately held. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification - software is not its product.

providers.name: Bright Peak Therapeutics
providers.description: Bright Peak Therapeutics AG is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and co-located in Allschwil, Switzerland (Switzerland Innovation Park Basel Area) and San Diego / Del Mar, California. The company engineers next-generation multi-functional immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease, using a protein-engineering and site-specific chemical-conjugation platform to build multi-functional PD-1 inhibitors and cytokine immunoconjugates that combine novel and clinically validated mechanisms in a single molecule. Its lead program, BPT567, is a first-in-class PD1-IL18 immunoconjugate that entered a Phase 1/2a clinical trial. The company has raised a USD 90 million Series C led by Johnson & Johnson Innovation (JJDC) alongside Versant Ventures, RA Capital Management, Fidelity, Qatar Investment Authority, Invus, Venrock, KB Investment, Alexandria Venture Investments and Northleaf Capital Partners. Bright Peak is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: CoRegen
providers.description: CoRegen, Inc. (CoRegen Science) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Houston, Texas developing adoptive cell therapies for aggressive solid tumors. Its platform, licensed exclusively from the O'Malley Lab at Baylor College of Medicine, uses CRISPR gene editing to knock out the SRC-3 steroid receptor coactivator gene in regulatory T (Treg) cells, reprogramming them from immunosuppressors into tumor-killing effectors. The lead program, CRG-150, received FDA IND clearance for a first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial in advanced solid tumors, and the underlying science won the 2023 Cozzarelli Prize. CoRegen is a therapeutics organization, not a software company: it publishes a nine-page marketing and science site (about, the science, preclinical studies, pipeline, publications, leadership, news, careers, contact) and no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: HistoSonics
providers.description: HistoSonics is a medical device company commercializing histotripsy, a non-invasive, non-thermal and non-ionizing sonic beam therapy that uses focused ultrasound to form a controlled bubble cloud which mechanically destroys and liquefies targeted tissue at a sub-cellular level. Its robotically assisted Edison Histotripsy System received U.S. FDA marketing authorization through the De Novo Classification Request process in October 2023 for the non-invasive destruction of liver tumors, making it the first histotripsy platform authorized anywhere in the world, and has since added CE Mark authorization in Europe and an FDA submission covering kidney tumors. The underlying science originated with researchers at the University of Michigan, and the company maintains clinical partnerships with the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin. HistoSonics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API specification; its public web surface is a marketing, clinical-evidence, physician-education and eIFU site rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Latus Bio
providers.description: Latus Bio is a clinical-stage gene therapy company engineering novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids to deliver genetic medicines to precise cell types in the central nervous system and peripheral tissues. The company screens tens of millions of novel capsid variants to build a proprietary database of tissue-targeting "delivery zip codes," pairing engineered capsids with optimized routes of administration so therapeutics reach the intended tissue at a fraction of conventional doses and with minimal off-tissue biodistribution. Its lead programs are LTS-201 for Huntington's disease (AAV.DB-3 capsid) and LTS-101 for CLN2 disease, spanning CNS and ocular delivery (AAV.Ep+ capsid). Latus Bio operates offices and laboratories in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and in Boston's Seaport district, and is backed by DCVC Bio, 8VC, BioAdvance, Samsung Venture Investment, and KDB. Latus Bio is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company; it publishes no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Rivus Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Rivus Pharmaceuticals is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019, with corporate offices in South San Francisco, California and research operations in Charlottesville, Virginia. Grounded in mitochondrial biology, it develops oral small-molecule controlled metabolic accelerators for obesity and associated cardio-metabolic disease. Lead candidate HU6 is in Phase 2 development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and has reported Phase 2a data in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF); RV-8451, an oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity, is in IND-enabling studies. Rivus is a therapeutics developer, not a software or technology vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Trace Neuroscience
providers.description: Trace Neuroscience, Inc. is a biotechnology company developing genetic medicines for neurodegenerative diseases. Its lead investigational medicine, TRCN-1023, is designed to restore the function of the UNC13A protein, which is disrupted in most people living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The company sponsors the FUNCtion ALS Phase 1/2 trial (NCT07674667) evaluating TRCN-1023 delivered by intrathecal injection. Trace Neuroscience is backed by GV and does not currently publish a public developer portal or APIs.

providers.name: Valar Labs
providers.description: Valar Labs is an AI oncology company building diagnostics that interpret solid tumors from routine pathology slides to predict cancer treatment response. Its proprietary CHAI (Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence) platform analyzes digitized H&E-stained slides — trained on 500,000+ pathologist annotations of tumors and their microenvironment — to help physicians and patients make evidence-based therapy decisions. Products include Vesta Bladder (predicting BCG response in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer), Vesta Prostate, and Vitara Pancreas ChemoPredict (guiding first-line chemotherapy selection in advanced pancreatic cancer). Founded at the intersection of AI and oncology and backed by a16z and DCVC, Valar Labs delivers results within days without requiring additional tissue. The company operates a physician ordering portal at portal.valarlabs.com and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Atlas5D
providers.description: Atlas5D is a healthcare technology company that develops an Ambient Measurement System (AMS) for assessing health and wellness through motion in any environment. Its passive, privacy-preserving sensor platform recognizes specific individuals, characterizes and quantifies their movement, and interprets daily routines to predict trends and assess risk of adverse events such as falls, without wearables, without transmitting video, and without storing images. Atlas5D serves individuals monitoring aging loved ones, assisted-living and other institutional care settings, and healthcare and clinical-trial teams that need clinical-grade, real-world evidence of patient movement wherever people live. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Iambic Therapeutics
providers.description: Iambic Therapeutics is a clinical-stage AI drug discovery company headquartered in San Diego. Its proprietary AI platform pairs the NeuralPLexer 3D generative model for protein-ligand structure prediction with the Enchant multimodal transformer for clinical and preclinical endpoint prediction, integrated with automated wet-lab capabilities. Iambic's clinical pipeline includes IAM1363 (HER2), IAM-K1 (KIF18A), and IAM-C1 (CDK2/4) in oncology. Iambic is a therapeutics developer rather than an API provider and does not publish a public developer API or open-source platform.

providers.name: Kiko Labs
providers.description: Kiko Labs is a neuroscience-based early-learning company (a 500 Global portfolio company) that builds adaptive brain-training games for children ages 3-7. Its flagship product, Kiko's Thinking Time, is a voice-guided iOS app developed with Harvard and UC Berkeley neuroscientists with support from the US Department of Education and National Science Foundation. The program trains executive functions — working memory, inhibition, focus, and cognitive flexibility — through progressive games, and includes a parent and educator dashboard for tracking skill development. Kiko Labs is a consumer edtech company and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Roche
providers.description: F. Hoffmann-La Roche is a Swiss multinational healthcare company with two divisions: Roche Pharma and Roche Diagnostics. Roche does not publish a general public developer API but exposes interoperability through the navify diagnostics platform, the cobas infinity laboratory software, and an open-source GitHub presence focused on data-science tooling such as pyreadstat, foxops, and OligoGym.

providers.name: Conformal Medical
providers.description: Conformal Medical, Inc. is a Nashua, New Hampshire medical device company developing the CLAAS (Conformal Left Atrial Appendage Seal) and next-generation CLAAS AcuFORM left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) systems, foam-based implants intended to seal the left atrial appendage and reduce stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation without requiring pre-procedure CT sizing. The company runs the CONFORM pivotal IDE trial and the GLACE study, and publishes a public marketing site segmented for patients, physicians and company/investor audiences. W. L. Gore & Associates completed its acquisition of Conformal Medical on 2026-02-19. Conformal Medical is a regulated medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its only software artifacts are clinical-trial companion mobile apps for enrolled sites.

providers.name: Ablative Solutions
providers.description: Ablative Solutions, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Kalamazoo, Michigan, with offices in San Jose, California. It develops the Peregrine System, a percutaneous catheter platform that performs chemical renal denervation by infusing dehydrated alcohol into the perivascular space around the renal arteries to deactivate surrounding sympathetic nerves, as a treatment for systemic and uncontrolled hypertension. The Peregrine System Infusion Catheter holds FDA 510(k) clearance for infusion of diagnostic and therapeutic agents into the perivascular area of the peripheral vasculature; the Peregrine System Kit remains an investigational product under clinical study in the United States and has received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for drug-resistant hypertension. The company is certified to ISO 13485. Ablative Solutions publishes a small corporate and clinical-information website only; it operates no developer program, public API, documentation portal, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Accent Therapeutics
providers.description: Accent Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering a new class of small-molecule precision cancer therapies that target critical intracellular dependencies spanning multiple types of cancer. Its pipeline is led by ATX-295, a novel KIF18A inhibitor in clinical development, with data presented at AACR and ASCO. Backed by GV, Accent focuses on precision oncology drug discovery and development. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its corporate and web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aerska
providers.description: Aerska is a biotechnology company developing RNA interference (RNAi) medicines to treat, delay, and prevent diseases of the brain and central nervous system. The company pairs next-generation RNAi therapeutics with receptor-mediated "brain shuttle" delivery technology engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier and silence disease-causing genes in the CNS. Founded in 2025 by Jack O'Meara, Stuart Milstein, and Dave Hardwicke, Aerska is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland with research operations in London. It emerged from stealth in 2026 having raised a Series A round led by the EQT Dementia Fund and age1, with additional backing from Speedinvest and Backed. Aerska is a pre-clinical drug-discovery company and does not currently publish a public developer API or platform.

providers.name: AIRNA
providers.description: AIRNA Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision RNA editing therapeutics based on ADAR (adenosine deaminase acting on RNA), a naturally occurring human protein the company redirects to convert adenosine to inosine at a targeted RNA site — changing protein function without permanently altering DNA. Its oligonucleotide medicines are designed for durable, reversible and repeatable dosing. The lead program, AIR-001, targets alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), alongside cardiometabolic RNA editing programs spanning rare genetic disorders and common conditions. Founded by scientific pioneers of ADAR editing, AIRNA operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Tübingen, Germany (AIRNA Bio Germany GmbH). AIRNA publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; therapeutics, not software, are the product.

providers.name: Alamar Biosciences
providers.description: Alamar Biosciences is a privately held life sciences company headquartered in Fremont, California, building precision proteomics tools aimed at the earliest detection of disease. Its NULISA (NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) chemistry and Attobody reagents, run on the ARGO and ARGO HT automated immunoassay systems, deliver attomolar-sensitivity, high-multiplex protein measurement for biomarker discovery, translational research, neurodegeneration and immuno-oncology panels. Alamar publishes no public web API. Its developer-facing surface is open source rather than service based: the first-party NULISAseqR R package (GPL-3) for importing, normalizing, quality-controlling and analyzing NULISAseq XML output, documented at nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com, alongside the NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) that ships with the instruments.

providers.name: AminoChain
providers.description: AminoChain operates a transparent, decentralized research ecosystem for patient-centric biomedical research. Its Specimen Center helps researchers discover and access legacy biospecimens through decentralized specimen discovery and collaboration, while its Donor Platform enables prospective participant registries and manages participant involvement in studies. The platform emphasizes privacy-preserving re-engagement, cryptographic tracking of biospecimens, auditable consent, and benefit-sharing models that return value to patients and donors. Backed by a16z. AminoChain currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: antengene
providers.description: Antengene Corporation is a commercial-stage, R&D-driven global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing first-in-class and best-in-class therapies for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Headquartered in Shanghai with a global footprint across the Asia Pacific region and beyond, Antengene's marketed product XPOVIO (selinexor) and a pipeline of oncology assets such as the Claudin 18.2 antibody-drug conjugate ATG-022 and the CD73 inhibitor ATG-037 target unmet needs in cancer care. Antengene operates in the life sciences sector and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and captured in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence and enrichment.

providers.name: Asher Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Asher Biotherapeutics (Asher Bio) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2019 and headquartered at 650 Gateway Blvd. in South San Francisco, California. The company develops cis-targeted immunotherapies — engineered biologics that simultaneously engage an immunomodulatory receptor and a cell-type-specific target on the same immune cell, so a cytokine is only activated on the intended cell population rather than acting indiscriminately across immune subsets. Its lead candidate, etakafusp alfa (AB248), is a cis-targeted IL-2 directed at CD8+ effector T cells and is in Phase 1a/1b clinical development in cancer, alongside earlier-stage programs AB821 and AB359 and a cis-targeted cytokine augmentation program for cell therapies. Asher Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Believer Meats
providers.description: Believer Meats is a cultivated-meat company founded in 2018 in Rehovot, Israel as Future Meat Technologies by Hebrew University bioengineer Yaakov Nahmias, rebranded to Believer Meats in November 2022 and later headquartered in the United States under CEO Gustavo Burger. It grew chicken, lamb and beef from animal cells in a continuous fermentation process rather than raising and slaughtering animals, raised roughly USD 390 million across a 2019 Series A and a 2021 USD 347 million Series B backed by Tyson Foods, ADM, Emerald Technology Ventures, Bits x Bites, Cibus Fund and Menora Mivtachim, and completed a 200,000 square-foot production plant in Wilson, North Carolina billed as the largest cultivated-meat facility in the world. In 2025 it received an FDA "No Questions" letter for its cultivated chicken followed by USDA label and facility clearance, and then ceased operations in December 2025 after its largest investor withdrew. It was a food-biotechnology and manufacturing business rather than a software vendor: it published no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract, and its Webflow marketing site — last republished in October 2025 — now stands as an archive of a company that is no longer operating.

providers.name: BioNTech
providers.description: BioNTech is a Mainz-based biotechnology company that pioneered the use of messenger RNA (mRNA) technology in human therapeutics. Best known for co-developing Comirnaty, the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine with Pfizer, BioNTech is building a broad oncology pipeline across mRNA cancer immunotherapies, next-generation immunomodulators such as the bispecific antibody BNT327, and targeted therapies, as well as continuing infectious disease vaccine development. BioNTech does not currently expose a public developer API; this index captures the company's products, pipeline, clinical trials, and corporate resources as an API Evangelist profile.

providers.name: Bitterroot Bio
providers.description: Bitterroot Bio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Palo Alto, California, pioneering the emerging field of cardio-immunology — the interplay between the immune system and cardiovascular disease. Its lead program, BRB-002, is a novel investigational immunomodulating protein therapy that targets CD47 to treat atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) by acting on atherosclerotic plaque through the immunomodulation of macrophages, an approach distinct from current standards of care. Founded in 2021, the company is advancing BRB-002 through its MATADOR Phase 2a proof-of-concept study. Bitterroot Bio is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its public web identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cartography Biosciences
providers.description: Cartography Biosciences is a South San Francisco biotechnology company developing precision cancer immunotherapies designed around tumor-selective antigens. Using single-cell genomics, proteomics, and novel binder-discovery methods, the company profiles antigen expression across thousands of patient samples and millions of cells to build a comprehensive antigen atlas, classifying cancers by antigen expression rather than histology or genetic mutation. Its goal is to direct immunotherapies toward the safest and most effective targets. Backed by a16z, Cartography was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a corporate and careers website but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Cellares
providers.description: Cellares is an Integrated Development and Manufacturing Organization (IDMO) for cell therapies, operating a global network of automated "Smart Factories." Its FDA-recognized Cell Shuttle platform delivers high-throughput, end-to-end, cGMP industrial-scale cell therapy manufacturing, and its Cell Q platform automates quality-control testing of cell therapy products. Smart Factories operate in South San Francisco (CA), Bridgewater (NJ), Leiden (Netherlands), and Kashiwa (Japan). Cellares was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a cell therapy manufacturing organization it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Corsair Pharma
providers.description: Corsair Pharma, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary prodrugs of treprostinil for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Its lead program, the TRX-248 transdermal system, is an investigational once-daily patch that delivers an inactive treprostinil prodrug across the skin for conversion to active drug in the liver, aiming to combine the efficacy and titration profile of parenteral prostacyclin therapy with non-invasive once-daily dosing. The company completed its preclinical program, announced positive Phase 1 results for TRX-248 in June 2026, closed a $23M Series B led by New Rhein Healthcare Investors, and has entered a strategic collaboration with United Therapeutics to advance novel treprostinil prodrugs. Corsair Pharma is a drug developer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a five-page marketing and investor-news site with no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Cour Pharmaceuticals Development
providers.description: COUR Pharmaceuticals Development Co., Inc. (COUR Pharma) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in the Chicago area (Northbrook/Skokie, Illinois), spun out of research at Northwestern University. COUR develops antigen-specific immune tolerance therapies built on its proprietary COUR Nanoparticle (CNP) platform: biodegradable polymer nanoparticles of roughly 500 nm carrying about 1% disease-specific antigen, which mimic apoptotic bodies so that antigen-presenting cells in the liver and spleen re-recognize the antigen as self, deleting pathogenic T cells and expanding regulatory T cells. Active clinical programs include CNP-103 for Type 1 Diabetes and CNP-106 for Myasthenia Gravis, with earlier work in Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Celiac Disease. COUR is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Covance (Fortrea)
providers.description: Covance was a contract research organization (CRO) acquired by Labcorp in 2015 and rebranded as Labcorp Drug Development in 2021. In 2023, the clinical development business was spun off as Fortrea, an independent CRO headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, operating in 90+ countries and serving the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries with clinical trial management, central laboratory, and bioanalytical services. No public API or developer portal is currently published; integrations are arranged through sponsor and partner agreements.

providers.name: Creyon Bio
providers.description: Creyon Bio (branded Creyon) is a San Diego drug-development company operating an AI-powered nucleic acid engineering platform, NucleIQ, that designs oligonucleotide and RNA therapies with tissue- and cell-specific delivery. Creyon uses aptamer-based delivery, lipid nanoparticles, and transferrin-receptor aptamers to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting immunology, central nervous system (CNS), and neuromuscular indications including late-onset Pompe disease. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of DCVC and currently advances three wholly-owned programs. This profile is a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network; Creyon publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.
