Founded in 2019 by Shelley Force Aldred and Nathan Trinklein, its pipeline includes RNDO-564 (Phase 1 for bladder cancer) plus programs targeting ovarian, endometrial, and renal cancers, backed by a Series A led by Canaan and Red Tree Venture Capital and a collaboration with Eli Lilly. Rondo publishes a corporate and pipeline website but exposes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API surface; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Santa Ana Bio
providers.description: Santa Ana Bio is a precision immunology company developing targeted therapies to stop autoimmune and inflammatory disease at the source. The company pairs a multi-omics discovery platform (integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data) with a pipeline of bispecific and multi-specific antibody and antibody-drug-conjugate programs (SAB01, SAB05, SAB06) advancing toward IND submissions across 2026-2027. Backed by a16z and GV, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. It publishes a corporate and careers website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Visolis
providers.description: Visolis is a biomanufacturing company that combines synthetic biology with chemical catalysis to convert plant biomass into MEV (mevalonic acid), a proprietary platform molecule used to make sustainable, bio-based alternatives to petroleum-derived chemicals and fuels. Its products include bio-isoprene for synthetic rubber (a partnership with Zeon), AroSAF 100% bio-based sustainable aviation fuel, and non-toxic bio-based industrial solvents (piloted with the U.S. Department of Defense). Headquartered in San Leandro, California and led by CEO Deepak Dugar, Visolis is a climate-tech company surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Visolis publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aspect Biosystems
providers.description: Aspect Biosystems is a Vancouver, British Columbia biotechnology company developing Bioprinted Tissue Therapeutics — implantable, allogeneic living tissues designed to replace, repair, or supplement biological function in the body. Spun out of an interdisciplinary medicine-and-engineering collaboration at the University of British Columbia in 2013, the company operates a self-described full-stack tissue therapeutic platform that integrates proprietary AI-powered microfluidic bioprinting, computational tissue design tools, therapeutic and hypoimmune-engineered cells, and advanced biomaterials. Its clinical pipeline targets metabolic and endocrine disease, led by pancreatic tissue programs for type 1 diabetes and programs in rare endocrine disorders and liver disease. Aspect has raised more than US$350M, including a US$115M Series B, and holds partnerships with Novo Nordisk (announced 2023, valued at over US$2.6B in milestones) and the governments of Canada and British Columbia. It is a private, pre-commercial therapeutics developer: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Cajal Neuroscience
providers.description: Cajal Neuroscience, which now operates publicly as Cajal Therapeutics, is a Seattle, Washington biotechnology company founded in 2020 by Alex Vaughan, Andrew Dervan and Ian Peikon, and launched in November 2022 with a $96 million Series A led by The Column Group and Lux Capital with participation from Two Sigma Ventures and Bristol Myers Squibb. The company develops small-molecule and RNA medicines that restore iron homeostasis, built around "iron mobilizers" — small molecules that transport iron across membranes into the compartments where it is required, bypassing disease-driven bottlenecks such as chronic inflammation, altered iron transporter expression and lysosomal dysfunction. Its pipeline spans systemic disease (CTX001, a clinical-stage iron mobilizer for anemia of chronic kidney disease; CTX201 and CTX211, preclinical siRNA programs for inflammatory anemia and myelofibrosis anemia) and CNS disease (a discovery-stage brain-penetrant iron mobilizer for Parkinson's disease). This is a therapeutics company, not a software or data platform company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. Its public GitHub organization contains open-source laboratory hardware and firmware (a drone-motor spin coater, a microfluidic pressure sensor, a flow sensor) plus forks of third-party single-cell and genomics analysis tooling — none of which expose a network API.

providers.name: Cognito Therapeutics
providers.description: Cognito Therapeutics is a clinical-stage neurotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 out of MIT research by Ed Boyden and Li-Huei Tsai into the link between gamma-frequency neural oscillations and Alzheimer's disease progression. Its lead investigational product, Spectris, is a non-invasive at-home neuromodulation device that delivers synchronized 40Hz light and sound stimulation through a headset and glasses for one hour daily, evoking gamma activity to slow cognitive and functional decline in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. Spectris AD received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in 2021, and the company closed an oversubscribed $105M Series C in March 2026 led by Morningside Ventures. Cognito Therapeutics is a medical device and therapeutics company: it publishes a corporate and clinical-information website and no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Agomab Therapeutics
providers.description: Agomab Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: AGMB) developing novel disease-modifying therapies for fibro-inflammatory diseases, with an initial focus on chronic fibrotic indications of high unmet medical need such as Crohn's disease and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Building on deep expertise in growth factor biology, Agomab advances a pipeline of small-molecule and antibody candidates targeting the pathways that drive tissue fibrosis and inflammation. Headquartered in Belgium with operations across Europe and the United States, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biopharmaceutical company it publishes a corporate and investor-relations web presence rather than a public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the network catalog.

providers.name: Alchemab Therapeutics
providers.description: Alchemab Therapeutics is a UK-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation antibody therapeutics for hard-to-treat diseases. Its "Adaptive Immunity" platform identifies naturally resilient individuals, such as long-term cancer survivors, and harnesses their protective antibodies, using artificial intelligence and deep learning to translate these natural immune responses into novel human-derived therapeutics across neurodegeneration, oncology, and other areas of high unmet need. Alchemab was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As a research-stage therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Autobahn Therapeutics
providers.description: Autobahn Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in San Diego, California, developing regenerative medicines for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. The company pairs a proprietary brain-targeting chemistry platform - which creates orally administered small-molecule prodrugs designed to cross the blood-brain barrier - with validated human biology and biomarker-driven development strategies. Its pipeline includes elunetirom (its lead clinical program, being developed for indications such as bipolar depression), ABX-101 (a next-generation CNS-active S1P molecule), and ABX-003. Autobahn is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and Insight Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record captures company identity and published web properties only.

providers.name: BreezeBio (formerly GenEdit)
providers.description: BreezeBio, Inc. (formerly GenEdit) is a clinical-stage genetic medicines company based in South San Francisco, California, solving the central delivery problem of gene editing and genetic medicine. Its proprietary NanoGalaxy platform is a library of thousands of non-viral, non-lipid polymer nanoparticles engineered to deliver genetic payloads (mRNA, DNA, and CRISPR ribonucleoprotein) to specific cell types and tissues without triggering an immune response. The company is advancing an internal pipeline of precision genetic medicines focused on autoimmune disease and oncology, led by BRZ-101, a tolerance-inducing candidate for Type 1 diabetes. GenEdit rebranded to BreezeBio in February 2026 alongside a $60M Series B, and has established platform partnerships with Roche's Genentech and Sarepta Therapeutics. This is a therapeutics company with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Centivax
providers.description: Centivax is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, developing broad-spectrum vaccines to prevent infectious diseases at scale. Its lead program is a universal, broadly protective influenza vaccine in Phase 1 clinical development designed to protect against all strains of the virus. The company's pandemic-prevention work received a Gates Foundation Grand Challenge award and was featured in Netflix's "Pandemic: How to Prevent an Outbreak." Centivax's mission is to accelerate the world's transition to a post-pathogen humanity. This is a life-sciences company profile in the API Evangelist network; Centivax does not currently publish a public developer or API platform.

providers.name: Comanche Biopharma
providers.description: Comanche Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Concord, Massachusetts, developing investigational siRNA (small interfering RNA) medicines for maternal health. Its lead candidate, CBP-4888, is a subcutaneously administered siRNA therapy targeting sFlt1-mediated preterm preeclampsia, a leading and potentially life-threatening complication of pregnancy. The company's mission is to develop and make globally available the first therapy targeting a root cause of preeclampsia. In April 2025, CBP-4888 received Orphan Drug Designation from the European Medicines Agency. Comanche Biopharma is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). As a therapeutics company it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Contraline
providers.description: Contraline is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing non-hormonal, long-acting, reversible contraceptive options for men and couples. Its lead product, ADAM, is an investigational implant designed to provide long-lasting reversible contraception, and NES/T is a daily topical gel intended to pause sperm production. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Contraline runs clinical trials and participant programs from its Charlottesville, Virginia base. Its products are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA. The company operates a marketing and clinical-trial website with no public developer program or API; this API Evangelist profile captures its web presence, privacy posture, and domain security for the network catalog.

providers.name: Eikon
providers.description: Eikon Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company that integrates Nobel Prize-winning super-resolution single-molecule tracking (SMT) microscopy, advanced engineering, automation, and high-performance computing to visualize and measure the real-time movement of individual proteins in living cells. This proprietary live-cell imaging platform screens protein-ligand interactions across millions of cells per day, generating large, high-dimensional datasets that power the discovery and development of novel small-molecule medicines. Eikon advances a clinical- and preclinical-stage oncology and immunology pipeline, including EIK1001 (a TLR7/8 agonist) and IMP1734 (a selective PARP1 inhibitor). Backed by General Catalyst, the company is headquartered in Millbrae, California with offices in New York and Jersey City.

providers.name: Granata Bio
providers.description: Granata Bio is a reproductive-health biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018 and headquartered in the United States, focused on expanding access to fertility and IVF therapeutics across North America. The company identifies, licenses, and develops biopharmaceuticals spanning the in-vitro fertilization medication lifecycle from ovarian stimulation through luteal phase support, and is advancing a clinical pipeline that includes the Phase III GRACE Study. Granata Bio has raised over $30M, including a $14M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and a subsequent $15M Series A+. It operates a corporate and clinical web presence only and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or machine-readable interface; this profile captures its identity and web properties within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Grey Wolf Therapeutics
providers.description: Grey Wolf Therapeutics (Greywolf Therapeutics) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a new therapeutic class of immunotherapies through antigen modulation, aimed at treating people living with cancers and autoimmune disorders. Its approach modulates antigen presentation on cell surfaces so T cells can correctly recognize and target diseased cells, and it is pioneering modulation of Signal 1 in the T cell activation cascade. Lead assets include GRWD5769, a first-in-class oral ERAP1 inhibitor for oncology in Phase 1/2 trials, and GRWD0715, an autoimmunity-focused asset also in Phase 1/2. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company profile. It is a corporate/scientific organization and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: InterVenn
providers.description: InterVenn Biosciences is a digital-biology company applying artificial intelligence and mass spectrometry to glycoproteomics, the large-scale study of glycosylated proteins, to discover novel biomarkers for precision medicine. Its proprietary platform integrates liquid chromatography and tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with AI-driven analysis (including the OpenPIP software) to identify and quantify glycopeptides and glycan structures across complex diseases such as cancer. Surfaced as a portfolio company of amplify-partners and softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network. InterVenn publishes no public developer API, portal, or specifications as of this enrichment pass; this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Kanvas Biosciences
providers.description: Kanvas Biosciences is a spatial biology company building a microbiome drug screening, discovery, and manufacturing platform to accelerate development of next-generation live biotherapeutics. Its proprietary High-Phylogenetic-Resolution Spatial Mapping (HiPR-Map) platform uses oligonucleotide probes targeting ribosomal and messenger RNA to visualize microbial identity and cellular function within tissue across all kingdoms of life, illuminating host-microbiome interactions. The company advances a microbiome-based immuno-oncology pipeline (lead candidate KAN-001) and operates GMP manufacturing. Backed by DCVC. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; the enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Loyal
providers.description: Loyal (Cellular Longevity, Inc.) is a clinical-stage veterinary biotechnology company developing drugs intended to extend the healthy lifespan of dogs. Its lead programs — including LOY-002 for metabolic dysfunction in senior dogs and LOY-001/LOY-003 for large- and giant-breed dogs — are advancing through the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine approval process, with more than 1,300 dogs enrolled across clinical studies. Loyal also runs a veterinary Learning Hub for practitioner education. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and First Round Capital. As of this enrichment pass Loyal publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its public web identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Matwings Technology
providers.description: Matwings Technology (天鹜科技) is a global, AI-driven full-stack protein research and development platform. Centered on its self-developed MatwingsVenus general large model for protein design, the company integrates an in-house AI biological design agent (MatwingsVenus Agent), a ten-billion-scale protein sequence dataset (MatwingsVenus Pod), and an automated experimental platform (MatwingsVenus Auto) to deliver an end-to-end paradigm that spans AI design through AI validation. Capabilities include AI-directed evolution, AI enzyme mining, and de novo protein design, applied across affinity fillers and consumables, holistic health, and innovative drug discovery. Matwings is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company headquartered in Shanghai, with peer-reviewed work at ICLR, NeurIPS, and PNAS. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Mestag Therapeutics
providers.description: Mestag Therapeutics is a clinical-stage immunotherapy company based in Cambridge, UK, developing new treatments for cancer and inflammatory diseases by targeting the understudied role of activated fibroblasts in immune responses. Its lead cancer program, MST-0312, is a targeted LTBR-agonist bispecific antibody designed to drive tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) formation in solid tumors and is now in the Phase I STARLYS trial. Its inflammatory-disease program, M402, uses agonist antibodies against stromal inhibitory receptors for conditions including rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and lupus. Backed by GV, Mestag is a privately held biotech and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Moonwalk Biosciences
providers.description: Moonwalk Biosciences is a biotechnology company pioneering therapeutics in adipose (fat) biology, driven by deep genetic and epigenetic insights. Co-founded by Alex Aravanis (CEO), Arash Jamshidi (President & CTO), Justin Valley (Chief Platform Officer), and CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang, the company develops epigenetic and siRNA-based programs — including obesity therapies — and is backed by Khosla Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Google Ventures, Future Ventures, Alpha Wave Global, and YK Bioventures. Moonwalk does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or API documentation; this profile captures its corporate identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nchroma Bio
providers.description: nChroma Bio is a genetic medicines company developing durable in vivo therapies by pairing best-in-class genetic cargoes, including epigenetic editing approaches, with targeted delivery technologies for diseases of significant unmet need. Headquartered at 201 Brookline Avenue in Boston, Massachusetts, the company is backed by DCVC and GV. This is a corporate research and therapeutics organization; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Octant Bio
providers.description: Octant (Octant Bio) is a precision-medicine and therapeutics company based in Emeryville, California, founded by Sri Kosuri and Ramsey Homsany. Octant engineers small-molecule drugs that modulate cellular mechanisms behind serious disease, with a focus on protein misfolding and mistrafficking disorders. Its Navigator platform merges synthetic biology, massively parallel experimentation in human cells, high-throughput chemistry, and AI/ML to understand and modulate how target proteins actually behave inside cells. Programs span rare genetic diseases (including autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa and Fabry disease), oncology, metabolism, and immunology. Octant is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Catalio Capital Management. As of this profile Octant publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this record captures the company's public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PhaseV
providers.description: PhaseV is a biopharma software company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts that builds AI and machine-learning solutions for clinical-trial optimization. Its platform helps pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs improve trial design, reduce enrollment and cost, shorten timelines, and increase probability of success through simulation and Bayesian adaptive design (Trial Optimizer), biomarker and patient-subgroup identification (Response Optimizer), disease-progression causal analysis (Portfolio Optimizer), site selection and operational analytics (ClinOps Optimizer), and ML-based early-derived endpoint identification. PhaseV publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Accel and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Pheon Therapeutics
providers.description: Pheon Therapeutics is a preclinical-stage oncology biotechnology company developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for a wide range of hard-to-treat solid tumors. Leveraging two decades of ADC experience, Pheon arms monoclonal antibodies against both novel and clinically validated targets with warheads from its proprietary payload platform, which offers a novel mechanism of action, or with off-the-shelf linker-payload combinations, balancing safety and efficacy for each target. The company is privately held and backed by specialist healthcare investors. Pheon publishes a corporate and scientific web presence only; it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known API discovery surface.

providers.name: Preveta
providers.description: Preveta is a healthcare software company that builds an AI-driven care navigation platform and "command center" for specialty clinics. Built on clinical pathways, its software transforms EMR data into actionable insights, giving oncology, urology and gastroenterology practices an entirely new way to view, navigate and manage their patient populations across the cancer care continuum. Preveta is backed by Bullpen Capital and Techstars. As of this profile the company markets a closed clinical SaaS product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Quris
providers.description: Quris-AI is a Bio-AI company building what it describes as pharma's first AI safety-prediction platform, aiming to predict which drug candidates will be safe in humans before they reach clinical trials. Its approach couples machine learning with "Patients-on-a-Chip" technology — miniaturized, organ-representative human tissue models that generate automatically-tagged biological data used to train classification algorithms for drug-safety prediction. The company targets the roughly 89% of drugs that fail in clinical trials, seeking to de-risk and accelerate pharmaceutical development. Based in Boston and Tel Aviv, Quris was co-founded with pioneers including Moderna co-founder Robert Langer and Nobel Laureate Aaron Ciechanover. Quris is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and is profiled in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Reify Health
providers.description: Reify Health is a clinical research technology company whose mission is to remove clinical trial operations as the bottleneck to delivering new therapies to patients. It is the parent organization behind OneStudyTeam, whose StudyTeam platform is a cloud-based patient enrollment and recruitment management system connecting research sites, sponsors, patients, and vendors on a unified workspace, and Care Access, a business unit expanding trial access to underserved communities. StudyTeam is used by roughly 70% of the sponsors running the most clinical trials (including Amgen, AstraZeneca, and Eli Lilly), across 10,000+ research sites in 100+ countries. Reify Health is backed by Altimeter Capital, Battery Ventures, ICONIQ Capital, and Sierra Ventures. No public developer API, developer portal, or API specification was found during enrichment; this profile captures company identity, links, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: sanegenebio
providers.description: SanegeneBio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing RNAi (RNA interference) genetic medicines for metabolic, cardiovascular, and complement-mediated autoimmune diseases, including obesity. Its proprietary LEAD (Ligand and Enhancer Assisted Delivery) platform enables receptor-mediated, targeted delivery of siRNA therapeutics to adipocytes, skeletal myocytes, and other tissues beyond the liver. The company operates as a fully integrated global biotech and has raised over $150 million to advance its pipeline. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a corporate website (about, technology, pipeline, news, contact) but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Scribe Therapeutics
providers.description: Scribe Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California, engineering CRISPR-based genetic medicines through its proprietary "CRISPR by Design" platform. Co-founded by molecular engineers Benjamin Oakes, Brett Staahl, and David Savage alongside CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, the company builds highly engineered CasX-derived enzymes — including its X-Editing (XE) molecules for precise gene editing and ELXR epigenetic long-term X-repressor technology for durable gene silencing without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Scribe focuses initially on cardiometabolic disease, the leading cause of death globally, and expands into areas such as sickle cell disease and neurological conditions through strategic pharmaceutical partnerships. The company is backed by a16z and Menlo Ventures and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a venture portfolio company. Scribe Therapeutics is a therapeutics and drug-discovery company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface.

providers.name: Sequence Bio
providers.description: Sequence Bio is a life sciences and population genomics company based in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, focused on discovering the genetic causes of disease to power the development of new medicines. The company leverages the founder-effect genetics of the Newfoundland and Labrador population, running a large-scale Study of the Genetic Causes of Inherited Disease to identify novel drug targets and predictors of treatment response for pharmaceutical partners. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a corporate and research website but does not currently expose a public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Vivodyne
providers.description: Vivodyne is a bio-AI company working to make human biology computable through large-scale human tissue engineering. Its TissueDisk platform cultivates hundreds of self-assembling, vascularized human tissues on a single microfluidic disk, and its autonomous HIVE robotic labs cultivate, perturb, and analyze thousands of tissues to generate multi-modal phenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data at single-cell resolution for pharmaceutical drug discovery and AI model training. The company operates as a B2B partner to pharma and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ashvattha Therapeutics
providers.description: Ashvattha Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a new class of precision nanomedicines built on hydroxyl dendrimer therapeutics (HDTs), a platform exclusively licensed from Johns Hopkins University. Hydroxyl dendrimers traverse tissue barriers such as the blood-retinal and blood-brain barrier and are selectively taken up by activated cells in regions of inflammation, allowing known small-molecule drugs to be delivered intracellularly to diseased tissue with sustained effect and reduced off-target exposure. The company is advancing programs across ophthalmology, neurology, and inflammatory disease, led by migaldendranib (MGB), a first-in-class subcutaneously administered nanomedicine in Phase 2 development for diabetic macular edema and neovascular age-related macular degeneration, plus hydroxyl dendrimer PET imaging tracers such as [18F]OP-801. Founded by Jeffrey L. Cleland, Kannan Rangaramanujam, and Sujatha Kannan. Ashvattha publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Celerion (H.I.G. Capital)
providers.description: Celerion is a global contract research organization (CRO) specializing in early-stage clinical research, Phase I clinical trials, clinical pharmacology, and bioanalytical services that accelerate drug development from first-in-human studies through proof-of-concept. Headquartered in Lincoln, Nebraska with clinical and bioanalytical sites across North America and Europe, Celerion supports pharmaceutical and biotechnology sponsors with healthy-volunteer and special-population studies, bioanalysis, biomarker assays, ECG/cardiac safety, and its LabNotes bioanalytical data-management software. The company is a portfolio holding of H.I.G. Capital and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network via the bain-capital-ventures portfolio graph. As a corporate/marketing web presence with no public developer or API program, this profile carries only the artifacts that could be observed on the public web (llms.txt, domain-security posture).

providers.name: Clasp Therapeutics
providers.description: Clasp Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage precision immuno-oncology company developing next-generation T cell engagers (TCEs) built on its proprietary pHLAre platform, which redirects T cells to mutant peptides — such as p53 R175H and mutant KRAS — presented by specific HLA molecules on the surface of tumor cells. The approach is intended to yield off-the-shelf, antibody-like medicines that hit common oncogenic driver mutations with tumor-exclusive specificity. Its lead candidate CLSP-1025 (p53 R175H / HLA-A*02:01) is in the Phase 1 GUARDIAN-101 trial (NCT06778863), and CLSP-5282, a first-in-class KRas-directed TCE, was unveiled at AACR 2026. Founded on research from Bert Vogelstein, Drew Pardoll and colleagues at Johns Hopkins, the company launched in March 2024 with $150 million led by Catalio Capital Management, Third Rock Ventures and Novo Holdings, and operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Rockville, Maryland. Clasp Therapeutics is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Convergent Therapeutics
providers.description: Convergent Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing next-generation targeted radiotherapies for cancer. Founded in 2020 by Philip Kantoff, the company builds alpha radioantibodies that pair a humanized monoclonal antibody against prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) with the alpha emitter actinium-225, delivering short-range, high-energy alpha radiation to tumor cells. Its lead candidate, CONV01-alpha (rosopatamab tetraxetan), is in the Phase 2 CONVERGE-01 trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, including patients previously treated with Lu-177 PSMA radioligand therapy, with a pivotal Phase 3 planned. Convergent announced a $90 million Series A financing in 2023. The company publishes a corporate website covering its pipeline, technology, scientific publications and press, but operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Evox Therapeutics
providers.description: Evox Therapeutics is an Oxford, United Kingdom based biotechnology company developing genetic medicines that expand the reach of gene therapy into the brain to transform the treatment landscape for severe neurodegenerative diseases. Its proprietary ExoEdit platform combines the natural transport capabilities of exosomes with CRISPR-based gene editing to improve the delivery, potency, and safety of genetic treatments for central nervous system disorders such as Rett Syndrome. Evox is a venture backed life-sciences company (investors include GV) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a corporate and scientific website but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Formation Bio
providers.description: Formation Bio (formerly TrialSpark, founded 2016 in New York City) is a tech-driven, AI-native pharmaceutical company that aims to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. Rather than discovering drugs, Formation Bio in-licenses and acquires clinical-stage drug assets from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then develops them using proprietary technology platforms, process automation, and large language models applied across the drug development lifecycle — patient recruitment, e-consent, data management, monitoring, and biostatistics. The company rebranded from TrialSpark to Formation Bio in 2023 as it moved from a pure clinical-trial software platform to combined platform-plus-asset ownership. It raised a $372M Series D in 2024 and announced a first-in-class AI collaboration with Sanofi and OpenAI. Formation Bio operates hybrid teams across New York City, Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area, and North Carolina's Research Triangle. It is a private company with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kyverna Therapeutics
providers.description: Kyverna Therapeutics (Nasdaq: KYTX) is a patient-centered, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Emeryville, California, developing engineered T cell therapies for patients suffering from autoimmune diseases. Kyverna adapts CD19 CAR T-cell therapy — originally developed for B cell cancers — to deeply deplete the B cells that drive autoimmunity, with the goal of durable, drug-free remission. Its lead candidate, mivocabtagene autoleucel (miv-cel, KYV-101), is a fully human CD19 CAR T-cell therapy in Phase 2 development for stiff person syndrome, myasthenia gravis and multiple sclerosis, and in Phase 1/2 development for systemic sclerosis and lupus nephritis in the United States and Germany. The pipeline also includes next-generation autologous and allogeneic CAR T constructs, including KYV-201, built on the company's Ingenui-T rapid manufacturing platform. Kyverna is a biopharmaceutical operating company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web, corporate and investor surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Leyden Labs
providers.description: Leyden Labs is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Leiden, The Netherlands, with a regional office in Singapore, developing intranasal antibody products that protect people against known and newly emerging respiratory viruses. Its approach pairs mucosal immunity — delivering antibodies directly into the nasal passages, the gateway respiratory viruses use to enter the body — with broad protection, by targeting conserved regions of viral proteins so a single product can cover circulating strains and future variants. Its lead program, PanFlu, is an intranasal antibody candidate in clinical trials derived from CR9114, among the most broadly neutralizing influenza antibodies identified to date. Founded in 2021 by Koenraad Wiedhaup and Ronald Brus with founding scientist Jaap Goudsmit, the company is backed by GV and the SoftBank Vision Fund alongside the European Innovation Council Fund, the European Investment Bank and Invest-NL. Leyden Labs publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK; this profile captures its public web, security and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: LifeMine Therapeutics
providers.description: LifeMine Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts, with sites in Gloucester, Massachusetts and Basel, Switzerland. It pioneers a Top-Down Drug Discovery approach that leverages evolutionary insights from fungi to find next-generation precision medicines. Its LifeBank collection of deep-sequenced wild-type fungi and its Avatar-Rx platform combine human genetics and genomics, bioinformatics, machine learning and synthetic biology to mine biosynthetic gene clusters for genetically encoded small molecules, using embedded target genes as avatars to predict therapeutic effect independent of chemical structure. Its lead program LIFE-001 is a precision-engineered calcineurin inhibitor in Phase 1 for immune-mediated disorders and organ transplant rejection, alongside a genomic drug discovery alliance with GSK. LifeMine publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Noetik
providers.description: Noetik is an AI-native biotechnology company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, focused on discovering and developing cancer therapies with machine learning. The company has assembled one of the largest multimodal tumor datasets and trained foundation models (including its OCTO world model for cancer biology) to represent tumor microenvironments and simulate spatial biology with virtual cells. Its platform spans human data generation, foundation models, and therapeutic applications aimed at enriching clinical trials, repositioning drugs to the right patient populations, and discovering novel oncology targets. Noetik is backed by DCVC. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this record captures its public web and organizational surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: OrsoBio
providers.description: OrsoBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, developing first-in-class oral therapies that restore energy homeostasis in patients living with severe metabolic disorders — obesity, type 2 diabetes, severe dyslipidemias, lipodystrophies and MASH. The name is drawn from the metabolic adaptability of bears ("orso" in Italian). Its pipeline is led by three mitochondrial protonophores — TLC-6740, TLC-1180 and TLC-1235 — intended to increase energy expenditure and improve metabolic and cardiovascular health, alongside an LXR inverse agonist (TLC-2716) for severe hypertriglyceridemia and MASH, an ACC2 inhibitor (TLC-3595) for insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes, and an ACMSD inhibitor to augment NAD+ biosynthesis in metabolic and inflammatory liver and kidney disorders. The company closed an oversubscribed $67 million Series B in September 2024, co-led by Ascenta Capital and Woodline Partners with participation from Samsara BioCapital, Enavate Sciences and Longitude Capital. OrsoBio publishes a corporate site covering its science, pipeline, team, board, publications, events and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. The only machine-readable surface on orsobio.com is the site's own WordPress CMS route index, which the site's robots.txt explicitly disallows at /wp-json/ and which is therefore not harvested or catalogued here.

providers.name: Treeline Biosciences
providers.description: Treeline Biosciences is a drug discovery and development company that aspires to make great medicines reliably and repeatedly, matching compelling disease targets with clinically proven drug approaches -- small-molecule inhibitors, protein degraders, and antibody drug conjugates -- enabled in-house at its U.S. and EU research facilities and integrated with in silico and machine learning models that help its scientists understand protein targets at an atomic level. The company pursues a target-centric preclinical pipeline serving patients with serious diseases across oncology, immunology, and neurology, and is a portfolio company of GV. Treeline publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Turbine
providers.description: Turbine (Turbine Ltd) is a Budapest-based AI biotechnology company that virtualizes biological experiments to accelerate and de-risk drug discovery. Its Simulated Cell platform trains virtual cells on genomic, transcriptomic, and perturbation-response data, then runs millions of in silico experiments per day to predict therapy response across cell lines, patient-derived organoids and xenografts, and patient samples. Turbine offers partner-facing products for target discovery and de-risking, combination design, and ADC (antibody-drug conjugate) intelligence, and works with pharmaceutical partners including AstraZeneca and MSD. The company publishes research code and benchmarks on GitHub but exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Amyris
providers.description: Amyris, Inc. is a synthetic-biology and precision-fermentation company that engineers microbes to convert plant-derived sugars into high-performance renewable molecules — including farnesene, squalene, squalane, and bisabolol — at industrial scale. The company offers strain development, process development, piloting, scale-up, and manufacturing services for custom renewable chemistry used across personal care, cosmetics, flavors and fragrances, and other industries, emphasizing resilient supply chains, product consistency, and reduced ecological impact. Amyris is a private company that emerged from a 2023 Chapter 11 restructuring; it does not currently publish a public developer API or technology platform.

providers.name: Tahoe
providers.description: Tahoe (Tahoe Therapeutics) is a San Francisco AI-biotech company building "the ground truth for biological superintelligence." It generates gigascale perturbative single-cell datasets and trains foundation models of the human cell to design therapeutics, starting with cancer. Flagship open assets include Tahoe-100M — the largest interventional single-cell dataset to date (100M+ transcriptomes across ~1,100 chemical perturbations and 50 cancer cell lines) — and Tahoe-x1, a family of perturbation-trained single-cell foundation models with up to 3 billion parameters, released fully open-source with open weights plus training and evaluation code. Tahoe's Mosaic platform makes in vivo, single-cell-resolution data generation scalable. Backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital, Tahoe publishes no commercial REST API; its programmatic surface is open-source models, datasets, and the first-party tahoe-x1 Python library.

providers.name: Biostack Platforms
providers.description: BioStack Platforms is a San Francisco healthcare-data company (Y Combinator Spring 2026, backed by Afore Capital, Verdict, Heroic VC, and angels from Meta and Google DeepMind) building the data engine for healthcare and drug-discovery AI. It sources and structures ML-ready biomedical datasets — longitudinal, multimodal data across EHR, medical imaging, ECGs, labs, clinical notes, audio, and outcomes — and turns real clinical and preclinical workflows into training environments, evals, reward functions, and verifiable tasks for reinforcement learning and post-training. It serves biotech startups, frontier AI labs, and healthcare data companies. At profiling time BioStack publishes a marketing site and blog only; it exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this remains an identity-only profile in the API Evangelist network pending a public developer offering.

providers.name: Clinflash
providers.description: Clinflash (易迪希医药科技 / Clinflash Healthcare Technology) is a Chinese clinical-research technology company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud-based clinical trial information platform for pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and research sites. Its self-developed suite spans more than ten systems, including Clinflash EDC (electronic data capture), IRT/IWRS (randomization and trial supply management), eCOA/ePRO (electronic clinical outcome and patient-reported outcomes), Safety/PV (pharmacovigilance and drug-safety alerting), CTMS (clinical trial management), eTMF (electronic trial master file), eCTD, eConsent, eSign, Coder (medical coding), and ePAY (subject payment). Clinflash has supported thousands of clinical trial projects for over a thousand pharmaceutical, generic, medical-device, and IVD organizations, including pivotal Phase III and international multi-center studies. The platform is delivered as a login-gated SaaS at cloud.clinflash.com and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer/API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Orchestra Bio
providers.description: Orchestra (orchestra.bio) is an agentic operations platform for drug development and life sciences R&D organizations, helping teams unify planning across leadership, programs, and scientific groups, automate R&D workflows, and reduce the operational risks that derail breakthrough science. The San Francisco company pairs unified program roadmaps with intelligent operations and decision support, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), 8VC, Haystack, and other investors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Orchestra publishes a product marketing site, a company blog, and a hosted web application, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: PolyXLabs
providers.description: PolyXLabs is a Techstars-backed biotechnology and sustainable-materials company developing biodegradable plastic alternatives from lignocellulose-based biomass, including food waste such as spent coffee grounds. The company produces customized, toxin-free, microplastic-free polymers designed to be lightweight and durable as drop-in replacements for conventional plastics in consumer goods and packaging, with operations across the United States and Europe and headquarters in Martonvasar, Hungary. PolyXLabs currently publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Barinthus Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Barinthus Biotherapeutics plc (Nasdaq: BRNS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel immunotherapies designed to guide and reprogram T cells to overcome autoimmunity, inflammatory disease, chronic viral infection, and cancer. Its lead SNAP-TI and SNAP-CI antigen-specific platforms and ChAdOx/MVA immunotherapeutic candidates power a five-program pipeline including VTP-1000 (celiac disease), VTP-300 (chronic hepatitis B), VTP-200 (high-risk HPV), VTP-850 (recurrent prostate cancer), and VTP-1100 (HPV-related cancer). The company was formed in 2021 through the merger of Oxford University spinout Vaccitech plc and NIH/Johns Hopkins spinout Avidea Technologies, and is headquartered in Germantown, Maryland with research facilities in the UK. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or agent surface.

providers.name: biolink
providers.description: BioLink (百林科医药科技（上海）有限公司) is a Shanghai-based bioprocessing company that manufactures core equipment and single-use consumable solutions for biopharmaceutical manufacturing. Its product lines span cell culture and bioreactors, fluid management, chromatography purification, process filtration, and pre-formulated aqueous products (buffers, water for injection, defoamers), serving antibody therapeutics and ADCs, vaccines, cell and gene therapy, and recombinant protein production. BioLink is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: dMed Global (Caidya)
providers.description: dMed Global, now operating as Caidya, is a global, full-service clinical research organization (CRO) headquartered in Shanghai, China and backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company provides flexible, patient-centric clinical trial solutions to biopharmaceutical innovators, running studies across more than 40 countries and regions. Its capabilities span clinical operations, regulatory services, data management, biostatistics, and complex trial execution across core therapeutic areas. Caidya operates an English-language corporate site at caidya.com and a Chinese-language site at caidya.cn. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; the company publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Draig Therapeutics
providers.description: Draig Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformative, best-in-class therapies for major neuropsychiatric disorders, including Major Depressive Disorder. A Cardiff University spinout co-founded with SV Health Investors, Draig ("dragon" in Welsh) leverages its founders' expertise in modulating the core glutamate/GABA pathways that underlie synaptic excitation and inhibition imbalance in the brain. Its pipeline is led by DT-101, a next-generation AMPA receptor positive allosteric modulator (PAM) advancing toward Phase 2 in MDD, alongside DT-201 and DT-301, subtype-selective GABAA receptor modulators. The company launched from stealth in June 2025 with a $140 million (£107 million) oversubscribed Series A led by Access Biotechnology, with participation from Canaan Partners, SR One, Sanofi Ventures, Schroders Capital, SV Health Investors, and ICG. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Adcendo
providers.description: Adcendo ApS is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with US operations in Boston, Massachusetts, developing a new generation of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancers with high unmet medical need. Founded in 2017 out of research by Lars Henning Engelholm and Niels Behrendt, the company advances a clinical and pre-clinical pipeline that includes ADCE-T02 (targeting Tissue Factor, in the Phase 1b Tiffany-01 study across advanced solid tumors), ADCE-D01 (targeting uPARAP, granted FDA Fast Track designation for soft tissue sarcoma), and the pre-clinical ADCE-B05. Adcendo is a privately held, venture-backed therapeutics developer; it publishes a corporate website, pipeline and publications pages, and investor press releases, but it operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Altos Labs
providers.description: Altos Labs is a biotechnology company pursuing cellular rejuvenation programming to restore cell health and resilience, with the goal of reversing disease, injury, and the disabilities that can occur throughout life. Launched publicly in January 2022 with roughly $3 billion in initial funding from investors including Jeff Bezos and Yuri Milner, the company operates geographically distributed Institutes of Science in the San Francisco Bay Area, Cambridge (UK), and San Diego, alongside an Institute of Medicine and an Institute of Computation. Altos combines experimental biologists with computational scientists to translate laboratory discoveries in cell biology into transformative medicines. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; as a research-stage life-sciences company it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Arcus Biosciences
providers.description: Arcus Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated cancer immunotherapies, headquartered in Hayward, California. Its pipeline pairs multiple novel molecules across intra-tumoral immune pathways, including the HIF-2a inhibitor casdatifan, the CD73 inhibitor quemliclustat, the anti-TIGIT antibody domvanalimab, the anti-PD-1 antibody zimberelimab, and the CD39 inhibitor AB598. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile. Arcus publishes an agent-facing surface (llms.txt, an AI content map, and an Organization schema) but no public developer API.

providers.name: Candid Therapeutics
providers.description: Candid Therapeutics is a San Diego, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing T-cell engager (TCE) antibody therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Launched publicly in September 2024 with a $370 million Series A financing and assembled by acquiring Vignette Bio and TRC 2004, Candid in-licenses differentiated bispecific TCE assets and advances them through US clinical development. Its approach redirects T-cells to selectively deplete autoreactive B-cells, aiming for deeper and more durable depletion than conventional antibody therapy without the manufacturing burden of cell therapy. Its lead investigational asset, cizutamig, is a BCMA x CD3 bispecific antibody. UCB completed its acquisition of Candid Therapeutics on 17 June 2026 for up to $2.2 billion ($2.0 billion upfront plus up to $200 million in milestones), and the company now operates as part of UCB. Candid Therapeutics publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: CorWave
providers.description: CorWave SA is a French clinical-stage medical device company, incorporated in 2012 by the startup studio MD Start and headquartered in Clichy, France, that develops implantable cardiac assist pumps for patients with advanced heart failure. Its patented wave membrane technology — a biomimetic polymer membrane driven by an electromagnetic actuator, inspired by the undulating movement of marine animals — produces truly pulsatile, physiological blood flow, differentiating the CorWave LVAS and Nemo pumps from commercially available rotary-pump LVADs. The company has raised more than EUR 80 million, operates an urban manufacturing facility in Clichy, employs more than 90 people, and announced the first in-human implantation of its Left Ventricular Assist System in 2025. CorWave LVAS remains an investigational device and is not approved for commercial use in any country. CorWave publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Link Cell Therapies
providers.description: Link Cell Therapies is a South San Francisco clinical-stage cell therapy company founded by Stanford investigators Robbie Majzner and Crystal Mackall in partnership with Samsara BioCapital, working on the development of safe and effective CAR T agents for patients with solid tumors. The company's logic-gate technology produces AND-gate CAR T cells that require co-expression of two cancer targets before driving cell cytotoxicity, giving greater tumor specificity than existing logic-gate approaches and aiming to avoid off-tumor toxicity. Alongside additional platforms under development, Link is advancing therapeutic programs across solid tumors and certain hematologic cancers, including a dual-targeting AND-gated CAR program (LNK001) directed at clear cell renal cell carcinoma, and in January 2026 entered a strategic collaboration with Johnson & Johnson to develop logic-gate LINK CAR T therapies. Link Cell Therapies publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface; this profile captures company identity and probed public-surface posture only.

providers.name: Rejoni
providers.description: Rejoni, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage women's health medical device company founded in June 2020 by serial entrepreneur Amar Sawhney, PhD and Pramand LLC, and headquartered at 201 Burlington Road in Bedford, Massachusetts. It develops proprietary hydrogel-based biomaterial therapies for gynecological surgery, with a stated mission of protecting, preserving and healing the uterus. Its lead product, the Juveena Hydrogel System, is designed to prevent the formation and reformation of intrauterine adhesions (IUAs) — the scar tissue that forms after transcervical procedures such as dilation and curettage, myomectomy or treatment of heavy bleeding, and a leading cause of infertility and abnormal uterine bleeding. The system pairs a low-profile proprietary transcervical catheter with two liquid precursors that cross-link on delivery into a soft, temporary hydrogel implant that mechanically separates the uterine walls during healing and then resorbs on its own in roughly two to three weeks, about one menstrual cycle, so no removal procedure is required. Juveena is investigational only and pending FDA approval; the FDA filed Rejoni's premarket approval (PMA) application in January 2026, and the company completed patient enrollment in its US IDE pivotal study. Rejoni closed a $25 million financing in June 2026 with ClavystBio, Amed Ventures, Ascension Ventures, Catalyst Health Ventures, Delos Capital, FemHealth Ventures, Iyengar Capital and Sparta Group, and appointed women's health MedTech leader John Nealon as chief executive officer in May 2026. Rejoni runs no developer program and publishes no public API: its entire web presence is a small Webflow marketing site, and probes for OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path returned HTTP 404 against a verified real-404 origin, while api./developer./docs./app./portal.rejoni.com resolve only to a wildcard A record with no listener answering on either port 80 or 443.

providers.name: Andes
providers.description: Andes (Andes Ag, Inc.) is a climate-technology and agricultural-biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California. Andes engineers and selects beneficial soil microorganisms that are applied alongside seed in commodity row-crop production — corn, soybean, wheat and canola — where they accelerate the natural conversion of atmospheric carbon dioxide into stable soil inorganic carbon (carbonate minerals), a process the company calls Microbial Carbon Mineralization. Andes sells the resulting durable carbon dioxide removal as verified credits to corporate buyers and Scope 3 programs, and pays participating growers through the Andes Carbon Program. The company published the first Microbial Carbon Mineralization methodology, developed with EcoEngineers under ISO 14064, and has run field trials with Bayer, Cargill, Corteva, Nutrien and Wilbur-Ellis. Andes has raised roughly $38M, including a Series A co-led by Leaps by Bayer and Cavallo Ventures, and its shares trade on private secondary venues including EquityZen and Nasdaq Private Market. Andes publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Infinitopes
providers.description: Infinitopes is an Oxford University spinout biotech company (founded 2021, based at the BioEscalator in Oxford, UK) developing off-the-shelf precision cancer vaccines aimed at preventing deaths from cancer metastases. Its proprietary Precision Immunomics platform identifies tumor-specific antigens by integrating immunopeptidomics, advanced laboratory methods, machine learning, and validated biological testing across cancer types, paired with engineered viral vectors that elicit protective CD8 T-cell responses. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Amplify Partners (also supported by Cancer Research UK). This is a digital-biology company profile; Infinitopes publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Insempra
providers.description: Insempra is a biotechnology company that produces sustainable, bio-based ingredients using precision fermentation. It develops alternatives to petrochemical and naturally-extracted ingredients for the beauty and personal care, food and nutrition, and fibers and performance materials industries. Products include a bio-based Phenyl Ethyl Alcohol fragrance ingredient, an Omega-7 biolipid, and Biomelanin (in development), produced from agricultural and forestry waste streams through circular manufacturing. Insempra is a portfolio company of EQT Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Seismic Therapeutic
providers.description: Seismic Therapeutic is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformative biologic medicines for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. The company pairs structural biology with machine learning through its proprietary IMPACT platform to design multi-functional antibodies and Immunoglobulin Sculpting (IgSc) enzymes across cell-mediated, allergic, and antibody-mediated immune diseases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As a therapeutics R&D company it publishes no public developer or API surface at seismictx.com; this profile captures its corporate identity only.

providers.name: Ampersand Biomedicines
providers.description: Ampersand Biomedicines is a Boston-based biotechnology company founded in 2020 out of Flagship Pioneering that designs programmable biologic medicines intended to act only at the site of disease. Its computationally powered Address, Navigate, Determine (AND) Platform pairs a multi-omics "Address Map" of healthy and diseased human tissue with high-throughput microfluidic binder generation and AI-guided binder prediction to design AND-Body therapeutics, which combine a localizing element with an actuator so activity is conditional on the target tissue. The company raised a $65M Series B in March 2025 from Flagship Pioneering and Eli Lilly, and partners with Pioneering Medicines and Pfizer. It is a preclinical therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: the computational platform is internal tooling for its own drug discovery and is not offered to third parties, and the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Atomic AI
providers.description: Atomic AI is a biotechnology company fusing machine learning with structural biology to unlock RNA drug discovery. Founded in 2017 by Raphael Townshend and based in San Francisco, the company builds ATOM-1, an AI foundation model that predicts the three-dimensional structure of RNA to enable the discovery and optimization of RNA-targeted small molecules and RNA-based medicines for previously undruggable targets, including certain cancers and neurodegenerative diseases. Atomic AI pairs its proprietary 3D RNA structure engine with large-scale in-house wet-lab assays. It is backed by Playground Global, 8VC, Greylock, and others. Atomic AI operates as a proprietary R&D drug-discovery platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and web-surface signals for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Beacon Therapeutics
providers.description: Beacon Therapeutics is a clinical-stage ophthalmic gene therapy company founded in 2023 to save and restore the sight of people living with rare and prevalent retinal diseases that lead to blindness. Built around adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy, the company delivers functional copies of mutated genes into retinal cells so the body can produce the missing therapeutic protein. Its lead clinical program, laru-zova (laruparetigene zovaparvovec), targets X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP), alongside preclinical programs in dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD) and cone-rod dystrophy (CRD), the latter in-licensed from the University of Oxford. Beacon operates across the United Kingdom and the United States, with a corporate base in London and a US presence in the Cambridge, Massachusetts area. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software or data platform company, and publishes no public API, SDK or developer program.

providers.name: Berry Genomics
providers.description: Berry Genomics (Beijing Berry and Kang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., 贝瑞基因) is a Chinese genomics and genetic-testing company operating across reproductive health screening, hereditary disease detection, tumor and cancer diagnostics, laboratory solutions, sequencing equipment and reagents, and genomic big-data services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company publishes a corporate marketing site (news, investor relations, careers, and a legal statement) but does not currently expose a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: BioAge Labs
providers.description: BioAge Labs (Nasdaq ticker BIOA) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Emeryville, California, developing therapies that target the biology of human aging to treat metabolic diseases such as obesity and its related conditions. Its proprietary discovery platform mines longitudinal human multi-omics data to identify aging-related molecular pathways, which feed a therapeutic pipeline that includes BGE-102, an oral NLRP3 inhibitor aimed at chronic inflammation and cardiovascular risk, and an APJ (apelin receptor) agonist developed as an exercise mimetic for obesity. The company is backed by a16z and Redpoint Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile. BioAge Labs publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time; this profile captures its corporate and web-property identity plus a domain-security probe of its primary web host.

providers.name: Braveheart Bio
providers.description: Braveheart Bio is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and related cardiac conditions. Its lead candidate, BHB-1893, is a selective cardiac myosin inhibitor (licensed as HRS-1893 from Hengrui Pharma) designed to reduce excessive heart-muscle contraction and improve cardiac performance in patients with obstructive and non-obstructive HCM. The San Francisco-based company launched in November 2025 with a $185M Series A led by a16z alongside Forbion, OrbiMed, Enavate Sciences, and Frazier Life Sciences, and filed for a Nasdaq IPO in July 2026. Braveheart Bio is a corporate/scientific organization and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals (CANbridge Life Sciences Ltd.) is a global, China-based biopharmaceutical company founded in 2012 that focuses on the research, development, and commercialization of transformative therapies for rare diseases and rare oncology. The company in-licenses and develops differentiated drug candidates from around the world for the Chinese and global markets, with a portfolio of approved products and a gene-therapy and enzyme-replacement pipeline. Headquartered in Beijing with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Suzhou, and Burlington, Massachusetts (USA), CANbridge is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming; CANbridge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Carrick Therapeutics
providers.description: Carrick Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, developing novel oncology therapies aimed at improving outcomes for patients with aggressive and treatment-resistant cancers. Its pipeline centers on transcriptional CDK inhibition, led by samuraciclib (a CDK7 inhibitor in Phase 2) and CT7439 (a CDK12/13 inhibitor in Phase 1), pursued as combination therapies across advanced hormone-receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, and additional indications. The company is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: CereVasc
providers.description: CereVasc, Inc. is a clinical-stage medical device company developing novel, minimally invasive treatments for patients with neurological diseases. Its lead product, the eShunt System, uses percutaneous transvenous-transdural access to the central nervous system to treat communicating hydrocephalus — including normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) — as a less invasive alternative to conventional neurosurgical shunt placement. The eShunt System is an investigational device limited by United States federal law to investigational use, and is being evaluated in the STRIDE pivotal study (NCT06498960). CereVasc raised a $70M Series B in 2024 and has received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation. The company builds implantable hardware and publishes no public API, developer program, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cofactor Genomics
providers.description: Cofactor Genomics is a precision-medicine biotechnology company that applies RNA-sequencing and machine learning to build predictive immuno-oncology diagnostics. Its flagship OncoPrism assay is designed to predict which cancer patients will respond to immunotherapy, and the company runs the multi-center PREDAPT clinical trial across more than 24 healthcare systems spanning 11 solid-tumor cancers. Cofactor Genomics is a diagnostics and life-sciences company rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (DCVC, Menlo Ventures, Y Combinator) and enriched with identity and domain-security metadata.

providers.name: Convoke
providers.description: Convoke is building an AI-native operating system for the biopharmaceutical industry. Founded in 2024 and based in South San Francisco, the platform unifies fragmented internal knowledge, workflows, and external data into a continuously updating workspace, codifies the decision logic behind high-stakes choices, and generates critical deliverables such as competitive intelligence briefs, portfolio strategy analyses, market research, and scientific manuscripts across the drug development lifecycle. Convoke serves biopharma teams working in business development, competitive intelligence, portfolio strategy, market research, and medical affairs. The company raised an $8.6M seed round co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Dimension. As of this profile, Convoke publishes a public marketing and company site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Deep Genomics
providers.description: Deep Genomics is an AI-driven genetic medicines platform company based in Toronto, Canada. It uses biological foundation models (its BioFM Platform) and lab-integrated AI workflows to discover and develop RNA-based genetic medicines, combining AI model development, high-throughput screening technologies, and information systems to accelerate drug discovery and advance new treatments. Founded by deep learning researcher Brendan Frey, the company is backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta and SoftBank Vision Fund. It surfaces no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Delphia Therapeutics
providers.description: Delphia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology biotechnology company pioneering "activation lethality," a precision-medicine approach that targets cancer cells' vulnerability to oncogene overactivation by selectively over-activating cancer-linked signaling until tumor cells can no longer survive. Founded by oncology drug developers Kevin Marks, Bill Sellers, and Mike Dillon, the company launched with a $67 million Series A financing led by GV, with participation from Nextech Invest, Polaris Innovation Fund, and Alexandria Venture Investments. Delphia is a preclinical-stage drug developer and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Earli
providers.description: Earli is a biotech company using AI-designed genetic switches for early cancer detection and treatment. Its synthetic-biomarker technology forces cancer cells to reveal themselves for earlier, more accurate detection, and can program cancer cells to self-destruct while sparing healthy tissue. Founded by Cyriac Roeding and backed by a16z and Menlo Ventures, Earli is a research-stage company with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Formation Bio
providers.description: Formation Bio is an AI-native pharmaceutical company building the pharma company of the future. Rather than applying AI to drug discovery, it focuses on drug development — acquiring and in-licensing clinical-stage drug candidates from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then running them through clinical development far more efficiently than industry standards using its proprietary AI-native platform, data, and fine-tuned models. Led by CEO Benjamine Liu and CTO Linhao Zhang, the company raised a $372M Series D in 2024 led by a16z with participation from Sanofi, Sequoia, Thrive, Emerson Collective, and others, and partners with Sanofi and OpenAI on custom models for the drug development lifecycle. Formation Bio does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Granza Bio
providers.description: Granza Bio is an early-stage biotechnology company reprogramming immunity for target-specific medicines. Founded in 2024 by Dr. Ashwin Nandakumar, Dr. Ashwin Jainarayanan, and Prof. Michael Dustin, the company builds on the discovery of "attack particles" — killing entities released by cytotoxic immune cells, characterized in Prof. Dustin's laboratory at the University of Oxford. Granza Bio is developing an engineered delivery-shell platform that directs therapeutic cargo to specific tissues, with the goal of advancing treatments for cancers, autoimmune disorders, and infections. The company raised $7.14M in seed funding co-led by Refactor Capital and Felicis, with participation from Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator. It is a research-stage life-sciences company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: ImmuneBridge
providers.description: ImmuneBridge is a San Francisco biotech company building a first-in-class integrated screening and manufacturing platform for allogeneic cell therapies. The company screens and expands stem cells from multiple sources (umbilical cord blood, mobilized blood, bone marrow), uses high-throughput automated assays with machine-learning models to predict donor and process performance early, and scales production with IBR403, a small molecule enabling up to 100,000-fold expansion of hematopoietic stem cells. The stated goal is to manufacture tens of thousands of affordable, high-quality immune cell doses (HSCs, NK cells, T cells, and more) from a single cord blood unit. ImmuneBridge is backed by Insight Partners, NFX Bio, M Ventures, and other institutional investors. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Inari
providers.description: Inari Agriculture, Inc. — "The SEEDesign company" — is a Cambridge, Massachusetts agricultural biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering in 2016, with additional sites in West Lafayette, Indiana and Ghent, Belgium. Its SEEDesign platform combines genomics, artificial intelligence and predictive design with a multiplex gene-editing toolbox to accelerate crop improvement in soybean, corn and wheat, targeting 10-20% yield gains alongside roughly 40% reductions in nitrogen and water use. Inari runs a partner-first, business-to-business model, licensing designed seed to independent seed companies and breeders rather than selling to farmers directly. Inari publishes an llms.txt at inari.com/llms.txt but operates no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; its data platform (Databricks-based) is internal. Not to be confused with the unrelated medical-device company Inari Medical.

providers.name: Inceptive
providers.description: Inceptive is an AI biotechnology company founded in 2021 by transformer co-author Jakob Uszkoreit and Stanford biochemist Rhiju Das, building foundation models of life to rationally design sequence-based medicines such as mRNA, siRNA, ASOs, and peptides. The company pairs large-scale deep learning with high-throughput in-house wet-lab experiments in a tight design-build-test loop, then licenses successful molecules to pharmaceutical partners. Inceptive is headquartered in Palo Alto with offices in Berlin and Zurich, is backed by a16z Bio + Health, Obvious Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA), and S32, and has announced strategic collaborations including a multi-year agreement with Alnylam Pharmaceuticals. Inceptive is a research-partner biotech and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Menten AI
providers.description: Menten AI is a biotechnology company pioneering generative AI for peptide drug design. Its MAUD 1.0 platform designs peptide macrocycles de novo for complex, previously undruggable targets by combining generative AI with physics-based models and quantum simulations, reporting nanomolar potency, oral bioavailability, cell permeability, and a greater-than-90% hit rate. The company operates through enterprise partnerships with pharmaceutical organizations rather than a public developer platform, and at the time of this profile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation.
