Its lead product is Zorifertinib (formerly AZD-3759, marketed as Zorifer), a next-generation EGFR TKI designed for EGFR mutation positive advanced NSCLC patients with central nervous system metastases, which received NMPA approval in November 2024 as the first EGFR-TKI indicated for lung cancer with brain metastases. Alpha Biopharma also partners with Wugen Inc. on universal off-the-shelf memory NK and CAR-T cell therapies. The company raised a Series A led by Qiming Venture Partners. Alpha Biopharma publishes a corporate marketing website only and operates no public API, developer portal, or software platform.

providers.name: Alume Biosciences
providers.description: Alume Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in La Jolla, California, developing nerve-targeted fluorescent agents for precision surgery. Its lead candidate, bevonescein (ALM-488) — a peptide-dye conjugate co-invented by the late Nobel Laureate Dr. Roger Tsien and surgeon Dr. Quyen Nguyen — is administered intravenously roughly an hour before an operation so surgeons can see nerves illuminated in the surgical field and avoid inadvertent nerve injury. The compound has FDA Fast Track designation, is in Phase 3 pivotal trials in head-and-neck surgery, and the company has stated it plans a New Drug Application submission in 2026. Alume is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ankyra Therapeutics
providers.description: Ankyra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing "anchored" immunotherapies for cancer and immune-mediated diseases. Its proprietary platform tethers immune-modulating drugs to aluminum hydroxide so that treatment concentrates locally at the disease site, broadening the therapeutic window while reducing systemic toxicity and dosing frequency. The lead candidate, ANK-101, is an anchored IL-12 therapy in clinical evaluation for patients with advanced solid tumors. Ankyra is backed by investors including Google Ventures (GV), Mithril, Polaris Partners, Sands Capital, and Fidelity. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Ansun Biopharma
providers.description: Ansun Biopharma is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in the Sorrento Valley district of San Diego, California, founded in 2003 by virologists and molecular biologists and led by CEO Dr. Nancy Chang. Rather than targeting viruses directly, Ansun develops host-directed immuno-biologic therapies built on a recombinant sialidase platform. Its lead candidate, DAS181 (Ansun-181), is a multi-function sialidase fusion protein that removes the sialic acid receptors respiratory viruses use to enter host cells, and has been studied in parainfluenza virus (PIV), severe influenza, human metapneumovirus and COVID-19 in immunocompromised and hospitalized patients. The company also advances earlier-stage programs in oncology and autoimmune disease from the same sialidase platform. Ansun is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate WordPress site covering its pipeline, research and technologies, publications, intellectual property, investors, news and careers, and exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: BioTheryX
providers.description: BioTheryX is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, discovering and developing first-in-class targeted protein degraders — both bifunctional degraders and molecular glues — for cancer and inflammatory disease. Its proprietary PRODEGY platform is built on Cereblon-binding expertise carried over from founders who worked on FDA-approved Cereblon modulators. The lead program BTX-9341, a dual CDK4/CDK6 degrader, is in Phase 1 for HR+/HER2- breast cancer, alongside BTX-10908 targeting SOS1 for pan-KRAS mutant cancers and PDE4 degraders for inflammatory conditions; the company also partners with Incyte on molecular glue degrader discovery. BioTheryX is a therapeutics developer with no public developer program: probes on 2026-08-02 returned 404 for /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path on biotheryx.com, and there is no api./developer./docs./portal. subdomain, GitHub organization, or published SDK.

providers.name: Cullgen
providers.description: Cullgen Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2018 and focused on first-in-class targeted protein degradation medicines. Its proprietary uSMITE (ubiquitin-mediated, small molecule-induced target elimination) platform harnesses the body's own ubiquitin-proteasome system to selectively degrade disease-causing intracellular proteins, including targets considered undruggable by conventional small molecules, and the company extends that chemistry into degrader-antibody conjugates (DACs). Its lead TRK degrader program has entered Phase 1 clinical dosing, and the company has partnered with Astellas and taken investment from AstraZeneca. Gyre Therapeutics completed an all-stock acquisition of Cullgen valued at approximately $300 million on 4 May 2026. Cullgen publishes a corporate marketing website only: profiling on 2026-08-04 found no developer portal, documentation, machine-readable API contract, package registry presence, or public code repositories.

providers.name: FindMeCure
providers.description: FindMeCure is a Sofia, Bulgaria healthtech company (founded 2015, backed by Techstars) that connects patients with clinical trials through a patient-facing search engine often described as "the Google of clinical trials," letting people search, find, and join a trial within a few clicks. Its sister B2B product, TrialHub, is a clinical-trial strategy, feasibility, and patient-recruitment intelligence platform covering 70 countries and serving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs including Takeda, Novartis, and Syneos Health. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's identity and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: Immune-Onc Therapeutics
providers.description: Immune-Onc Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2016 by Charlene Liao and Guo Liang Yu. The company develops novel antibody therapeutics that target myeloid cell inhibitory receptors — with a current focus on the Leukocyte Immunoglobulin-Like Receptor subfamily B (LILRB) — to treat blood cancers, solid tumors, and autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its clinical pipeline includes IO-108, a fully human IgG4 antagonist antibody targeting LILRB2 (ILT4) in Phase 1b/2 for solid tumors including hepatocellular carcinoma, and IO-202, a first-in-class IgG1 antibody targeting LILRB4 (ILT3) in Phase 1b for acute myeloid leukemia and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, which holds FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations. Preclinical programs include IO-312, a LILRB4-directed bispecific antibody, and IO-106 targeting LAIR1. The company has clinical collaborations with BeiGene, Regeneron, and Roche, and has raised approximately $138 million across Series A and Series B financings from investors including Northern Light Venture Capital, Vivo Capital, CLI Ventures, and the Stanford-StartX Fund. Immune-Onc is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization and no /.well-known/ discovery surface — its only machine-readable documents are two Squarespace RSS feeds for its news and press-release collections. This record therefore captures the company's verified public identity, its published web properties, its clinical-trial registry presence, and the probed security posture of its public web surface.

providers.name: ArrePath
providers.description: ArrePath is an AI-driven pharmaceutical company based in Princeton, New Jersey, applying machine learning to accelerate small-molecule drug discovery in infectious disease. Its platform treats heterogeneous, small, and noisy bioactivity datasets as a modeling opportunity, enabling work on novel chemical classes where conventional approaches struggle; a public-data oral bioavailability model lifted a lead series from roughly 22% to 89% bioavailability. Lead programs include an oral LpxH inhibitor for outpatient urinary tract infections (pre-IND targeted mid-2026) and antibacterial programs against non-tuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) lung disease and tuberculosis, plus an early non-infectious discovery effort. ArrePath is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Arzeda
providers.description: Arzeda Corp is a Seattle, Washington protein design company — "The Protein Design Company" — founded in 2008 by David Baker (2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Alexandre Zanghellini and colleagues out of the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design. Its Intelligent Protein Design Technology combines physics-based computational protein design, generative AI and an agentic design-build-test-learn loop over fifteen years of proprietary in-house experimental data to create designer enzymes and proteins that do not exist in nature, then scale them to commercial production. Commercial programs span food and beverage (ViaLeaf Reb M / ProSweet Reb M stevia sweeteners with MANE), home and personal care enzymes (Unilever), advanced materials (W. L. Gore & Associates) and pharmaceutical biologics (Takeda), alongside DARPA and NSF funded work on AI-driven protein design and cell-free biomanufacturing. Arzeda co-founded the OpenFold consortium for open-source protein structure prediction. It sells designed molecules and joint development programs, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Basecamp Research
providers.description: Basecamp Research is a London-based biotech company mapping global genetic biodiversity to power AI-based design of biological systems. Its core asset is BaseGraph, a Neo4j-backed knowledge graph of billions of biological relationships assembled from novel protein and genome sequences collected under access-and-benefit-sharing partnerships with biodiversity-rich countries. On top of this data it builds foundation models and tools including EDEN (a large-scale biology sequence model), BaseFold (3D protein structure prediction that improves on AlphaFold2 for large, complex structures and small-molecule interactions), and BaseScan (an automated annotation pipeline). Basecamp works with pharma and biotech partners on drug discovery and enzyme/protein design, and has collaborated with NVIDIA to bring BaseFold to the BioNeMo platform. Backed by True Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Basecamp Research currently exposes no public self-serve developer API - data and models are accessed via partnerships, and product docs sit behind an authenticated portal.

providers.name: BigHat Biosciences
providers.description: BigHat Biosciences is a biotechnology company that pairs machine learning with a high-throughput, fully integrated wet lab to design next-generation antibody-based therapeutics. Its platform closes the loop between in-silico antibody design and in-house synthesis and characterization, generating proprietary experimental data that trains its models and speeds the discovery of biologics with improved developability. The company has publicly discussed its Reccy antibody design studio (RADS) and has entered machine-learning-enabled biologics collaborations with Eli Lilly (including Lilly TuneLab), Johnson & Johnson, and Lonza/Synaffix. BigHat is a private, venture-backed company (8VC, a16z) and maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source computational-biology tooling. It does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: DEM Bio
providers.description: DEM BioPharma is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing first-in-class cancer therapeutics that target the signals solid tumors use to evade immune destruction. The company pioneers next-generation macrophage and innate-immune immunotherapies discovered through its proprietary CHoMP (Co-culture with Human Myeloid Phagocytes) functional-genomics platform, which uses CRISPR-based screening to identify novel "don't-eat-me" and activating targets on myeloid cells. DEM launched in 2022 with $70M in Series A financing and is backed by Longwood Fund, Emerson Collective, Pfizer Ventures, Astellas, and Insight Partners. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; DEM publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Ditto Biosciences
providers.description: Ditto Biosciences (Ditto Bio) is a San Francisco biotechnology startup, founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch), that discovers drugs for autoimmune diseases by identifying and engineering immune-controlling proteins that parasites, viruses, ticks, and worms have naturally evolved over millions of years to modulate the human immune system. The company pairs an AI platform with wet-lab biology to mine more than a million natural proteins, identify candidates predicted to hit clinically validated human immune-disease targets, and transform them into therapeutic candidates. Ditto is an early-stage, three-person team led by founders Dennis Sun (CEO), Adair Borges (CSO), and Emily Weiss (CTO). This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Ditto Bio currently publishes a marketing and science website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Insilico Medicine
providers.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

providers.name: Isomorphic Labs
providers.description: Isomorphic Labs is a London-based AI-first drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 and operating as an Alphabet subsidiary. Founded and led by Sir Demis Hassabis, the company applies frontier AI — including derivatives of the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system and its proprietary Unified Drug Design Engine — to accelerate the design of small-molecule and biologic therapeutics across oncology, immunology, and other therapeutic areas. The Drug Design Engine is positioned as a target- and disease-agnostic, multi-modality platform that combines predictive and generative models with a curated proprietary life-science "Dataverse" and large-scale GPU infrastructure. Isomorphic Labs monetises through strategic pharmaceutical research collaborations — disclosed deals include Novartis (January 2024, expanded February 2025), Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson (January 2026) — and through its own internal therapeutic pipeline. The company closed a $600M external Series B investment round in March 2025. Isomorphic Labs does not operate a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of its Drug Design Engine; external researcher access to AlphaFold-family models is provided separately by Google DeepMind via the free AlphaFold Server (alphafoldserver.com) for non-commercial use, and via the open-source AlphaFold 3 inference code released by DeepMind. The Isomorphic Labs GitHub organisation hosts only a small number of forks of internal Kubernetes and configuration-management tooling.

providers.name: Joes Future Food (Zhouzi Future)
providers.description: Joes Future Food (周子未来 / Nanjing Zhouzi Future Food Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Nanjing-based cellular agriculture and food-technology company pioneering cultivated (cell-cultured) meat in China. The founding team produced what it describes as China's first piece of cultivated meat, and the company develops cell-cultured pork products (pork belly, fatback, skin, meatballs, and a mixed family pack) alongside serum-free culture media and a catalog of primary and gene-edited animal cell lines (porcine adipose and muscle stem cells, bovine muscle and adipose cells, chicken embryo fibroblasts, and more) used across cultivated-meat research and biomanufacturing. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company runs a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Mendel AI
providers.description: Mendel AI is a San Jose, California clinical AI company founded in 2017 by Dr. Karim Galil to streamline oncology research by organizing real-world data and accelerating clinical-trial workflows. Its flagship platform, Mendel Hypercube, pairs large language models with a clinician-built clinical knowledge hypergraph to add physician-like reasoning to LLMs operating over electronic health records, pathology reports, genomic data, clinician notes, claims, diagnostic data, and EDC submissions. Hypercube is offered as three productized experiences — Hypercube Cohort for patient cohort discovery (with funnel-style criteria analysis and direct integration to clinicaltrials.gov), Hypercube Analyst for AI-driven analysis of structured and unstructured real-world data, and Build Your Own Hypercube for custom clinical-data queries. The platform integrates with enterprise data warehouses (Databricks, Snowflake) and BI tools (Tableau, Qlik), and is available through the AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Azure Marketplace, and natively on the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. Mendel serves pharma, providers, payers, and research organizations including Quest Diagnostics, Boston Scientific, Gatehouse Bio, and the University of Pennsylvania, with published evidence in oncology trial prescreening. Mendel has no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source GitHub repositories; integration is delivered through enterprise contracts and cloud-marketplace deployments.

providers.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) is a Salt Lake City-based AI-enabled drug discovery company that operates the Recursion Operating System (Recursion OS), a vertically integrated platform combining automated wet-lab cellular phenomics, transcriptomics (Trekseq), proteomics, ADME, chemistry, and patient data with machine learning to map biology and design drug candidates. The platform runs on BioHive-2, a NVIDIA-built supercomputer ranked among the top global systems and dedicated to biopharma workloads, and is fed by 50+ petabytes of proprietary biological and chemical data. In November 2024 Recursion completed the acquisition of Exscientia, folding Exscientia's generative AI chemistry, Centaur Chemist, and clinical pipeline into the combined company; Recursion now runs more than 10 clinical and preclinical programs (REC-4881 for FAP, REC-3565 MALT1 inhibitor, REC-1245 RBM39 for biomarker-enriched solid tumors and lymphomas, REC-617 CDK7 inhibitor, REC-994 for cerebral cavernous malformation, REC-2282 for NF2- mutated meningiomas, REC-4209 for IPF, REC-7735 for HSD obesity), 10+ advanced discovery programs, and 10+ partnered programs across Roche (Genentech), Bayer, Sanofi, and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt). Recursion does not currently expose paid commercial APIs to external developers; assets and data access are delivered through licensing, scientific collaborations, and the MapApp web product. Externally, Recursion ships substantial open tooling: the RxRx family of open phenomics datasets (RxRx1, RxRx2, RxRx3, RxRx3-core, RxRx19a, RxRx19b) hosted at rxrx.ai and Hugging Face, the OpenPhenom-S/16 foundation model (released on Hugging Face and Google Cloud's Model Garden, with Phenom-Beta on NVIDIA BioNeMo), the MolE molecular foundation model, the gflownet library for graph and molecular generative modeling, SynFlowNet/synflownet-boltz for retrosynthesis-aware molecular design, maes_microscopy (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight masked autoencoders for cell microscopy), and rxrx1-utils for the NeurIPS 2019 CellSignal competition. The combination positions Recursion as a Tier-2 AI drug discovery provider with no commercial API surface but a meaningful open-source and open-model presence aimed at the computational biology research community.

providers.name: Synonym
providers.description: Synonym (rebranding to Roebling) is a biomanufacturing infrastructure and finance company founded in 2022 by Edward Shenderovich and Joshua Lachter and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It develops, finances, and builds commercial-scale bio-manufacturing facilities to give synthetic biology producers flexible fermentation capacity, and it operates bioproduction tools including a techno-economic modeling suite (TEA/FEL-1/FEL-2 engines) and the Capacitor-powered Match platform that connects clients with production capacity. As of this profile Synonym publishes only a marketing website and private product surfaces; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Until Labs
providers.description: Until Labs (branded "until") is a San Francisco deep-tech biotechnology company developing reversible cryopreservation technology for human donor organs. Its mission is to build a "pause button for biology" by safely vitrifying organs at ultra-low temperatures without ice formation, then rewarming them for transplant — extending the viability window for donor organs and improving transplant outcomes. The company builds perfusion hardware, cryoprotective agents, cooling and rewarming infrastructure, and organ-health assessment methods, working toward whole-body medical hibernation. Co-founded by Laura Deming and Hunter Davis, Until has raised over $100M including a $58M Series A (September 2025) led by Founders Fund with Lux Capital participating. As a wet-lab hardware and life-sciences company, Until publishes no public developer API, SDK, or software platform. This profile was surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: BociMed
providers.description: Shanghai BociMed Pharmaceutical Research Co., Ltd. (上海博志研新药物研究有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CRO/CDMO founded in 2012 in the Zhangjiang Pharmaceutical Valley, Shanghai, with an R&D headquarters in Zhangjiang, a production base in Lingang, and a clinical subsidiary in Chengdu. BociMed offers small-molecule chemistry, CMC and process development, a portfolio of drug delivery technology platforms (oral, injectable, nasal, pulmonary, transdermal, ocular, implant, liposome and exosome), clinical research and SMO services, global regulatory registration consulting, and commercial API, intermediate and solid-dosage manufacturing. It is a laboratory and manufacturing services business rather than a software vendor: it publishes a marketing website in Chinese and English and no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Alexion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Alexion Pharmaceuticals was a global biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on developing life-transforming therapies for rare diseases. Founded in 1992, the company pioneered complement inhibition therapy and developed leading treatments for rare hematological and neurological conditions including Soliris (eculizumab) and Ultomiris (ravulizumab). AstraZeneca acquired Alexion in July 2021 for $39 billion, and the company now operates as Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease. The combined entity maintains research programs in complement biology, hematology, nephrology, neurology, metabolic disorders, cardiology, and ophthalmology. Alexion's GitHub organization (alxndgb) hosts research tools including genomic data analysis platforms, precision medicine knowledge graphs, and rare disease target discovery systems.

providers.name: Applied Cognition
providers.description: Applied Cognition is a clinical-stage neuroscience company unlocking the therapeutic power of the brain's glymphatic system, the waste-clearance mechanism implicated in neurodegeneration. The company pairs a first-in-human, non-invasive platform for continuous, real-time measurement of glymphatic function (validated against contrast-enhanced MRI) with a small-molecule drug pipeline targeting Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and post-traumatic headache, supported by issued platform patents and datasets positioned for AI integration. Backed by Mayfield, it was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It is a therapeutics/medical company and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Arc Institute
providers.description: Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit biomedical research organization headquartered in Palo Alto, California, co-founded in 2021 by Silvana Konermann (Executive Director), Patrick Hsu (Core Investigator), and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison. With 300+ staff ("Arconauts") across 9 core laboratories and 5 technology centers, Arc develops AI foundation models for biology that span DNA, RNA, proteins, and single cells. Its flagship releases include Evo (Science, 2024) and Evo 2 (Nature, 2026) — DNA foundation models trained on trillions of nucleotides at single-nucleotide resolution with up to a 1-megabase context; STATE and Stack single-cell foundation models for cellular perturbation and in-context learning; the Arc Virtual Cell Atlas; the SRAgent LLM agents for bioinformatics; and the BINSEQ binary sequencing format. Models are released under Apache 2.0 on GitHub and Hugging Face, with hosted inference for Evo 2 available through NVIDIA BioNeMo and the NVIDIA build.nvidia.com API. Arc is funded by philanthropic donations from Patrick and John Collison, Vitalik Buterin, the Ron Conway family, Dustin Moskovitz, Daniel Gross, Elad Gil, and other technology benefactors; it does not sell APIs, SaaS, or models commercially.

providers.name: Auransa
providers.description: Auransa Inc. is a clinical-stage, AI-native biopharmaceutical company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2014 by Pek Lum. Auransa uses its proprietary SMarTR Engine — a hypothesis-free machine learning platform that mines human disease data such as RNA transcriptome and gene-expression profiles — to discover novel small-molecule therapeutics without starting from a predefined drug target. The company has analyzed more than 500,000 gene-expression profiles across roughly 70 diseases to identify molecular disease subtypes and match them to candidate compounds. Its lead program, AU-409, is a first-in-human Phase 1 candidate for liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma), with additional pipeline work in heart-safe chemotherapy and other oncology indications. Auransa is a DCVC / DCVC Bio portfolio company, also backed by Lux Capital, 11.2 Capital, and Harmonix Fund. Auransa is a private drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cellanome
providers.description: Cellanome is a life-sciences technology company building multimodal single-cell analysis instrumentation. Its R3200 Platform combines live-cell imaging with single-cell transcriptomics using proprietary CellCage technology to isolate, observe, and perturb individual cells and track their dynamics over time, with applications across neurobiology, immunology, cancer research, aging, and CRISPR screening. Cellanome is venture-backed (8vc, DCVC, General Catalyst, SV Angel, Wing Venture Capital) and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and scientific-resources website but no public developer, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: EpiBiologics
providers.description: EpiBiologics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Mateo, California, developing bispecific antibodies for directed extracellular protein degradation. Its proprietary EpiTAC platform leverages an atlas of 270+ degradation-inducing cell-surface receptors to build tissue-selective therapies that degrade disease-causing proteins while sparing healthy tissue, targeting cancer, autoimmune, and other serious diseases. The company dosed its first patient with EPI-326 (an EGFR-driven solid-tumor bispecific) in a Phase 1 study in April 2026 and closed a $107M Series B round in January 2026. Backed by GV, EpiBiologics was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile; it publishes a corporate website but no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Iambic Therapeutics
providers.description: Iambic Therapeutics is a San Diego, California AI-driven drug discovery company founded in 2019 by Thomas Miller (CEO) and Fred Manby (CTO) that designs small-molecule therapeutics for oncology and other indications. Iambic builds proprietary AI models for drug discovery, including Enchant, a multimodal transformer that predicts clinical properties (pharmacokinetics, cellular and biochemical activity) of candidate molecules from early discovery data, and NeuralPLexer (now NeuralPLexer3), a flow-based generative model for protein-ligand complex structure prediction used to identify cryptic pockets and guide structure-based design. Both lines of work have been published at venues including NeurIPS 2025. The company's internal pipeline is oncology-led: IAM1363, a brain-penetrant selective HER2 / HER2-mutant inhibitor, completed Phase 1/1b dose escalation in 2025 and is in dose optimization with clinical activity reported at ESMO 2025; IAM-K1 (KIF18A) and IAM-C1 (CDK2/4) are preclinical, alongside undisclosed neurology, gastrointestinal, and inflammation discovery programs. In February 2026 Iambic announced a discovery and technology collaboration with Takeda worth up to ~$1.7B plus royalties, following a $100M+ private financing in November 2025 and total disclosed funding of approximately $334M. The company has been named to the CNBC Disruptor 50 list in 2025 and 2026 and has signaled intent to access public markets, including via a SPAC. Iambic's public GitHub footprint is limited to np-bench, a BSD-3 benchmark library for 3D biomolecular structure prediction; the underlying NeuralPLexer and Enchant models are proprietary and there is no public developer API, SDK, or commercial platform offering.

providers.name: Ndata
providers.description: nData (ndata.cz) is a European pharmaceutical software company operating since 2005 that builds GxP-compliant, AI-assisted systems for the pharma lifecycle: portfolio and project management (ePM), regulatory affairs (eRA), quality control planning (eQCP), artwork and packaging management (eAW), controlled documentation (eDOCS), clinical trial documentation / eTMF, plus eLAB (R&D lab operations), and eGO and eTRANSFER (launching Q3/2026). Its public web presence is a marketing and product-catalog site; nData publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specifications. Note: this repo was seeded as a bain-capital-ventures ai-infrastructure portfolio stub, but the ndata.cz surface is a pharmaceutical GxP software vendor — the portfolio match appears to be a mismatch.

providers.name: Red RidgeBio
providers.description: RedRidge Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company that identifies and develops biparatopic antibodies, an antibody class engineered to bind two distinct sites (epitopes) on a single target protein for greater potency and selectivity. Its programs span oncology (antibody-drug conjugates for solid tumors) and autoimmunity (immune-cell modulators), pursued through partnerships and internal discovery. The company operates from Basel, Switzerland with additional presence in Cambridge, Massachusetts and San Francisco. RedRidge Bio was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web presence.

providers.name: Allorion Therapeutics
providers.description: Allorion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2020 by Qiang Ding and Fang Li, developing novel small-molecule therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Operating from Natick, Massachusetts and Guangzhou, China, Allorion applies mutant-selective and isoform-specific medicinal chemistry across a pipeline that includes ARTS-011 (a TYK2 inhibitor), ARTS-021 (a CDK2 inhibitor targeting CCNE1-amplified tumors), and ARTS-023/AVZO-023 partnered with Avenzo Therapeutics, alongside an exclusive option and global license agreement with AstraZeneca for an allosteric EGFR L858R inhibitor. The company is a drug-discovery organization backed by Qiming Venture Partners and INCE Capital; it markets internal data and high-throughput screening platforms but publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco-based biotechnology company founded in 2021 that is pioneering RNA-based gene editing. Its multi-kilobase RNA writing platform is designed to correct thousands of diverse mutations across a patient population with a single product, rather than requiring an independent therapy for each separate mutation. The company positions the approach as safe (minimal off-target effects), reversible, and capable of edits far larger than conventional base or prime editing, targeting previously undruggable genetic disease populations. Amber Bio launched publicly in August 2023 with an oversubscribed $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health. It is a pre-clinical therapeutics company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Avicenna Biosciences
providers.description: Avicenna Biosciences, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina drug development company using machine learning-enhanced medicinal chemistry to accelerate the lead-to-candidate optimization process for small molecule drug development. Founded in 2020 and led by president and CEO Chris Meldrum, the company applies computational screening of candidate molecules for drug-like properties to the "last mile" of small molecule discovery, targeting neurodegenerative disease programs including Rho kinase inhibitors for Parkinson's disease and ALS. Avicenna raised a seed round led by DCVC Bio and has signed research collaborations with partners such as Molecure S.A. The company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable interface as of this enrichment pass; it is catalogued here as an AI-for-drug-discovery company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Bionaut Labs
providers.description: Bionaut Labs is a clinical-stage medical robotics company headquartered in Los Angeles, California, developing "Bionauts" — remote-controlled, magnetically steered microscale robots roughly the size of a grain of rice that travel through tissue to deliver drugs, biologics and nucleic acids directly to targets deep in the brain and central nervous system. Founded in 2016 by CEO Michael Shpigelmacher, the company is pursuing treatments for malignant glioma, Dandy-Walker syndrome, Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease, and has raised more than $80 million from investors including Khosla Ventures. Its product is a therapeutic device and navigation platform regulated as a medical device, not software sold to developers: Bionaut Labs operates no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Celgene
providers.description: Celgene Corporation was a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of innovative therapies for cancer and immune-inflammatory diseases. Celgene was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) in November 2019 and its operations are now consolidated under BMS. No public developer API has been identified; engagement is organized through BMS clinical trials, study connect, and investigator-sponsored research portals.

providers.name: Chiral Quest
providers.description: Chiral Quest (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (凯瑞斯德生化（苏州）有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CDMO specializing in chiral chemistry. The company operates asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation, enzyme-catalyzed biosynthesis, flow chemistry, and process innovation technology platforms, using proprietary catalysts to develop and manufacture chiral drug molecules, key raw materials, regulatory starting materials (RSMs), and advanced GMP intermediates for global pharmaceutical companies. Founded around its asymmetric hydrogenation catalyst technology, Chiral Quest merged with Jiangxi Longlai in 2012 and with Suzhou Pengxu in 2020; the group employs more than 800 people including a research team of roughly 150. Suzhou is the parent company and R&D center, Jiangxi Longlai is the manufacturing base, and the company maintains offices in the United Kingdom and the United States. Chiral Quest is a brochure-site company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable data surface.

providers.name: Cirius Therapeutics
providers.description: Cirius Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage pharmaceutical company based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, developing oral therapies for chronic metabolic diseases driven by insulin resistance, including Type 2 Diabetes, Type 1 Diabetes, obesity and gestational diabetes. Its lead candidate, azemiglitazone (CIR-0602K / MSDC-0602K), is a next-generation insulin sensitizer that inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) to re-balance mitochondrial metabolism, improve glycemic control, preserve lean muscle mass and shift visceral fat to subcutaneous and brown adipose tissue, including in combination with GLP-1 receptor agonists such as tirzepatide. The company publishes a corporate marketing website only; it operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: CivaTech Oncology
providers.description: CivaTech Oncology is a Durham, North Carolina medical device manufacturer that develops polymer-encapsulated low dose rate (LDR) brachytherapy radiation sources for the treatment of solid tumors. Its FDA-cleared product line includes CivaSheet, a flexible, bioabsorbable, unidirectional planar source that can be custom-sized in the operating room and shields healthy tissue; CivaString, a polymer-encapsulated brachytherapy seed used for prostate and other localized cancers; and CivaDerm for dermatological applications. The company markets to radiation oncologists and surgical teams across pancreatic, sarcoma, colorectal, gynecologic, head and neck, lung and prostate indications, and its research has been supported by NIH/NCI and SBIR programs. It publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Denali Therapeutics
providers.description: Denali Therapeutics is a South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and delivers therapeutics for people living with serious neurodegenerative and lysosomal storage diseases. Its proprietary Transport Vehicle (TV) platform is engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier so that large-molecule therapies can reach the brain and body. Denali maintains a public GitHub organization publishing open-source computational-biology and cheminformatics research tools (archs4, basechem, napari-mito-hcs), but publishes no public developer API. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Exscientia
providers.description: Exscientia was an Oxford UK-based AI-driven precision medicine and drug design company, founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Dundee. Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

providers.name: IQVIA
providers.description: IQVIA empowers life sciences organizations to accelerate innovation, improve patient outcomes, and bring treatments to market faster through advanced analytics and technology. IQVIA is a Fortune 500 company offering data, analytics, clinical research, and connected intelligence services.

providers.name: Liberate Bio
providers.description: Liberate Bio is a genetic medicine company developing in vivo cell therapies that reach cell populations beyond the liver, the long-standing limit of lipid nanoparticle delivery. Its RAPTOR discovery platform is a scalable in vivo screening system that identifies LNP delivery vehicles which work with existing biology to carry genetic payloads into immune cells in blood, bone marrow, and the spleen. Liberate Bio applies that delivery capability to in vivo CAR-M (chimeric antigen receptor macrophage) programs, reprogramming monocytes and macrophages to eliminate disease-driving cells without ex vivo manipulation, with programs in hematologic oncology and in autoimmune disease via depletion of pathogenic B-cell populations. Founded by Nessan Bermingham, Theresa M. Reineke, and Michael Mitchell, and led by CEO Shawn Davis and CSO Walter Strapps, the company raised $31M from Khosla Ventures in October 2025. It is pre-clinical and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Novartis
providers.description: Novartis AG is a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical corporation headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, and one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world by revenue. The company focuses on innovative medicines across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic disease areas. Novartis does not publish a public external developer API. The company does maintain an Open Source Science programme that releases scientific computing libraries, Drupal modules, and informatics tooling on GitHub for use by the research community.

providers.name: Novo Nordisk
providers.description: Novo Nordisk A/S is a Danish multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Bagsværd, Denmark, and the world leader in diabetes care. The company also develops treatments for obesity, rare blood disorders, and growth-hormone therapy, including its widely known GLP-1 medicines Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus. Novo Nordisk does not publish a public commercial developer API. The company maintains a research GitHub organization (novonordisk-research) that releases open-source scientific computing libraries and an SDK for the Waters Empower Web API (OptiHPLCHandler) used in pharmaceutical analytical chemistry workflows.

providers.name: Quanta Therapeutics
providers.description: Quanta Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018 and headquartered at 2 Tower Place in South San Francisco, California, with a second site in Radnor, Pennsylvania. It develops oral allosteric small-molecule medicines for RAS-driven cancers by targeting the protein-protein interactions that drive oncogenic RAS signaling, an approach the company describes as conformational blockade of RAS. Its discovery engine is a proprietary high-throughput Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) optical platform that detects subtle protein conformational changes and so surfaces allosteric modulators of signaling complexes that conventional binding assays miss. The clinical pipeline is a set of direct multi-KRAS inhibitors: QTX3034, a G12D-preferring oral multi-KRAS inhibitor in Phase 1 as monotherapy and in combination with cetuximab in KRAS G12D-mutant solid tumors; QTX3544, a G12V-preferring multi-KRAS inhibitor cleared for IND in January 2025; and QTX3046, which dosed its first patient in a Phase 1/1b trial in June 2024. Indications span pancreatic, colorectal, lung and endometrial cancers. The company announced a $60 million Series C in October 2021 and a Series D of over $50 million in May 2023 led by Avidity Partners alongside Sofinnova Investments, Vida Ventures, Surveyor Capital, Longitude Capital and AbbVie Ventures. Quanta Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no public API. Its corporate site is a single static HTML document served from Apache with anchor-based sections; probes for OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path returned HTTP 404, and no api./developer./docs. subdomain resolves.

providers.name: Quintiles Transnational Holdings
providers.description: Quintiles Transnational Holdings was a Fortune 500 contract research organization (CRO) that provided biopharmaceutical development and commercial outsourcing services to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. In October 2016, Quintiles merged with IMS Health to form IQVIA, a leading provider of advanced analytics, technology solutions, and contract research services to the life sciences industry. The legacy Quintiles entity no longer operates as an independent company and does not maintain a public API program; all developer-facing capabilities are now part of IQVIA.

providers.name: Relay Therapeutics
providers.description: Relay Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage precision medicines company (NASDAQ: RLAY) using protein motion to drug historically intractable oncology and genetic-disease targets. Its Dynamo platform combines full-length protein engineering, cryo-EM, ambient-temperature X-ray crystallography, long-timescale molecular dynamics, machine learning, virtual screening, activity- and ligand-based screening, and an ML-powered DNA-encoded library (REL-DEL) to design molecules against conformational states that static structures miss. The clinical pipeline is led by zovegalisib (RLY-2608), described as the first allosteric, pan-mutant, isoform-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor, in Phase 3 for HR+/HER2- breast cancer and Phase 1/2 for vascular anomalies and PROS; RLY-8161, an NRAS- selective inhibitor, is in Phase 1/2 for NRAS-mutant solid tumors; an alpha-galactosidase A non-inhibitory chaperone for Fabry disease is in discovery; lirafugratinib (RLY-4008, FGFR2) was out-licensed to Elevar Therapeutics in December 2024. Relay has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the Dynamo platform is proprietary internal R&D tooling, and the company's GitHub organization currently has no public repositories. The commercial surface is therapeutic candidates, clinical partnerships, and out-licensing rather than data products.

providers.name: Scorpion Therapeutics
providers.description: Scorpion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision oncology biotechnology company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It pursued what it called Precision Oncology 2.0 — integrating target discovery, medicinal chemistry and translational medicine to produce mutant-selective small-molecule cancer drugs — led by STX-478, an oral mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor in Phase 1/2 trials for breast cancer and other advanced solid tumors, and STX-721, a covalent EGFR/HER2 exon 20 inhibitor. In January 2025 Eli Lilly agreed to acquire Scorpion and its PI3K-alpha program in a transaction valued at up to $2.5 billion, with the non-PI3K-alpha pipeline and staff spun into a separate independent company. Scorpion is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and its own domain now redirects to the acquirer's announcement.

providers.name: Smart Diagnostics Systems
providers.description: Smart Diagnostics Systems (SDS) is a food-safety diagnostics company based in Columbia, Missouri, founded in 2016 and backed by Techstars. SDS builds the PathoMeter, a state-of-the-art rapid diagnostic system for the detection of foodborne pathogens such as E. coli, Listeria, and Salmonella, helping food processors and companies protect consumers from foodborne illness. The company operates as a hardware and laboratory diagnostics business; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company for API-surface discovery and is re-evaluated on each enrichment run.

providers.name: uncommonbio
providers.description: Uncommon (uncommonbio.co, formerly Higher Steaks) is a Cambridge, UK biotechnology company backed by Balderton Capital. The company sold its cultivated meat platform to Vow and has pivoted to launch SymphoRNA, a new venture developing nucleic acid delivery technology for multi-RNA combination medicines that target complex diseases such as fibrosis, heart failure, and neurodegeneration. As a life-sciences research and platform company, Uncommon publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Balderton Capital and enriched via the local enrichment pipeline, which confirmed the absence of an API surface while capturing live domain-security posture.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: 1yongcloud
providers.description: Beijing Yiyong Technology Co., Ltd. (北京壹永科技有限公司 / 1yongcloud), founded in October 2017, is a Chinese oncology big-data and artificial-intelligence company. It builds medical-data collection, quality-control and governance capabilities and healthcare information products for hospitals and government health programs. Its product lines include a tumor diagnosis-and-treatment standardization and cost-rationalization platform, a hospital cancer opportunistic-screening platform, an integrated clinical-research platform, and a smart-hospital comprehensive operations decision platform. The company is backed by investors including Qiming Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital China, and Cathay Capital. It operates no public developer portal, API, or SDK; this profile tracks 1yongcloud as a company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AbCellera
providers.description: AbCellera (NASDAQ: ABCL) is a Vancouver-based antibody discovery and development company that integrates biology, computation, and engineering to develop antibody-based medicines. Its technology platform combines high-throughput single-cell antibody screening, GPCR and ion-channel capabilities, bispecifics, antibody-drug conjugates, structure-based design, and AI for sequence and structure analysis. The company operates a hybrid business model with a co-development partner network (40+ partners and 100+ antibody drug programs since 2015) alongside a growing wholly-owned pipeline that includes ABCL635 (non-hormonal vasomotor symptoms), ABCL575 (atopic dermatitis), ABCL688 (autoimmunity), and ABCL386 (oncology), plus 20+ discovery programs. AbCellera does not publish a public API or developer portal; capabilities are delivered through partner collaborations and contract terms.

providers.name: Again
providers.description: Again is a Copenhagen-based carbon-utilization biotech spun out of research from the Danish Technical University, Stanford, and MIT. Rather than storing captured carbon, Again feeds industrial CO2 waste and hydrogen into bioreactors where AI-designed biocatalysts ferment the gas — much like brewing — into commercial-grade acetate and other green chemicals used in adhesives, solvents, plastics, textiles, cosmetics, aromas and flavors, industrial enzymes, proteins, and fertilizers. The company runs carbon-utilization facilities in Copenhagen (CPH-1), Texas City (TXS-1, with Dow and HELM AG), and Porsgrunn, Norway (NOR-1). Again raised a $43M Series A co-led by GV (Google Ventures) and HV Capital in 2024. No public developer API surface was found during API Evangelist enrichment.

providers.name: Akston Biosciences
providers.description: Akston Biosciences Corporation is a privately held biotechnology company headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts, founded in 2011 by the team from SmartCells, Inc. and led by CEO Todd Zion, Ph.D. Akston designs, develops and manufactures protein therapeutics built on its proprietary Ambifect Fc-fusion protein platform, with a pipeline focused on companion-animal (veterinary) medicine: PD-L1 monoclonal antibody oncology candidates (AKS-701d, AKS-619d), a long-acting GLP-1 for feline weight management (AKS-562c), an IL-31 targeting therapy for canine pruritus (AKS-699), and NGF-targeting candidates for osteoarthritis pain. Its veterinary insulin program was sold to Dechra in 2024, and human programs continue through the Vakston and Diamune Therapeutics subsidiaries. The company announced a manufacturing expansion in Shreveport, Louisiana. Akston is a therapeutics developer and manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Antiva Biosciences
providers.description: Antiva Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing topical therapeutics that target oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and the precancerous cervical lesions they cause, aiming to stop cervical cancer before it starts with at-home, non-surgical treatment. Its lead candidate, ABI-2280, is a topical antiviral in Phase 1b/2 clinical development for high-risk cervical HPV infection, and the company frames its work in support of the World Health Organization's global Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative. Antiva is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and GV, and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Ark Biopharmaceutical
providers.description: Ark Biopharmaceutical (爱科百发, Ark Biosciences) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of innovative therapies for respiratory diseases and pediatric conditions. Its pipeline includes AK0529 (ziresovir) for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, AK0901 for ADHD, AK3280 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, AK0610 for RSV prevention, and AK0705 for COPD. The company is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As a drug-development company it publishes a corporate website, R&D pipeline, and news center, but exposes no public developer platform, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Atlas Discovery
providers.description: Atlas Discovery is an AI-powered biotechnology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building foundation models of human patient biology to predict how people will respond to drugs in clinical trials. Nine of ten drugs fail in trials because no animal model or cell in a dish reliably predicts a human response; Atlas Discovery trains models on preclinical and clinical data to improve trial design and rescue stalled drug programs. Its research spans single-cell representation learning (ExpressionVAE) and clinical response prediction, with work presented at ICLR '26, ICML '26, and CSHL '26. The company is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer program, or product surface yet; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting a public developer offering.

providers.name: Atomwise
providers.description: Atomwise pioneered the use of deep convolutional neural networks for structure-based drug discovery, with its AtomNet platform applying AI to virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets. The company ran the Artificial Intelligence Molecular Screen (AIMS) academic collaboration program, partnered with biotech and pharma companies on discovery contracts, and built an internal pipeline of small-molecule programs. As of 2026, atomwise.com redirects to Numerion Labs (numerionlabs.ai), reflecting an apparent rebrand or successor entity that positions itself as an AI superplatform exploring drug-like chemical space with programs in immune and inflammatory diseases. Atomwise never exposed a public commercial API; AtomNet screening was delivered to partners as a service. The legacy GitHub organization (github.com/atomwise) hosts no public repositories.

providers.name: Be Biopharma
providers.description: Be Biopharma (Be Bio) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in October 2020 by Longwood Fund together with B cell engineering researchers David Rawlings, M.D. and Richard James, Ph.D. of Seattle Children's Research Institute. The company develops engineered B Cell Medicines (BCMs) — a patient's own B cells engineered to produce a therapeutic protein — for genetic disease, cancer and other serious conditions. Its lead candidate, BE-101, inserted a functional Factor IX gene into primary human B cells for hemophilia B and held FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations; a second program, BE-102, targeted hypophosphatasia. The company raised $82M in October 2024 and $92M in a January 2025 Series C, dosed the first participant in the Phase 1/2 BeCoMe-9 trial in July 2025, and terminated that trial in June 2026 for stated strategic business reasons. Be Biopharma is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it has never published a developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: DeepCell
providers.description: Deepcell is a Menlo Park, California life-sciences company building an AI-powered platform for label-free single-cell morphology analysis, a field it calls morpholomics. Its REM-I platform combines label-free imaging, deep learning, and gentle cell enrichment to treat single-cell morphology as a high-dimensional, quantitative biological readout without destructive sample preparation. Applications span oncology and tumor heterogeneity profiling, phenotypic drug discovery, cell and gene therapy quality control and manufacturing, regenerative medicine, transplant monitoring, neurobiology, and agriculture. Backed by a16z and DCVC, Deepcell was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it currently publishes a corporate site, blog, and publications but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Dizal Pharma
providers.description: Dizal Pharma (Dizal (Jiangsu) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing novel medicines in oncology and immunology. Originating in 2017 from research capabilities established in China, the company operates research and development across Shanghai and Wuxi (Jiangsu), China, and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market (ticker 688192). Dizal's most advanced programs include sunvozertinib (DZD9008), an oral EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor for non-small cell lung cancer marketed as Zegfrovy, and golidocitinib (DZD4205), a selective JAK1 inhibitor developed for relapsed/refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma. Dizal Pharma was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). As a pharmaceutical developer it publishes a corporate marketing and investor-facing website but does not expose a public developer platform, API program, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile captures the company identity for the network.

providers.name: Elektrofi
providers.description: Elektrofi is a Boston-based biopharmaceutical formulation technology company reinventing how biologic therapies are delivered to patients. Its Hypercon ultra-high-concentration microparticle platform and Elektroject process turn monoclonal antibodies, therapeutic proteins, and other large-molecule drugs into stable, syringe-injectable formulations suited to small-volume, at-home subcutaneous self-administration instead of intravenous infusion. The company has partnered with Eli Lilly and Janssen Biotech (Johnson & Johnson) on multi-target drug-delivery collaborations, and was acquired by Halozyme Therapeutics in November 2025. Elektrofi is a biotechnology company and does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company entity within the network.

providers.name: Gate Bioscience
providers.description: Gate Bioscience is a preclinical biotechnology company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Brisbane, California, creating a new class of small-molecule medicines called Molecular Gates. Molecular Gates selectively eliminate disease-causing extracellular proteins at their origin inside the cell by binding the secretory translocon, the channel through which proteins exit the cell, so targeted proteins are degraded rather than secreted. The company's proprietary Molecular Gate Discovery Platform pairs a privileged library of molecules with bespoke secretion-focused assays and deep secretory-pathway biology to pursue more than 1,000 diseases linked to extracellular proteins. Gate Bioscience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, GV, Versant Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Forbion and Eli Lilly, and has raised roughly $134M across Series A and an oversubscribed $65M Series B. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is an API Evangelist network company record maintained for the portfolio graph.

providers.name: Hexagon Bio
providers.description: Hexagon Bio is a Menlo Park, California biotechnology company developing novel payloads for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in oncology. The company designs next-generation ADC payloads intended to overcome resistance to current payloads and to expand the range of cancer indications ADCs can treat. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Hexagon Bio operates a therapeutics pipeline and research platform rather than a public developer program: it publishes no API, SDK, or developer documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched from Hexagon Bio's own public website (company, pipeline, science/platform, and news pages).

providers.name: M20 Genomics
providers.description: M20 Genomics is a life-science technology company advancing single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. Its VITA platform delivers single-cell full-length transcriptome sequencing across sample types and species, supported by the VITAcruizer single-cell partitioning system, VITApilote library-preparation kits, and VITAseer bioinformatics software. The company's M20 Seq and M20 Spatial technologies serve basic research (cancer, neurobiology, immunology, developmental biology), clinical research (oncology, reproductive medicine, infectious diseases), and drug development and target screening, including prokaryotic and eukaryotic single-cell RNA sequencing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes lab instruments, reagent kits, and analysis software rather than a public web API or developer platform.

providers.name: Medra
providers.description: Medra builds an AI-powered robotic platform for autonomous laboratory work in the life sciences. Its "Physical AI Scientist" combines robotic hardware, computer vision, and scientific reasoning AI to design, execute, and continuously optimize experiments — gene editing, RNA/nucleic-acid work, antibody design, and cell-based assays — the way a human scientist would. Units are deployed at partner sites including Genentech and Addition Therapeutics, with a DARPA collaboration on its AI Experimentalist reasoning layer. Founded by Michelle Lee and headquartered in San Francisco, Medra raised a $52M Series A (Dec 2025) from investors including Lux Capital and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Medra publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Monsanto
providers.description: Monsanto was a global agricultural products company that produced seeds, biotechnology trait products, and herbicides before being acquired by Bayer AG in 2018. Operations and brands have since been integrated into the Bayer Crop Science division.

providers.name: Monte Rosa Therapeutics *
providers.description: Monte Rosa Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering molecular glue degrader (MGD) medicines. It pairs its QuEEN discovery engine — integrating artificial intelligence, machine learning, and structural biology — with proprietary chemistry to design small molecules that selectively degrade disease-causing proteins previously considered undruggable, across oncology and immunology, with collaborations including Novartis and Roche. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile captures its web presence and probed domain-security surface.

providers.name: OMass Therapeutics
providers.description: OMass Therapeutics is an Oxford, UK biotechnology company developing medicines for immunological and rare diseases. It harnesses proprietary biochemistry, native mass spectrometry and custom chemistry through its OdyssION drug discovery platform to interrogate drug targets and how they interact with their native biological ecosystem, separate from the confounding complexity of the cell. The company operates a corporate and scientific web presence (science, pipeline, publications, news and blog) and, as a therapeutics company, publishes no public developer or API surface. Backed by GV and other life-sciences investors.

providers.name: Ouro Medicines
providers.description: Ouro Medicines is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, defining the future of treatment for people with immune-mediated diseases. Its pipeline centers on T cell engager programs for autoimmune conditions, including the lead candidate OM336 (evaluated in the AIC-1001 clinical trial), alongside an expanded access policy. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As a therapeutics developer, Ouro Medicines publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface. Recent company news includes a definitive agreement for Gilead Sciences to acquire Ouro Medicines to advance its first-in-class T cell engager program for autoimmune diseases.

providers.name: Presidio Medical
providers.description: Presidio Medical is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2017 by Kenneth Wu and led by CEO and Chairman Michael Onuscheck. It is developing an implantable Ultra Low Frequency (ULF) neuromodulation platform intended to treat diseases of undesired neural activity, with a first indication in chronic nociceptive low back pain. The therapy delivers ultra low frequency current through an epidural spinal cord stimulation (SCS) lead to reversibly inhibit pain-signaling neurons via sodium channel inactivation, positioned as a non-opioid alternative to conventional SCS. The company raised a $72M Series C in 2023 led by Deerfield Management with Invus Opportunities, Action Potential Venture Capital and ShangBay Capital, and received FDA IDE approval for the global pivotal FULFILL randomized controlled trial in the United States and Australia. Presidio Medical sells an implantable medical device, not software; it has never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract. As of 2026-08-05 its corporate WordPress site at presidiomedical.com is offline, returning a WP Engine "Site Not Configured" HTTP 404 on every path including the root.

providers.name: Radical Numerics
providers.description: Radical Numerics is an AI research lab building what it calls "general biological intelligence" — next-generation AI architectures aimed at biology and science rather than language. It was founded by machine-learning researchers Michael Poli, Stefano Massaroli, Eric Nguyen, and Armin W. Thomas (associated with the Hyena and Evo / Evo 2 genomics model families), with an advisory board including Eric Horvitz, Chris Ré, George Church, and Andrew Weber. The lab focuses on the science of scaling, architecture, and systems: massive context windows scaling toward one billion tokens, generative genomics, biological threat detection, and multimodal biological intelligence. Its first product, Omnii, is an early-access health research preview. The company announced a $50M seed round in June 2026, with backing including Obvious Ventures. As of this profile Radical Numerics publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Relay Therapeutics
providers.description: Relay Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision-medicine company in Cambridge, Massachusetts that discovers and develops small-molecule therapeutics for cancer and genetic disease. Its proprietary Dynamo platform combines computational and experimental approaches — motion-based drug discovery, protein-motion simulation, structural biology, and biophysics — to drug targets that have historically been difficult to reach. The company advances a pipeline of oncology and precision-medicine candidates. Relay Therapeutics was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biotechnology / drug-discovery company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web properties.

providers.name: Rome Therapeutics
providers.description: Rome Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing therapies that target the "repeatome" — the vast repetitive, non-coding regions of the human genome (the "dark genome," including LINE-1 and other transposable elements) implicated in cancer and autoimmune disease. Its discovery engine pairs ROMEMap, a proprietary high-resolution database of annotated functional repeats, with ROMEQuant, a machine-learning method for quantifying repeat expression and prioritizing targets and biomarkers. Backed by a16z and GV, the company raised a $77M Series B (2021) plus a $72M Series B extension to advance its lead program into clinical development. These are internal research/data-science tools; the company publishes no public developer or web API. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Somite
providers.description: Somite (now operating as Cellular Intelligence) is an AI-native TechBio company backed by Khosla Ventures building a universal virtual cell-signaling foundation model to engineer cellular fate. In 2026 the company rebranded from Somite to Cellular Intelligence and entered an agreement with Novo Nordisk to advance STEM-PD, a clinical-stage cell therapy for Parkinson's disease that carries FDA Fast Track Designation. The company works at the intersection of machine learning and regenerative medicine and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Trishula Therapeutics
providers.description: Trishula Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing cancer immunotherapies that target immune-evasion mechanisms in the tumor microenvironment. Its lead candidate, TTX-030, is a first-in-class monoclonal antibody that inhibits CD39, an enzyme in the adenosine pathway that tumors exploit to suppress anti-tumor immunity; TTX-030 has advanced into Phase 2 clinical trials, including studies in metastatic pancreatic cancer. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a therapeutics company with a corporate web presence and no public API, developer, or software product surface.

providers.name: Ventus Therapeutics
providers.description: Ventus Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on small-molecule drug discovery for biologically validated targets historically considered undruggable, across inflammatory, immunological, cardiometabolic, and neurological diseases. Its ReSOLVE platform combines AI/ML, protein science, structural biology, and biophysics to accelerate discovery; the pipeline includes VENT-03 (cGAS inhibitor), VENT-02 (NLRP3 inhibitor), and VENT-04 (caspase-4/5 inhibitor). Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts with a site in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, and backed by GV and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company operates no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Virtuoso Therapeutics
providers.description: Virtuoso Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company advancing a pipeline of novel bispecific antibodies to treat cancer. Using a differentiated approach to antibody engineering, the company designs molecules intended to overcome the limitations of existing therapies and to address major hurdles facing emerging classes of oncology treatments. Virtuoso is a venture-backed portfolio company of Canaan Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Soley Therapeutics
providers.description: Soley Therapeutics is a science-first, tech-enabled drug discovery and development company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, using human cells as biological sensors to uncover first-in-class medicines. Its cell stress sensing platform captures time-resolved cellular responses across thousands of features and applies computer vision and machine learning to compress them into compact signatures, screening hundreds of thousands of compounds per week on proprietary automation and robotics. The company is advancing a lead oncology asset for acute myeloid leukemia toward an IND filing, a second oncology asset for solid tumors in IND-enabling studies, and non-oncology stress-reducing candidates for neurodegenerative and metabolic disease. Soley raised a $200M Series C in January 2026, bringing total funding to roughly $290M. The platform is an internal discovery engine: Soley is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Revvity
providers.description: Revvity is a life sciences and diagnostics company providing instruments, software, reagents, and services to support drug discovery, development, diagnostics, and applied research. Formed from the former life sciences and diagnostics businesses of PerkinElmer, Revvity serves pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical, academic, and applied markets with offerings spanning reproductive health screening, omics, imaging, and laboratory automation.

providers.name: abbisko
providers.description: Abbisko Therapeutics (上海和誉生物医药科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of innovative small-molecule therapeutics, primarily in oncology. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or agent surface — this is a biopharmaceutical R&D company, not an API provider — so no API artifacts apply; only a live domain-security probe was captured.

providers.name: Acceleron
providers.description: Acceleron is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: aceabio
