providers.description: ACEA Biosciences (aceabio) is a life-sciences company known for cell-analysis instrumentation that was acquired by Agilent Technologies; its aceabio.com.cn domain now redirects to an Agilent landing page (explore.agilent.com/ACEA-joins-Agilent). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture firm and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or public API surface for the standalone entity — the operating web presence has been folded into Agilent.

providers.name: aceatherapeutics
providers.description: ACEA Therapeutics (aceatherapeutics.com) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative small-molecule and antibody-drug-conjugate treatments across oncology, autoimmune, and antiviral therapeutic areas, with product candidates including Olgotrelvir, Abivertinib, AC0058, STI-6129, and AC0939. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company oriented toward patients, physicians, and investors, ACEA Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time; this profile captures its verifiable web/domain footprint only.

providers.name: Achira
providers.description: Achira is a digital-biology company building molecular world models to transform drug discovery and the physical sciences. Founded by John Chodera, Theofanis Karaletsos, and Zavain Dar, it blends geometric deep learning, generative AI, physics, quantum chemistry, and statistical mechanics into foundation simulation models that enable out-of-distribution prediction at the atomistic scale — a "third path" between pure machine-learning approaches and traditional molecular dynamics simulation. Achira raised a $33M Series A from Dimension, Amplify Partners, NVIDIA NVentures, and Compound. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: acxel
providers.description: ACXEL is a digital cell biology company building advanced microfluidics platforms and productivity tools for life sciences research and drug development. Its self-developed AP-LOC (Active Pixel Lab-on-Chip) technology enables high-throughput, parallel, and precise microdroplet manipulation, alongside AM-EWOD and AM-DMF digital microfluidic platforms supporting cell sorting, cell therapy, antibody therapy, synthetic biology, and chemical synthesis with full-process chip integration and real-time feedback monitoring. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. ACXEL is a hardware and platform provider and publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: aistarfish
providers.description: aistarfish (aistarfish.com) is the web home of Haixin Health (海心健康), a Chinese digital-health company operated by Zhejiang Haixin Zhihui Technology Co., Ltd. that provides full-course disease management and support services for cancer patients across their entire treatment journey. Its consumer-facing products are iOS and Android mobile apps built around a patient community, peer-support networks, patient and official medical diaries, and patient-to-doctor connections, under the mission of "helping cancer patients live longer and live better." The company holds an Internet Pharmaceutical Information Service qualification. It is surfaced here as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture network. As of this pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Allena Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Allena Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: AMPLY Discovery
providers.description: AMPLY Discovery is a UK (Belfast, Northern Ireland) biotechnology company turning the roughly 98% of the genome largely ignored by drug developers — the "dark genome" — into a pipeline of first-in-class therapeutics. The company pairs six AI/computational discovery engines with two wet labs in a closed loop between silicon and bench to find novel antimicrobial and therapeutic candidates targeting drug-resistant pathogens and complex diseases. AMPLY is a Techstars portfolio company and has been backed by Innovate UK, Invest NI, QUBIS and other UK/NI innovation programmes. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; AMPLY Discovery publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Arda Therapeutics
providers.description: Arda Therapeutics is a San Carlos, California biotech company founded in 2021 that develops targeted cell depletion therapies for chronic disease. Rather than modulating the proteins that pathogenic cells produce, Arda uses a single-cell sequencing and computational discovery engine to map disease-specific cell states, identify surface markers on harmful cells, and design targeted biologics that selectively deplete them across fibrotic, autoimmune, and metabolic conditions. Backed by a $43M Series A led by a16z Bio + Health with GV, Two Sigma Ventures, Eli Lilly and others. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and web surface; Arda currently publishes a corporate marketing site with no public developer API.

providers.name: Areteia Therapeutics
providers.description: Areteia Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, operating in the life-sciences sector. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company is no longer operating: areteiatx.com serves only a closure notice directing asset and general inquiries to contact addresses, and the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other technical developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; retained for network completeness with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Aria Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Aria Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to drug discovery, using a computational platform to identify and advance small-molecule therapeutic candidates for complex, inflammatory, and immunological diseases. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Aria operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; an enrichment pass found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other programmatic developer surface for the company at this time.

providers.name: Arpelos Biosciences
providers.description: Arpelos Biosciences is a seed-stage biotechnology company based in Kendall Square, Cambridge, developing multivalent medicines — therapeutics engineered for high potency and selectivity by engaging multiple targets or sites simultaneously. The founding team comprises scientists from UCSF, Penn, Stanford, and MIT spanning computational biology, immunology, and protein engineering, and the company is backed by prominent biotech investors including Wing Venture Capital. Arpelos currently operates as a stealth-stage research company with a single-page web presence and does not publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: ArriVent Biopharma
providers.description: ArriVent BioPharma (NASDAQ: AVBP) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the identification, development, and commercialization of differentiated medicines for the treatment of cancer. Its lead candidate is firmonertinib, an EGFR inhibitor being studied across non-small cell lung cancer indications, and its pipeline includes next-generation antibody drug conjugates such as ARR-002. The company operates by identifying novel oncology programs, in-licensing drug candidates through partnerships, and designing regulatory-compliant clinical development strategies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of HongShan and added to the API Evangelist network; as a traditional pharmaceutical developer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: ArsenalBio
providers.description: ArsenalBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco developing programmable, integrated cell therapies for solid tumors. Its platform engineers autonomous CAR-T cells using large-scale genome engineering and computational biology to create multi-functional therapies. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates in the healthcare and biotechnology sector. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: atantares
providers.description: Atantares (芯宿科技) is a Chinese synthetic-biology company based in Suzhou Industrial Park that builds "silicon-based biology" — semiconductor-driven biotechnology. Its chip-based, high-throughput platform (the EcoSyn synthesizer and ECHOS MicroArray, using electrochemical oligonucleotide synthesis on CMOS/MEMS microelectrode arrays) drives low-cost, high-fidelity DNA synthesis and is expanding into RNA and protein synthesis and detection. Research-service offerings include primer/oligo synthesis, gene synthesis, gene sequencing, cloning and mutagenesis, strain-library preparation, and gene editing, built on an in-house full-workflow automation, sequence-analysis, and order-management platform. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Atara Bio
providers.description: Atara Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage allogeneic (off-the-shelf) T-cell immunotherapy company developing transformative therapies that harness T cells to fight cancer and autoimmune conditions, and is the first company to receive regulatory approval for an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a corporate website but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found; this profile carries identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Autolus *
providers.description: Autolus is a life-sciences (biopharmaceutical) company operating in the cell-therapy space, developing programmed / engineered T cell (CAR-T) therapies for cancer and other serious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a clinical/commercial-stage biopharma, its public web presence (autolus.com) is a corporate marketing and investor-relations site rather than a developer platform: no public API, developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment. The only machine-discoverable artifact is a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Aviceda Therapeutics
providers.description: Aviceda Therapeutics is a private, late-stage clinical biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts that describes itself as the world leader in glyco-immune checkpoint therapeutics. It develops immune-mediated therapies built on a glyco-mimetic nanoparticle platform that targets the interaction between sialic acids on cell surfaces and Siglec immune receptors in order to modulate aberrant inflammation. Its lead asset, AVD-104, is an intravitreally administered sialic-acid-coated nanoparticle being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 SIGLEC trial for geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration. Aviceda is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Axcelius I/II
providers.description: Axcelius I/II is a biopharmaceutical company-creation vehicle backed by Canaan Partners, formed to found and incubate drug-development companies pursuing treatments for cancer, rare diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. It is led by managing partner Dennis Podlesak and sponsored at Canaan by general partner Brent Ahrens, and operates from San Francisco, California, with an associated holding entity registered in Connecticut at Canaan's Westport office. Rather than operating as a product company, Axcelius assembles management teams and capital around licensed therapeutic assets and spins them out as standalone biopharma companies; Transposon Therapeutics, developing therapies for ALS and Alzheimer's disease, is its best-documented creation. As of this enrichment pass the vehicle remains in stealth mode with no public developer surface -- no product website beyond a holding page, no documentation, developer portal, SDKs, GitHub organization, or API of any kind.

providers.name: bayomics
providers.description: Bayomics (贝普奥生物) is a Shenzhen-based biotechnology company specializing in spatial proteomics and trace (micro) proteomics solutions for pharmaceutical research and drug development. Its product lines include the SISPROT protein sample-preparation kits built on proprietary Spintip centrifuge-pipette technology that process nanogram-level samples in roughly two hours, VistaProX spatial visualization proteomics combining immunofluorescence staining with high-depth mass-spectrometry detection on a single slice, and high-throughput automation systems capable of processing up to 400 proteomics samples per day. Bayomics operates as a B2B reagent supplier and research-services provider and does not currently publish any public developer API, SDKs, or programmatic developer resources. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: BeiGene
providers.description: BeiGene (rebranded as BeOne Medicines in 2025) is a global oncology biopharmaceutical company founded in 2010, developing and commercializing cancer therapies worldwide. Its portfolio spans blood cancers and solid tumors, led by BRUKINSA (zanubrutinib), a BTK inhibitor, alongside programs in protein degradation (CDACs) and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The company is listed on NASDAQ (BGNE), HKEX, and the Shanghai STAR Market, with a global footprint across 30+ countries (beonemedicines.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; no public developer portal, API, or SDK program is currently published.

providers.name: BioOrbit
providers.description: BioOrbit is a London-based in-space manufacturing company, founded in 2023, that uses microgravity to crystallise protein-based biologic drugs at scale. Its autonomous BOX hardware — a compact, microwave-sized manufacturing unit designed to operate in low-Earth orbit — grows highly ordered crystalline forms of therapeutic proteins that reduce viscosity, enabling treatments normally given intravenously (including cancer therapies) to be reformulated as subcutaneous, self-injectable products. Co-founded by Dr Katie King and Dr Leonor Teles, BioOrbit raised the world's largest seed round for in-space manufacturing (~£9.8M / $13.2M) co-led by LocalGlobe and Breega with Seedcamp, Auxxo, Type One, 7percent and angels, and is supported by the UK Space Agency, ESA BIC and ESA BSGN. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: BlackThorn Therapeutics *
providers.description: BlackThorn Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015 and headquartered in South San Francisco, focused on discovering and developing targeted therapeutics for brain diseases and central nervous system (CNS) disorders such as major depressive disorder and schizophrenia, using a precision-medicine platform. It was backed by gv (Google Ventures) and later combined into Neumora Therapeutics, whose corporate site now resolves at neumoratx.com. This is a life-sciences company profile: it operates no public developer API, SDK, or agent surface, so API-oriented artifacts are not applicable beyond a domain-security probe of the corporate host.

providers.name: cansinotech
providers.description: CanSino Biologics (康希诺生物, cansinotech.com.cn / cansinotech.com) is a Tianjin-based Chinese biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 and dual-listed on the Hong Kong and Shanghai (STAR) exchanges. It researches, manufactures, and commercializes human vaccines across five proprietary technology platforms, with a portfolio covering COVID-19, meningococcal, pneumococcal, tuberculosis, Ebola, and DTcP indications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; only its corporate web presence was found.

providers.name: Celltype
providers.description: CellType is an AI-driven drug discovery company building what it calls "The Biological World Model" — foundation models and autonomous agents that simulate human biology to predict drug responses in human systems before clinical trials, reducing reliance on traditional preclinical models such as mice and cell lines. Its core technology, Cell2Sentence (C2S), teaches large language models to understand cellular biology by converting single-cell gene expression data into a text-like format that models can interpret, and the company reports using it to discover and validate a novel cancer treatment signal targeting tumor immunogenicity. A Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, CellType works with large pharmaceutical partners and currently operates as a B2B research and drug-discovery platform rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Centreherbs (Beijing Shengtaier Biotechnology)
providers.description: Centreherbs is the brand of Beijing Shengtaier Biotechnology Co., Ltd., a veterinary pharmaceutical company founded in 1999 and headquartered in the Daxing Biopharmaceutical Industrial Park, Beijing, China. An integrated research, development, production, and distribution organization for animal health, it specializes in veterinary traditional Chinese medicine preparations, animal vaccines for poultry and livestock, plant-based premixed feed additives, and pet health products, backed by four wholly-owned subsidiaries and an internal biotech research institute. It is a healthcare portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cerexa
providers.description: Cerexa was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in the mid-2000s (its cerexa.com domain was registered in March 2005) to develop anti-infective therapies for serious, drug-resistant bacterial infections in the hospital setting. Its lead program was ceftaroline fosamil, a fifth-generation cephalosporin antibiotic active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), in-licensed from Takeda Pharmaceutical Company and carried forward by Forest Laboratories; the compound was approved by the FDA on October 29, 2010 and marketed as Teflaro in the United States and Zinforo in Europe. Cerexa was backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, and its programs ultimately passed through Forest Laboratories into the Actavis/Allergan combination (Forest Laboratories was acquired by Actavis on July 1, 2014) and on to AbbVie. Cerexa no longer operates as an independent company and has no developer surface: it publishes no API, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no documentation, and its historical cerexa.com domain is now registered and operated by AbbVie, 301-redirecting to AbbVie's Allergan page. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chimerix
providers.description: Chimerix, Inc. was a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, focused on developing medicines for serious and life-threatening diseases. It is best known for brincidofovir (TEMBEXA), an antiviral approved by the U.S. FDA in 2021 as a smallpox medical countermeasure, and for dordaviprone (ONC201), an investigational small-molecule therapy for H3 K27M-mutant diffuse glioma, a form of brain cancer. Chimerix was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CMRX) and was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2025, primarily for dordaviprone; the chimerix.com domain now redirects to jazzpharma.com. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Chimerix does not operate a public developer program or API surface — this profile tracks it as a company entity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ChronicleBio
providers.description: ChronicleBio is a biotechnology company working at the intersection of human data and drug discovery, with the stated mission of translating human data into disease-defining medicines. It operates in the healthcare and life-sciences sector and was surfaced through the electric-capital portfolio. As of this profile, ChronicleBio publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer surface: enrichment found no API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or changelog. Domain security was probed live (TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, and a DMARC quarantine policy present; DNSSEC and CAA absent).

providers.name: Clinovas LTD
providers.description: Clinovas LTD (Clinova, clinova.ai) is an AI-powered patient recruitment platform for clinical trials. Per the company's own site, it matches eligible patients to trials in minutes rather than months using AI-powered patient matching against hospital electronic health records (EHR). The solution is hospital-based and HIPAA-compliant, targeting clinical research organizations and trial sponsors operating in emerging markets including Eastern Europe and the CIS region. Backed by 500 Global. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: cn
providers.description: cn is the China-region web presence (cn.ausperbio.com) of AusperBio Therapeutics (Hangzhou Ausper Bio / 杭州浩博医药有限公司), a Phase II clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming HBV treatment toward a functional cure and advancing oligonucleotide therapeutics. AusperBio leverages its proprietary Med-Oligo ASO platform with targeted delivery technologies to apply antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics across viral infections, metabolic conditions, genetic disorders, and immune diseases; its lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO advancing through Phase II/III trials for chronic hepatitis B. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; the company publishes a marketing website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: CSR Biotech
providers.description: CSR Biotech (超视计 / Chaoshiji) is a Chinese life-sciences instrumentation company that develops super-resolution optical microscopy systems for advanced biological research. Its product line includes the HIS-SIM and MI-SIM structured-illumination microscopes and the SIM-Ultimate platform, delivering live-cell imaging down to roughly 60nm resolution across many imaging modes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a scientific-instruments maker, CSR Biotech publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: CTRL Therapeutics
providers.description: CTRL Therapeutics (cTRL Tx) is a Chicago-based preclinical biotechnology company developing next-generation cell therapies for solid tumors. The company harnesses circulating tumor-reactive lymphocytes (cTRLs) - a rare, potent T cell population found in the blood and naturally equipped to fight cancer - to engineer polyclonal cell therapies that avoid invasive tumor-tissue surgery. From a single blood draw, CTRL's proprietary IsoQore cell-sorting platform isolates millions of migratory, tumor-reactive cTRLs via novel markers, aiming to simplify the discovery, manufacturing and administration of solid-tumor cell therapy. CTRL launched in 2023 with a $10M seed financing led by General Catalyst, with participation from Intermountain Health and FACIT. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a corporate website and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: D2G Oncology
providers.description: D2G Oncology is a precision-oncology company based in Mountain View, California, reported to have been founded in 2018 by Ian Winters. Public company descriptions characterize its work as applying quantitative and multiplexed functional cancer genomics to relate drugs to genotypes in order to advance precision cancer therapeutics. The company operates INSITE, a login-gated internal research portal at www.d2g-insite.com supporting preclinical study management and result exploration. D2G Oncology publishes no public developer API program, no developer portal, no API documentation, and no client SDKs, and third-party company trackers list the company as inactive as of 2026. It was surfaced through the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio and is retained here as an identity-only profile.

providers.name: Damae Medical
providers.description: Damae Medical is a Paris-based medical device company developing non-invasive imaging technology for dermatology and skin cancer diagnostics. Its flagship deepLive system is built on proprietary LC-OCT (Line-field Confocal Optical Coherence Tomography), which pairs deep tissue penetration with cellular resolution to produce histology-like vertical and confocal-like horizontal 3D views of the skin in vivo. deepLive received CE Mark Class IIa certification in 2023 and FDA 510(k) clearance in March 2025, and integrates quantitative analysis tools such as 3D surface segmentation, cellular network visualization, melanin distribution mapping, and dermal fiber segmentation. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Danaher
providers.description: Danaher Corporation is a global life sciences and diagnostics conglomerate whose operating companies include Beckman Coulter, Leica Microsystems, Cepheid, SCIEX, IDT, Cytiva, Abcam, Aldevron, Beckman Coulter Diagnostics, Radiometer, and others. Danaher itself does not publish a corporate-level developer API; product and service APIs are provided by individual operating companies under the Danaher portfolio.

providers.name: Data Driven Bioscience
providers.description: Data Driven Bioscience (now operating as Duoseq, a ddb.bio service) is a cancer genomics testing company that performs comprehensive molecular profiling of both DNA and RNA from a single sample in an on-site workflow, delivering results from sample to report in roughly two days. Its platform detects mutations, expression levels, gene fusions, and clonotype information, and integrates directly with Epic and other leading EHR systems so results flow into the patient chart. The company is a portfolio company of initialized-capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes a marketing/clinical website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Decibel Therapeutics *
providers.description: Decibel Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on gene therapies for hearing loss and balance disorders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain, decibeltx.com, 301-redirects to regeneron.com, consistent with the company having been acquired/absorbed by Regeneron; Decibel maintains no independent public developer portal, API, documentation, or other developer surface. This profile is retained as a network lead and carries only infrastructure-level (domain security) probe data.

providers.name: Deep 6 AI
providers.description: Deep 6 AI was a clinical-trial acceleration company that used artificial intelligence and natural language processing to mine structured and unstructured clinical data in electronic health records, matching eligible patients to clinical trials in minutes rather than months. The Techstars-backed precision-research platform was acquired by Tempus AI in early 2024, after which its standalone deep6.ai web presence was retired (the domain no longer serves a site, though its email/DNS records remain active). No public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or package registry entries could be found for Deep 6 AI during enrichment.

providers.name: Epiodyne
providers.description: Epiodyne is a San Francisco-based pharmaceutical company using structure-based drug discovery to develop small-molecule opioid medicines precisely calibrated for minimal side effects and minimal addiction potential. Its pipeline targets pain management and opioid use disorder (OUD), engineering compounds with specifically tuned receptor functions to address the opioid crisis. The company is a venture-backed biotech portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or technology platform.

providers.name: Epizyme
providers.description: Epizyme, Inc. was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing epigenetic therapies for cancer and other diseases. Its lead product, TAZVERIK (tazemetostat), is an oral EZH2 inhibitor approved by the FDA for epithelioid sarcoma and relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma. Epizyme was acquired by Ipsen in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub via the kleiner-perkins venture portfolio; the company operates no public developer program, API, or documentation surface, and its former corporate website (epizyme.com) is no longer serving a web presence though the domain remains registered and mail-active.

providers.name: EQRx
providers.description: EQRx was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Alexis Borisy with a mission to develop and deliver innovative, patent-protected medicines at radically lower prices. The company went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with CM Life Sciences III and built an oncology and immunology pipeline anchored by in-licensed candidates such as aumolertinib and sugemalimab. In 2023 EQRx wound down its drug-development programs and was acquired by Revolution Medicines in an all-stock transaction. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by a16z and GV); it never operated a public developer platform or API, and its web presence is no longer live.

providers.name: Evelo Biosciences *
providers.description: Evelo Biosciences was a Flagship Pioneering-founded, GV-backed microbiome biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing orally delivered investigational medicines acting on the small intestinal axis. Following clinical failures of its lead candidates EDP1815 and EDP2939, the company announced dissolution in November 2023 and has been wound down. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a dissolved life-sciences portfolio record: the evelobio.com domain now serves only a parked catch-all error page and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Everyone Medicines
providers.description: Everyone Medicines is a therapeutics company listed in the Khosla Ventures portfolio under the Therapeutics category, where it is described as "individualized precision therapeutics." The company has no public developer or API surface as of July 2026. Its original web address, everyonemedicines.com, now issues a 301 redirect to www.eomeds.com, a domain registered through GoDaddy on 2024-05-11 that currently resolves to no DNS A record, so the site is dark and no page, documentation, or .well-known document can be retrieved. Probes of the package registries (npm, PyPI), GitHub organizations (everyonemedicines, eomeds), and the .well-known discovery surface all returned nothing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed life-sciences lead; it carries probed domain-security data only and should be re-run once the company publishes a live site.

providers.name: Evonetix
providers.description: Evonetix is a Cambridge, UK deep-technology company developing a benchtop DNA synthesis platform built on semiconductor technology. Its core innovation is a silicon chip carrying thousands of independently thermally-controlled reaction sites, allowing many DNA strands to be synthesised in parallel with per-site temperature control, in-process error detection and correction, and assembly of high-fidelity genes at the desktop. The company's goal is to give synthetic biology, life-science, and drug-discovery researchers accurate, on-demand access to synthetic DNA without relying on centralised outsourced gene foundries. Evonetix was surfaced as a portfolio company of the deep-tech venture firm DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its primary web domain (evonetix.com) resolves to a suspended-account placeholder page.

providers.name: Excision
providers.description: Excision BioTherapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing CRISPR-based in vivo gene-editing therapies aimed at curing serious viral infectious diseases. Its programs apply multiplexed CRISPR editing delivered via AAV vectors to excise viral DNA from the host genome, led by EBT-101, an investigational one-time therapy for HIV. Excision is a therapeutics company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Excision BioTherapeutics
providers.description: Excision BioTherapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing CRISPR-based gene-editing therapies intended to functionally cure serious viral infectious diseases. Its programs use multiplexed CRISPR/Cas approaches delivered via adeno-associated virus (AAV) to excise latent viral DNA from infected cells, with a lead candidate (EBT-101) targeting HIV and additional research directed at herpesviruses and hepatitis B. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile therefore carries company identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Exo Therapeutics
providers.description: Exo Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of crv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Forty Seven *
providers.description: Forty Seven, Inc. was an immuno-oncology biotechnology company founded in 2015 to commercialize CD47 immune-evasion research licensed from Stanford University (Irv Weissman and colleagues). Its lead program was magrolimab, a monoclonal antibody targeting CD47 — the "do not eat me" signal tumor cells use to evade macrophage-mediated killing — studied in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Backed by GV, the company was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2020 for roughly $4.9 billion; the fortyseveninc.com domain now redirects to gilead.com. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Genesis Therapeutics
providers.description: Genesis Therapeutics (Genesis Molecular AI) is an AI-focused biotechnology company building GEMS (Genesis Exploration of Molecular Space), a generative and predictive AI operating system for small-molecule drug discovery. GEMS combines structure-based deep learning, language and diffusion models, and physics-based simulation (molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry) to generate and optimize molecules for complex targets, accelerating hit identification through lead optimization and candidate selection. In 2025 the company introduced Pearl, a next-generation foundation model for drug discovery. Headquartered in Burlingame, California with a laboratory in San Diego, Genesis has raised over $300M and partners with Eli Lilly, Gilead, Genentech, and Incyte while advancing its own therapeutic pipeline. It is not a public API provider: GEMS is a proprietary internal platform with no published developer portal, documentation, or API.

providers.name: Genomics Medicine Ireland
providers.description: Genomics Medicine Ireland (GMI) is a Dublin-based life-sciences company founded in 2015 to build a large-scale Irish genomic and clinical research programme, sequencing volunteer participant DNA and pairing it with longitudinal phenotypic data to study the genetic basis of common and rare diseases such as Alzheimer's, heart failure, inflammatory bowel disease and multiple sclerosis. GMI was absorbed into WuXi NextCODE and subsequently rebranded as Genuity Science (genuitysci.com), a precision-medicine business offering disease-enriched genomic cohorts, whole-genome and next-generation sequencing through a clinically accredited lab, and population-scale data-analysis services to pharmaceutical and biotech partners for target discovery and biomarker identification. As a genomics research and data-services organization it exposes no public developer API, portal, SDKs or OpenAPI; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly derived or probed for it.

providers.name: Georgiamune
providers.description: Georgiamune Inc. is a Gaithersburg, Maryland based biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class immunotherapies that reprogram immune signaling pathways to rebalance the immune system and restore health across cancer and autoimmune diseases. Built on a target-discovery platform, its pipeline of immunomodulators spans clinical, preclinical, and discovery stages, including the clinical-stage dual-functioning antibody GIM-122, the regulatory T-cell (Treg) inhibitor GIM-531, and the Treg activator GIM-407, alongside additional antibody and small-molecule programs. The company was surfaced as a venture-backed portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or programmatic interface.

providers.name: GigaCrop
providers.description: GigaCrop is an agricultural biotechnology company engineering the photosynthesis pathway to dramatically increase crop productivity. Founded by Chris Eiben, PhD, the company combines enzyme engineering and machine learning to optimize the RuBisCo enzyme, aiming to roughly double yields in staple crops such as corn and soy and to break past the limits that have held annual yield gains near one percent for a century. Backed by Playground Global, GigaCrop is working to make agriculture both more sustainable and more abundant.

providers.name: Gritstone Oncology
providers.description: Gritstone Oncology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: life-sciences. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: healthgenetech
providers.description: HealthGeneTech (HGT) is a genomics company focused on gene fragment analysis and the development of applications for genetic testing and diagnostics. It is a healthcare portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The public website healthgenetech.com redirects to www.hgt.cn. As of enrichment, no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification could be located, and the primary web host did not serve content to automated probes; this profile remains a lead awaiting a discoverable API surface.

providers.name: Helix Nano
providers.description: Helix Nano (HelixNano) is a Boston-based biotechnology company developing new ways to manipulate messenger RNA (mRNA) — the molecule that carries instructions from genes to the cell's protein-making machinery. Backed by DCVC since 2017, the company has developed techniques to improve the effectiveness and specificity of mRNA vaccines, including a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine engineered to resist viral mutation. HelixNano is now pursuing a broader vision of self-designing, adaptive therapeutics — drugs that could improve with every patient and, ideally, require only a single dose. The company operates out of 5 Channel Center Street in Boston, Massachusetts, and remains at an early, largely stealth stage with no public developer program or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Humane Genomics
providers.description: Humane Genomics Inc is a New York City biotechnology company engineering oncolytic RNA viruses to selectively target and destroy cancer cells. Using a first-principle, computer-aided design approach built on Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV) with aptazyme-controlled selective replication, the company develops precision viral therapies; its lead candidate targets pediatric liver cancer (hepatoblastoma). Backed by Union Square Ventures, Humane Genomics operates from Alexandria LaunchLabs and partners with Genezen for cGMP manufacturing. The company publishes no public API or developer surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: Hyalex Orthopaedics
providers.description: Hyalex Orthopaedics is a medical device company developing synthetic cartilage technology to repair and restore damaged joint surfaces. Its lead product, the HYALEX Knee System, uses a hydrogel-based material engineered to mimic the properties of natural cartilage and is intended to resurface damaged joints during surgery as an alternative to traditional implants. The company has received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and is conducting clinical studies. Hyalex Orthopaedics is a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. As a physical medical-device manufacturer it does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its verified public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: IconOVir Bio
providers.description: IconOVir Bio is a New York City-based, clinical-stage life sciences company whose stated mission is to cure cancer and restore life to patients. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) as a portfolio company, IconOVir Bio operates in the oncology and cancer immunotherapy space, developing therapeutics aimed at treating patients across a range of cancers. The company maintains a corporate presence at 689 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan and presents a single-page corporate website with no public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio lead; the enrichment pass confirmed there is no public API or developer surface to catalog beyond basic web-domain security posture.

providers.name: Illume Labs
providers.description: Illume Labs is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building a 24/7 AI personal health and longevity companion. Its platform is designed to connect a user's wearables, blood panels, and genomic data, then text them personalized, actionable insights — detecting patterns across data sources, answering health questions conversationally, and offering an interactive surface for deeper exploration of longevity signals. As of mid-2026 the company is pre-launch and operates a single marketing landing page ("A new lens on longevity") on Vercel with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface yet published. This profile remains a network lead pending a public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Immunos Therapeutics
providers.description: Immunos Therapeutics is a privately held biotechnology company focused on harnessing the immune system to treat cancer and inflammatory diseases. The company develops immuno-oncology and immunomodulatory therapeutic candidates, advancing a preclinical and clinical pipeline supported by scientific and clinical advisory boards. Immunos Therapeutics is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a therapeutics/drug-development company it operates in the life sciences rather than as a software API provider, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation at this time. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio discovery.

providers.name: IncreBio
providers.description: IncreBio (formerly JuiceInnov8) is a Thai food-biotech company founded in 2017 that uses biology to create the next generation of healthier food and drinks. Its flagship product, INCREDIBLE Juice, is a 100% juice with roughly 70% less sugar than standard juice, about 30 calories and 5g of fiber per serving, under the tagline "Make Juice and War on Sugar." IncreBio is backed by 500 Global. It is a consumer food-and-beverage brand with no public API, developer platform, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Industrial Microbes
providers.description: Industrial Microbes (iMicrobes) is a synthetic-biology company in Alameda, California that engineers microorganisms to convert renewable, low-carbon feedstocks such as ethanol and methane into commercial-grade industrial chemicals and bio-based materials. Founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Liz Clarke, Derek Greenfield, and Noah Helman, the company has produced 100% bio-based acrylic acid and targets net-zero or negative-emission building-block chemicals for coatings, paints, carbon-fiber precursors, biopolymers, and biodegradable plastics. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Industrial Microbes publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal, so the enrichment pipeline captured only verified company identity and website link properties.

providers.name: Innovent
providers.description: Innovent Biologics (信达生物制药) is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Suzhou Industrial Park, China, that discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes high-quality biologic medicines for the treatment of oncology, autoimmune, cardiovascular and metabolic, and ophthalmology diseases. Its portfolio includes the PD-1 inhibitor Tyvyt (sintilimab), developed in partnership with Eli Lilly, alongside a broad pipeline of monoclonal antibodies and other biologics. Innovent is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (01801.HK) and was surfaced through the Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) portfolio. Innovent is a therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile captures its corporate and domain-security identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Invetx *
providers.description: Invetx was a Boston-based veterinary biotechnology company developing protein-based therapeutics — species-specific, half-life-extended monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) — for chronic conditions in companion animals (dogs and cats). Its integrated platform spanned antibody discovery, optimization, Fc-variant half-life extension, development and manufacturing, with lead program IVX-01. Backed by GV, F-Prime Capital, Novo Holdings, Eight Roads, Anterra Capital, Casdin Capital and Tekla, Invetx was acquired by Dechra Pharmaceuticals in July 2024 for up to $520M. It exposes no public API, developer, or documentation surface, and its standalone website (invetx.com) has been decommissioned since the acquisition; this profile is retained as a network lead / portfolio record.

providers.name: Jacobio Pharma

providers.name: Senti Biosciences
providers.description: Senti Biosciences (Nasdaq: SNTI) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California that engineers programmable "Gene Circuits" into cell and gene therapies to treat cancer with greater precision and control. Its lead candidate, SENTI-202, is an off-the-shelf logic-gated CAR NK cell therapy in clinical trials for acute myeloid leukemia and other hematologic malignancies. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and menlo-ventures. As a therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Shasqi
providers.description: Shasqi is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing cancer treatment through click chemistry. Its CAPAC (Click Activated Protodrugs Against Cancer) platform uses a pre-targeting approach that captures therapeutic payloads at the tumor via in-vivo click chemistry, separating tumor-targeting molecules from their drug payloads and reuniting them at the cancer site to maximize drug delivery while reducing systemic toxicity. The company builds on the 2022 Nobel Prize-winning click chemistry work and operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a technology or API platform. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company; enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform surface.

providers.name: shsongli
providers.description: shsongli (Shanghai Pine & Power / Songli Biotech Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based biotechnology and medical-device maker specializing in the R&D, manufacture and sale of biological hemostatic products, most notably animal-derived quick-dissolving fibrin glue with independent IP, used in surgery and expanding into tissue engineering. The company operates a Class III medical-device line and is ISO 13485 and GMP certified. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. The enrichment pass found no public developer or API surface: the shsongli.com domain returns 404 on every path (EIMS web server) with an expired TLS certificate, and no docs, portal, packages, MCP, llms.txt, /.well-known/ endpoints, or security program were published.

providers.name: Sino Biological
providers.description: Sino Biological is a global life-science reagent supplier and contract research organization founded in 2007, headquartered in Beijing, China, with a US subsidiary in Wayne, Pennsylvania and offices across Europe. The company manufactures and sells recombinant proteins, antibodies, ELISA kits, cDNA clones, and other research reagents in-house, and provides contract biologics services (protein production, antibody development, gene synthesis) for academic, biopharmaceutical, and diagnostic customers worldwide. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company stub of Qiming Venture Partners, this profile was run through the enrichment pipeline; no public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic-access surface was discoverable (the corporate site is bot-protected and returns HTTP 403 to automated clients).

providers.name: Sinotau
providers.description: Sinotau (先通医药) is a Chinese pharmaceutical innovator specializing in the research, development, production, clinical application, and academic promotion of radiopharmaceuticals (nuclear medicine). Formally established in 2014, the company focuses on three therapeutic areas — oncology, neurology, and cardiology — and has brought its first innovative product, 欧韦宁 (Florbetaben Fluorine-18 injection for PET brain imaging), to market alongside a pipeline of 10+ products in development. Sinotau operates multiple R&D and production facilities, employs 400+ staff, and holds 80+ authorized patents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. As a corporate radiopharmaceutical manufacturer, Sinotau publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer platform, API, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: SQZ Biotech
providers.description: SQZ Biotech is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: life-sciences. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Stilla Technologies
providers.description: Stilla Technologies is a life-sciences instrumentation company that develops digital PCR (dPCR) systems, consumables, and assays, best known for its Naica system for Crystal Digital PCR and the Nio product line. With operations in France and the United States, its technology serves oncology diagnostics, cell and gene therapy, and infectious-disease testing. Stilla was acquired by Bio-Rad Laboratories (announced February 2025, ~$225M plus up to $50M in milestones, closed 2025); its web properties now redirect to Bio-Rad. The company operates laboratory hardware and consumables rather than a public developer platform — no OpenAPI, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or MCP surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Stipple Bio
providers.description: Stipple Bio is a preclinical precision-oncology biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2022 by cancer-biology researchers Aaron Ring (Fred Hutch) and Aashish Manglik (UCSF). Its Pointillist Platform performs cellular profiling and tumor-specific epitope discovery to design antibody binders and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that target tumor-specific cell-surface epitopes while avoiding on-target, off-tumor toxicity. Its lead asset, STP-100, is an ADC advancing toward early clinical studies. The company emerged from stealth in April 2026 with an oversubscribed $100M Series A co-led by RA Capital, a16z Bio+Health and Nextech Invest, with participation from Google Ventures (gv). As a therapeutics company, Stipple Bio publishes no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface.

providers.name: Stylus Medicine
providers.description: Stylus Medicine is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing in vivo genetic medicines built on engineered recombinases. Its platform aims to generate precise, durable CAR-T cells directly inside the body using cell-targeted lipid nanoparticle delivery to immune cells, with therapeutic programs spanning oncology, autoimmune disease, and genetic disorders. The company is a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures. It operates as a research-stage therapeutics company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Superluminal Medicines
providers.description: Superluminal Medicines is a drug discovery company that combines structure-based drug discovery with AI-powered computational methods and experimental validation to identify and develop small molecule therapeutics. Its pipeline targets G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) for cardiometabolic disease and obesity, including a collaboration with Eli Lilly worth up to $1.3 billion. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: SURGE Therapeutics
providers.description: SURGE Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing intraoperative cancer immunotherapy. Founded on research from Dr. Michael Goldberg's laboratory at Harvard Medical School, the company's SURGERx platform is an injectable, biodegradable hydrogel placed directly at the site of surgical tumor resection to provide extended, localized release of immunotherapy — addressing the surgery-induced inflammation that suppresses the immune system and allows residual disease to reawaken. Its lead program, SRG-514, completed Phase 1 dose escalation in breast cancer patients undergoing surgery and is being prepared for a registrational trial, with an additional IND cleared for a Phase 1/2a study in bladder cancer. SURGE has raised a $26M Series A and a $32M Series B. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software company, and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Syremis Therapeutics
providers.description: Syremis Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Tel Aviv, Israel and Boston, Massachusetts, developing best-in-class oral small-molecule medicines for serious mental health conditions. Its neuropsychiatric pipeline is rooted in clinically validated mechanisms including muscarinic M1/M4 agonism and next-generation NMDA antagonism; lead program ST-905 is a dual M1/M4 agonist in Phase 1 for schizophrenia, with ST-901 also spun out from Clexio Biosciences. The company launched publicly in December 2025 with a $165M Series A co-led by Dexcel Pharma and Third Rock Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Life Sciences, GV (Google Ventures), QVT, and Pictet. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV. This company publishes no public API, developer, or event surface at this time.

providers.name: Taysha Gene Therapies *
providers.description: Taysha Gene Therapies is a clinical-stage biotechnology company (Dallas, TX with a laboratory in Morrisville, NC) developing AAV-based gene therapies for rare monogenic diseases of the central nervous system. Its lead program, TSHA-102, targets Rett syndrome and has completed dosing in the REVEAL pivotal trial. The company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or technical integration surface; it was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: TenSixteen Bio
providers.description: TenSixteen Bio is a San Francisco-based clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the study of somatic mosaicism and clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) to discover and develop novel therapeutics for age-related diseases including cancer and cardiovascular disease. Founded by CEO Mark Chao and launched in 2022 with a $40M Series A from Foresite Capital and GV (formerly Google Ventures), the company combines human genetics, functional genomics and next-generation-sequencing (NGS) based assays to identify CHIP-linked mutations and translate them into companion diagnostics and precision-medicine treatments. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as a therapeutics and diagnostics company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: TenSixty Bio
providers.description: TenSixty Bio is an oncology-focused biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, working to revolutionize the treatment of cancer. The company combines biology, machine learning, and high-throughput technologies to build an atlas of antibody targets on the surface of cancer cells, discover novel cancer targets, and develop improved therapeutics from bench to bedside. TenSixty Bio is a privately held research-stage company backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital, and it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-capital portfolio pipeline and enriched with verified public company identity.

providers.name: TRIANA Biomedicines
providers.description: TRIANA Biomedicines is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: tripod-glp
providers.description: tripod-glp resolves to TriApex Laboratories, a next-generation pharmaceutical and biomedical contract research organization (CRO) headquartered in Nanjing, China with facilities in Shanghai, Kunming, Wenchang and Pennsylvania. TriApex provides integrated nonclinical services (safety assessment, efficacy, DMPK and research models) and clinical trial services across phases I-III, with disease expertise spanning cardiometabolic, CNS, ophthalmology, autoimmune and oncology. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, it publishes a corporate website (www.tri-apex.com) but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Trisk Bio
providers.description: Trisk Bio is a preclinical AAV (adeno-associated virus) manufacturing partner / CDMO that develops bespoke, scalable processes for AAV gene therapies to enable affordable preclinical manufacturing. It supplies research-grade and non-human primate (NHP) study-grade vectors across capsid serotypes and transgenes, offering custom process development, high-throughput optimisation of a single transgene against multiple capsids, and purification and supply of partials as reference material. Backed by Matrix Partners, Trisk Bio is a healthtech / biomanufacturing company; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing website but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TScan Therapeutics
providers.description: TScan Therapeutics (Nasdaq: TCRX) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Waltham, Massachusetts developing T-cell receptor engineered T-cell (TCR-T) therapies for the treatment of patients with cancer. The company uses a high-throughput, genome-wide target-discovery platform to identify the TCRs and antigen targets that drive T-cell recognition of tumors, building a multiplexed library of TCR-T candidates (ImmunoBank) for both hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Lead programs TSC-100 and TSC-101 target minor histocompatibility antigens to prevent disease relapse after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. As a therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and GV.

providers.name: Verge Labs
providers.description: Verge Labs (formerly Verge Genomics) is a frontier AI company applying machine learning to human biology, building an AI system designed to reason about neurological disease at the patient level. Its stated goal is a "virtual biopsy of the brain" — a reconstructed picture of what is happening inside a patient's brain generated from a routine blood draw. The company built proprietary genomic datasets from human brain tissue for neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS and Parkinson's, and after an early ALS clinical program refocused on AI methods for matching brain therapeutics to the patients most likely to benefit. Verge is a research-stage biotech/AI company backed by Threshold Ventures and other venture investors; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Verobioscience
providers.description: Vero Bioscience measures biological age at the organ level using advanced proteomics and machine learning. Its OrganAge test analyzes thousands of proteins from a single blood draw to detect the earliest molecular signs of organ-specific aging, enabling targeted interventions to slow or reverse the aging process. The company is a Khosla Ventures-backed longevity and diagnostics startup whose work has been published in Nature and Nature Medicine. As of this enrichment pass Vero Bioscience operates a consumer waitlist and partnership program and exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Verve Therapeutics
providers.description: Verve Therapeutics is a Boston-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of in vivo gene editing medicines designed to treat cardiovascular disease with a single, one-time treatment. Its programs use base editing and CRISPR technology to durably switch off disease-driving genes, led by VERVE-102 (targeting PCSK9 to lower LDL cholesterol), alongside VERVE-201 (ANGPTL3) and VERVE-301 (LPA). Verve was acquired by Eli Lilly in July 2025 in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. As a therapeutics/research company it publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Vicinitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Vicinitas Therapeutics is a biotechnology company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. It operates in the therapeutics and drug-discovery space (vicinitastx.com) and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. This profile records what is verifiable about the company and remains a lead awaiting any future API footprint.

providers.name: Vir Biotechnology
providers.description: Vir Biotechnology is a clinical-stage immunology company that engineers antibodies into medicines targeting serious infectious diseases and cancer. Its programs span chronic hepatitis delta, hepatitis B, oncology, and prior work on COVID-19 and Ebola, built on a next-generation antibody platform and the licensed PRO-XTEN protease-releasable masking technology. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a corporate/investor-facing life-sciences company; enrichment probes found no public developer, API, or partner-integration surface.

providers.name: Visterra
providers.description: Visterra is a Waltham, Massachusetts biologics research company developing antibody-based therapeutics for patients with immune-mediated and other difficult-to-treat diseases. It combines computational design, artificial intelligence, and experimental research with agile preclinical development and manufacturing. Visterra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Xilis
providers.description: Xilis is a life-sciences / precision-oncology company developing patient-derived MicroOrganoSphere (MOS) technology to model a patient's tumor outside the body for functional drug testing and drug discovery. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment probes found a marketing website only (SiteGround-hosted, bot-protection returns HTTP 403) with no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Zenasbio
providers.description: Zenas BioPharma is a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and delivering transformative treatments for patients with autoimmune and rare diseases. Its lead candidates are obexelimab, a bifunctional monoclonal antibody that inhibits B-cell activity without depleting B cells, and orelabrutinib, an oral central-nervous-system-penetrant BTK inhibitor. The company serves patients, caregivers, investors, and job seekers through its corporate website; it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Bolt Threads
providers.description: Bolt Threads, Inc. was a San Francisco Bay Area biomaterials company founded in 2009 to engineer protein- and mycelium-based materials. It is best known for Microsilk, a bioengineered spider-silk fiber; Mylo, a mycelium-derived leather alternative developed with partners including adidas, Kering, Lululemon, Patagonia and Stella McCartney; and b-silk protein, a silk-protein ingredient for beauty and personal care. The company went public on Nasdaq in August 2024 via a SPAC business combination under the ticker BSLK, halted Mylo production, was suspended from Nasdaq in January 2026, and now trades OTC Pink while deregistering with the SEC. Its website serves only a notice that the company is no longer operating. Bolt Threads was a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor, and never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: NewLimit
providers.description: NewLimit is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Parexel International
providers.description: Parexel International is one of the largest global biopharmaceutical services companies in the world, providing services that help clients accelerate the discovery and development of new therapies. No public developer API has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Adona Medical
providers.description: Adona Medical is a clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in Los Gatos, California, and a Shifamed portfolio company, developing an adjustable interatrial shunt with integrated bi-atrial pressure monitoring for patients with advanced heart failure. The implant uses nitinol shape-memory geometry so the shunt flow channel can be enlarged or reduced after implantation, allowing hemodynamic therapy to be re-titrated as a patient's condition evolves. The company completed enrollment in its ATHENS-HF first-in-human study of the device. Adona Medical is a device and clinical company rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specifications, and its device is investigational and not approved for sale.

providers.name: AllStripes
providers.description: AllStripes was a San Francisco healthcare technology company, founded in 2017 as RDMD by Nancy Yu and Onno Faber, that built a research platform dedicated to rare disease. It retrieved, digitized and de-identified patients' medical records into regulatory-ready real-world evidence for biopharma drug development, and paired that with a patient application through which families affected by conditions such as Batten disease, Hunter syndrome and sickle cell anemia could participate in treatment research from home. The company raised roughly $74M in venture funding, including a $50M Series B in August 2021 led by Lux Capital with JAZZ Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Medidata, McKesson Ventures and Maveron. PicnicHealth acquired AllStripes on October 23, 2023 and folded the platform into its own; the AllStripes brand has since been retired, and allstripes.com and app.allstripes.com now issue blanket 301 redirects to picnichealth.com. AllStripes never published a public developer portal, REST/OpenAPI contract, SDK, or webhook surface, and no such surface survives the acquisition.

providers.name: Atia Vision
providers.description: Atia Vision, Inc. is a clinical-stage ophthalmic medical device company headquartered in Campbell, California, and a portfolio company of the Shifamed medical innovation hub. It develops the OmniVu modular shape-changing intraocular lens (IOL) — a two-part implant pairing a fluid-filled, shape-changing base with an exchangeable fixed-power front optic — designed to work with the eye's natural accommodative mechanism to restore a full range of functional vision in cataract patients, and implanted using conventional cataract surgical technique. The company raised a $20M Series D and a $42M Series E, and in May 2025 the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted it an Investigational Device Exemption to begin a feasibility clinical study of the OmniVu Lens System; the device is investigational and is not approved for sale or use in the United States. Atia Vision is an implantable-device manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Bambusa Therapeutics
providers.description: Bambusa Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in the Boston Seaport, founded in 2024 by Shanshan Xu and Helmut Jeggle to develop next-generation bispecific antibodies for immunological and inflammatory (I&I) diseases. Its antibody-engineering platform combines half-life extension with high-concentration subcutaneous delivery, and its pipeline spans dermatology, respiratory, gastroenterology and rheumatology — led by BBT-001 (IL-31 x IL-4Ralpha, in a Phase 1b/2a atopic dermatitis trial) and BBT-002 for COPD. The company raised a Series Seed in 2024, an approximately $90M Series A led by RA Capital Management in February 2025, and an oversubscribed Series A-2 in November 2025. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, SDK or developer program.

providers.name: Cadence Neuroscience
providers.description: Cadence Neuroscience, Inc. is a clinical-stage medical device company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, developing a personalized neuromodulation system for pediatric and adult patients with focal drug-resistant epilepsy. Its implantable system, licensed from Mayo Clinic and incubated by a Mayo Clinic Rochester neurology and neurosurgery team, delivers chronic subthreshold cortical stimulation and detects EEG biomarkers of epileptiform activity in order to reduce or eliminate seizures. The company raised a $15M Series A in 2019 and a $26M Series B in 2023 led by the Angelini Lumira Biosciences Fund, with participation from F-Prime Capital, LivaNova USA, Angelini Ventures, Spectrum Financial Services and Mayo Clinic, and is using the proceeds to complete pivotal clinical studies and pursue FDA clearance. It is a regulated medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Faraday Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Faraday Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a Seattle, Washington clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 as a spinout of Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, built on the elemental-reducing-agent research of Dr. Mark Roth. It developed therapies intended to prevent and treat cardiac and skeletal muscle loss after acute critical illness, led by FDY-5301 — a proprietary intravenous formulation of sodium iodide designed to neutralize reactive oxygen species and limit reperfusion injury in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The company raised roughly $120M from an investor group led by ARCH Venture Partners and Polaris Partners. Its Phase 3 trial read out in late 2025 and failed to meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and Faraday announced in February 2026 that it had ceased operations and was winding down the business. Faraday never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its faradaypharma.com website is no longer served. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Abinitio Bio
providers.description: Abinitio Bio builds AI foundation models for biopharmaceutical manufacturing, positioning itself as the intelligence layer for drug manufacturing. Its first model, Echo, predicts manufacturing outcomes to assess manufacturability from day one through process scale-up — evaluating molecules early to reduce aggregation and regulatory liabilities, recommending optimal cell lines, media formulations, and bioprocess parameters, predicting process behavior across scales and operating conditions, and delivering lab-validated candidate molecules, processes, and characterization data ready for commercial scale-up. Founded in 2026 in Boston and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), MIT's Researcher-to-Entrepreneur Accelerator, and Fifty Years' 5050 Program. The company operates a B2B model with pharmaceutical companies and CDMOs and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Absci
providers.description: Absci is a Vancouver, Washington-based generative AI drug creation company (NASDAQ: ABSI) using AI and synthetic biology to design de novo antibodies in silico against specified epitopes. Its Integrated Drug Creation platform couples generative AI models — including the Origin-1 antibody foundation model — with a 77,000+ sq ft wet lab running proprietary SoluPro and ACE Assay technologies, screening millions of antibody sequence variants per cycle. The data flywheel between in silico design and high-throughput wet lab validation completes in as little as six weeks and can advance from target identification to development candidate in roughly 14 months. Absci's internal pipeline includes ABS-101, an anti-TL1A antibody for inflammatory bowel disease now in Phase 1; ABS-201, a novel anti-PRLR antibody for androgenetic alopecia in the Phase 1/2a HEADLINE trial; and ABS-301, a first-in-class AI-discovered oncology antibody. Strategic partnerships span AstraZeneca, Merck, Almirall, Twist Bioscience, NVIDIA, Owkin, Caltech, and the Gates Foundation. Absci's commercial model is therapeutic development (internal pipeline plus partnered programs and royalties); there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Origin-1 model or its drug creation platform.

providers.name: AgroSpheres
providers.description: AgroSpheres is an agricultural biotechnology company based in Charlottesville, Virginia, founded by University of Virginia researchers, that develops bio-based crop protection products built on its AgriCell bioparticle platform. The company uses a single-step fermentation process that produces and biodegradably encapsulates biological actives all at once, giving added stability and a tunable release profile for targeted, non-toxic pest and disease control intended to be safe for pollinators, people and soil. Its first commercial product, the broad-spectrum biofungicide FUN-THYME, is marketed through an exclusive partnership with Wilbur-Ellis and was approved in California in 2026. AgroSpheres manufactures at a biomanufacturing facility in Charlottesville. It is a physical agricultural-inputs business and publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco biotechnology company developing an RNA-based gene-editing platform capable of making multi-kilobase edits — rewriting thousands of bases on a single RNA strand in one step — to reach previously undruggable patient populations. Because edited RNA eventually degrades in the body, the approach is designed to be safer and reversible compared with permanent DNA editing.
