The platform pairs multi-kilobase RNA writing with AI foundation models to target diverse pathogenic variants across patients with a single product, initially focused on ophthalmology and central nervous system diseases. Founded by CRISPR-field researchers from the Broad Institute and UC Berkeley (co-founder and CTO Basem Al-Shayeb, advised by Nobel Laureate Jennifer Doudna), Amber Bio launched in 2023 with a $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz. It has no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Aurora Therapeutics
providers.description: Aurora Therapeutics is a CRISPR gene-editing biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing scalable, personalized genetic medicines for rare diseases. Founded by gene-editing pioneers including Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Fyodor Urnov and led by CEO Edward M. Kaye, the company uses an "umbrella" approach that bundles multiple rare disease-causing mutations under a single regulatory pathway, combining guide RNA design, AI-engineered editors, and delivery systems to correct mutations at scale. Backed by Menlo Ventures, Aurora is profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes a corporate website and news surface but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical/developer surface.

providers.name: Brilliant Planet
providers.description: Brilliant Planet is a carbon-removal company that grows microalgae in open-air ponds on otherwise-unproductive coastal desert land, using seawater rather than fresh water, to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide at scale. Harvested algal biomass is dried and stored to lock the captured carbon away durably, while the process also deacidifies the seawater it returns. The company operates research and demonstration facilities in coastal Morocco and is developing measurement, reporting, and verification approaches for its nature-based carbon capture. It is backed by Union Square Ventures and other climate-focused investors. This API Evangelist profile is a company/provider record; Brilliant Planet publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time (its primary web presence is access-restricted).

providers.name: C16 Biosciences
providers.description: C16 Biosciences is a New York City based synthetic biology company producing high-performance, sustainable ingredients for consumer goods manufacturers through its proprietary Palmless platform. Using microbial fermentation and biotechnology, C16 designs plant-free, deforestation-free alternatives to palm oil and petroleum-derived commodity ingredients for beauty and personal care, food, and home and personal care markets. Its flagship Palmless Torula Oil is a bioactive super-emollient with antioxidant properties for skincare formulations, alongside designer fats, oils, fatty acids, triglycerides, and alcohols. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCVC; it is an ingredients and biomanufacturing business and does not currently publish a public developer platform or API.

providers.name: Capacity Bio
providers.description: Capacity Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing mitophagy therapeutics to restore mitochondrial quality control in age- and disease-related conditions. Its platform advances small molecules, peptides, and nanoparticles that enhance identification and clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria. With operations in Los Angeles and Tokyo, the company closed a $35M financing round in 2023 and is backed by Insight Partners. As a drug-development firm, Capacity Bio publishes no public API, developer platform, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Dvlp Medicines
providers.description: DVLP Medicines is a drug-development software company building an end-to-end, configurable platform that moves molecules from discovery to commercialization with speed. The platform pairs a single data repository for pharmaceutical assets with specialized AI agents for pharma operations, document automation, knowledge synthesis, and decision support for portfolio management. It is positioned as a software co-pilot for drug development and a marketplace connecting project leaders with investors and outsourced R&D and manufacturing vendors, targeting underserved therapeutic markets such as new antibiotics for antimicrobial resistance and rare-disease therapies. DVLP Medicines is a portfolio company of DCVC (Computational Bio & Chem), first funded in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company publishes a marketing site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Elevation Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Elevation Pharmaceuticals was a San Diego specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2008 by Cam Garner, Bill Gerhart, and Ahmet Tutuncu to develop next-generation aerosol/inhalation therapies for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It raised a $30 million Series A in 2010 backed by Canaan Partners, TPG Growth, Care Capital, and Mesa Verde Venture Partners, and was acquired by Sunovion Pharmaceuticals in August 2012. The company is no longer independently operating; its domain now resolves to Sunovion nameservers and it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio record.

providers.name: Fable Therapeutics
providers.description: Fable Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing protein-engineered biologics for obesity and metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, FBL-140, is an infrequently dosed monoclonal antibody antagonizing the activin receptor type II (ActR2) pathway to reduce body weight and fat while preserving lean muscle mass and improving cardiometabolic health, with clinical trials expected to begin in early 2027. The company is also advancing a combination therapy pairing ActR2 antagonism with an incretin mimetic. Fable Therapeutics is a deep-tech portfolio company backed by DCVC. It operates as a traditional drug-development company and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or technical platform.

providers.name: Faircraft
providers.description: Faircraft is a biotechnology company creating a new class of cultivated materials, starting with real leather grown in the lab from animal cells rather than raised on farms. Using cell biology and protein engineering, it produces genuine leather (product lines FCL_001 through FCL_006) with the look, feel, and performance of traditional hides but with a lower environmental footprint and no animal farming, and customizable properties for fashion, automotive, and luxury brands. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Faircraft is a materials-science company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Fyodor Biotechnologies
providers.description: Fyodor Biotechnologies is a Baltimore, Maryland based biotechnology company focused on making malaria diagnosis fast, affordable, and non-invasive. Its flagship product, the Urine Malaria Test (UMT), is a rapid diagnostic that detects active malaria infection from a urine sample in minutes without a blood draw, working much like a home pregnancy test so it can be used at the point of care or at home in regions where malaria is endemic. The test has been validated through partnerships with Johns Hopkins University, Duke University, and the University of Lagos, carries a CE Mark, and has secured regulatory approvals in Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire, Kenya, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Fyodor was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes no public developer platform, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Genvec
providers.description: GenVec was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Gaithersburg, Maryland, that pioneered adenovector (AdenoVerse) gene-delivery technology to develop gene-based therapeutics and vaccines, including programs for hearing loss and balance disorders. Backed by Canaan Partners, ARCH Venture Partners, EDF Ventures and HealthCare Ventures, GenVec was acquired by Precigen (formerly Intrexon) on June 16, 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; the genvec.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Insamo
providers.description: Insamo is a biotechnology company building membrane-permeable, orally available cyclic peptides that combine the binding affinity of antibodies with the pharmacology of small molecules for drug discovery. Its platform automates the design, synthesis, and testing of peptides at large scale and applies machine learning across vast chemical spaces to identify therapeutic candidates. Founded in February 2024 with $12M from Playground Global, venBio, and MRL Ventures Fund, the company operates from Berkeley, California and Chippendale, New South Wales, Australia. Insamo currently publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Intrepida Bio
providers.description: Intrepida Bio, Inc. is a preclinical biotechnology company (founded 2019, headquartered in Encinitas / San Diego, CA) developing medicines that modulate the innate immune system to fight cancer and other diseases. Working with Biouniversa s.r.l., the company holds worldwide rights to develop proprietary monoclonal antibodies against the novel targets BAG3 and its receptor IFITM-2 — a signaling axis tumors hijack to build a growth-promoting, immune-evasive microenvironment (notably in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC). Intrepida raised roughly $9.5M from Canaan, Sofinnova, Indaco Venture Partners and Vertis to fund IND-enabling studies of its lead oncology program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. NOTE: this is a therapeutics/drug-discovery company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface; its website (intrepidabio.com) no longer resolves and the entity appears dormant/defunct, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Mammoth Biosciences
providers.description: Mammoth Biosciences is a genetic medicines company co-founded by CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, developing in vivo gene-editing therapeutics and CRISPR-based diagnostics. The company discovers and engineers novel CRISPR systems and proteins to overcome delivery challenges in genetic medicine, with the goal of creating permanent cures. It is a therapeutics- and diagnostics-focused biotechnology company rather than an API/platform provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or programmatic access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, Mayfield and SV Angel and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Manifold Bio
providers.description: Manifold Bio is a biotechnology company developing tissue-targeted biologic medicines. It runs a high-throughput in vivo discovery engine that pairs massively multiplexed in vivo screening — using mCode protein barcodes read out by DNA sequencing — with AI-powered protein and antibody design (mBER) and engineered mShuttle delivery vehicles. Its pipeline targets CNS diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's (amyloid-beta, tau, alpha-synuclein) and peripheral cardiometabolic disease. Backed by Playground Global. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or event surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Maxion Therapeutics
providers.description: Maxion Therapeutics is a UK biotechnology company developing protein therapeutics using its proprietary KnotBody technology, which fuses venom-derived knottin miniproteins with antibodies to drug previously untreatable ion channel- and GPCR-driven diseases across autoimmune, inflammatory, and related therapeutic areas. Maxion is a preclinical-stage drug-discovery company, not an API or developer-platform provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-tracking purposes and has no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: microTERRA
providers.description: microTERRA is a Mexico-based food-ingredient company that develops functional ingredients derived from Lemna (duckweed). Its MAS product line delivers natural flavor enhancers and texture modifiers for the food and beverage industry, positioned as sustainable, clean-label alternatives that support salt and sugar reduction in formulations. A Techstars-backed B2B startup, microTERRA sells to food formulators and manufacturers and does not currently expose any public developer API, SDK, CLI, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Molagri
providers.description: Molagri is a Toronto-based biotechnology startup building next-generation biopesticides for agriculture. The company designs pest-control molecules that target specific molecular pathways unique to pest insects while preserving pollinators and other beneficial organisms, and uses predictive modeling to stay ahead of the evolution of pest resistance. Molagri emphasizes higher efficacy and biobased production to reduce emissions across both manufacturing and field application. Founded in 2026 by University of Toronto PhD biochemists Zaky Hassan and Min Jin, the company was part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking; as an early-stage biotech it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Mycoworks
providers.description: MycoWorks is a San Francisco Bay Area biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2013 by artist Philip Ross and Sophia Wang, headquartered in Emeryville, California. It engineers premium leather-alternative biomaterials from mycelium using its patented Fine Mycelium process, sold under the Reishi brand to luxury fashion, automotive, and design partners. The company was backed by DCVC and other investors; it entered insolvency and was wound down through an Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors in late 2025. MycoWorks operates as a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Nobell Foods
providers.description: Nobell Foods is a molecular-farming food-technology company founded by Magi Richani that produces animal-free cheese from plant-grown casein. The company engineered soybean plants to grow the same dairy caseins found in animal milk, working with independent Midwest farmers to raise the crop from seed to flower, then converting the plant-derived proteins into cheese that melts, stretches, and tastes like conventional dairy. Backed by DCVC, Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, and investors including Bill Gates and Robert Downey Jr., Nobell raised a $75M Series B and has since rebranded to Alpine Bio, with Nobell Foods continuing as the animal-free cheese brand and product unit. It is a consumer-packaged-goods and biotech company with no public API or developer program; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity only.

providers.name: Nosh Bio
providers.description: Nosh.bio is a Berlin-based sustainable food-technology company founded in 2022 by Tim Fronzek and Felipe Lino that produces nutritional, highly functional proteins from non-GMO fungi via proprietary precision fermentation. Its flagship Koji Protein and Koji-Beef mince hybrid are mycelium-derived, clean-label mycoprotein ingredients with binding, gelling and texturizing properties, sold B2B to manufacturers across meat alternatives, seafood, dairy, sauces, confectionery, wellness and pet food. The company is a foodtech portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital and closed a EUR 3.2M seed round. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Nosh.bio publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Novira Therapeutics
providers.description: Novira Therapeutics was a biopharmaceutical company developing direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis B (HBV), notably HBV capsid assembly modulators. It was acquired by Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its domain (noviratherapeutics.com) is now run on Johnson & Johnson DNS and mail infrastructure with no public website, developer portal, or API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners; the enrichment pipeline confirms there is no API or developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Odyssey Therapeutics
providers.description: Odyssey Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing small-molecule and biologic therapeutics for autoimmune, inflammatory, and oncology indications. The company targets upstream immune signaling mechanisms to prevent pathological inflammation rather than only suppressing downstream responses, advancing a pipeline of precision medicines. It operates as a private, venture-backed drug-discovery company with no public developer or API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Omeat
providers.description: Omeat (rebranded as Evergreen Select) is a cultivated-beef company that partners with global meat producers to create price-predictable, industrial-scale beef supply. It produces 100% real beef without antibiotics, hormones, or plant-based fillers, positioning cultivated meat as a practical supplement to conventional supply chains while holding pricing at parity with commodity ground beef. Founded by tissue-engineering researcher Ali Khademhosseini and backed by GV, the company targets restaurants and meat processors seeking supply-chain stability and consistent quality. As of this enrichment pass Omeat operates as a food/biotech producer with a marketing website only: no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a company/lead record surfaced from the GV venture portfolio.

providers.name: Orbicle Bio
providers.description: Orbicle Bio is an agricultural biotechnology startup developing carbon-negative, microbial-based organic fertilizers derived from soil microbes to replace synthetic fertilizers. Backed by 500 Global, the company targets rice-farming productivity and soil sustainability across Southeast Asian markets such as Vietnam and Thailand, with a commercial product launch planned for 2026. Orbicle Bio publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness and enrichment.

providers.name: Patch Biosciences
providers.description: Patch Biosciences was a synthetic-biology and machine-learning company, founded in 2020 and based in New York, that built an AI platform for genetic sequence design — computationally engineering DNA "cargos" and regulatory elements to make gene and RNA therapies more effective, specific, and durable. It was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, Casdin Capital, and S32. Patch Biosciences was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in early 2024 and folded into Ginkgo's genetic-medicine services; it no longer operates as an independent company. Its former standalone website (patch.bio) is now parked and no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface exists. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record surfaced from a16z portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Pearlbio
providers.description: Pearl Bio is a synthetic biology company developing next-generation biomaterials for smart biologics. Its proprietary platform unites genome and ribosome engineering to produce novel biologics with diverse chemistries previously inaccessible, creating template-directed biomaterials with tunable properties by combining biological precision with chemical diversity. The company partnered with Merck on cancer-related biologics (announced March 2024) and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Pearl Bio operates as a research-and-partnership organization and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Plantner Inc.
providers.description: Plantner Inc. (PLANTNER) is a South Korean biotechnology company specializing in the extraction and manufacturing of alginic acid, a biodegradable marine-derived biomaterial. Operating as a bio-industry platform provider, Plantner supplies alginic acid-based solutions across medical devices (wound dressings, nutraceuticals), pharmaceuticals (gastroprotective agents, drug-delivery systems), cosmetics (modeling masks, hydrogels), advanced biotech (bio-ink, organoids, delivery carriers), and agriculture (controlled-release fertilizers, mulching films, eco-friendly herbicides). Headquartered in Seoul with an R&D center in Suwon, the company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a materials/biotech manufacturer and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Sample6
providers.description: Sample6 was a food-safety technology company (a Canaan Partners portfolio company) that developed rapid, bioluminescence-based pathogen detection and environmental monitoring products for the food industry, aimed at catching contamination such as Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli before product shipped. The business was acquired and absorbed into IEH Laboratories & Consulting Group; the sample6.com domain now redirects to iehinc.com. No independent developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts survive, so this record is retained as a historical company profile rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: SCiFi Foods
providers.description: SCiFi Foods was a San Francisco Bay Area food-technology startup, founded in 2019 by Joshua March (CEO) and Kasia Gora (CTO), that developed cultivated (cell-cultured) beef blended with plant-based ingredients to make burgers close to the taste of conventional meat. The company used a proprietary platform built on gene-editing tools such as CRISPR to create and screen hundreds of animal cell lines each month. Backed by a16z among others, SCiFi Foods raised roughly $40M before ceasing operations in June 2024; its cell lines were later released to academia via the Good Food Institute. The company is defunct and exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface.

providers.name: sinocelltech
providers.description: Sinocelltech (Beijing Sino Cell Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd.; Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market code 688520) is a biopharmaceutical research and development company founded in 2002 by Dr. Xie Liangzhi. It develops and commercializes recombinant protein and monoclonal antibody therapeutics across oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease, together with preventive vaccines including a recombinant 14-valent HPV vaccine and COVID-19 vaccines. The company has multiple marketed products in China and a pipeline of clinical-stage candidates. It publishes no public developer platform, API, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Solugen
providers.description: Solugen is a chemical manufacturing company that produces sustainable industrial chemicals through its proprietary Bioforge platform, which combines engineered enzymes, metal catalysis, and modular process design to convert renewable feedstocks into products with minimal waste. Solugen serves markets including oil and gas, renewable fuels, aerospace and defense, water treatment, cleaning, agriculture, concrete, and personal care. Backed by Founders Fund, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass Solugen publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Sonoma Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Sonoma Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing engineered regulatory T cell (Treg) therapies to restore immune balance in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Building on Nobel Prize-winning Treg biology, its lead program SBT-77-7101 is in Phase 1 clinical trials for conditions including refractory rheumatoid arthritis and hidradenitis suppurativa. Backed by 8VC and GV, the company operates in cell therapy and does not publish a public developer API surface. Sector: biotech.

providers.name: Soufflé Therapeutics
providers.description: Soufflé Therapeutics is a genetic medicine company developing nucleic acid (siRNA) therapeutics that use proprietary cell-specific ligand-conjugation technology to target and deliver treatments to specific cell types. Its initial programs address muscle and heart disorders, with first therapies targeting Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy (FSHD) and genetically-driven cardiomyopathies, with clinical trials expected to begin in 2026. The company is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts and was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It is a therapeutics/pharmaceutical company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Synthetic Design Lab
providers.description: Synthetic Design Lab is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancer therapy. Its SYNTHBODY platform and SYNTHBODY Engine engineer multispecific biologics with layered BIO-LOGIC control mechanisms and targeted payload delivery reported at 10x or more versus conventional ADCs. The company emerged from stealth in April 2025 with a $20M seed round led by Playground Global and Godfrey Capital, and is led by CEO Daniel S. Chen (formerly Global Head of Cancer Immunotherapy Development at Genentech) and CSO Ramesh Baliga. This is a therapeutics research company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Zymergen
providers.description: Zymergen was a synthetic-biology and bio-manufacturing company founded in 2013 in Emeryville, California, that used machine learning and automation to engineer microbes and discover novel bio-based materials and molecules. It went public on NASDAQ in 2021 and was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in October 2022; the zymergen.com domain now 301-redirects to Ginkgo Bioworks. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, Kindred Ventures, and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment found no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface — the company has no independent API footprint following the acquisition. This profile is retained as a portfolio/history record.

providers.name: Arresto Biosciences
providers.description: Arresto Biosciences, Inc. was a privately-held, development-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, focused on medicines to treat fibrotic diseases and cancer by targeting enzymes involved in the synthesis of the extracellular matrix. Its lead product was AB0024, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the human lysyl oxidase-like-2 (LOXL2) protein, then in Phase I studies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and advanced solid tumors. Founded circa 2007 and backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, HealthCare Ventures, Northgate Capital, DAG Ventures and Abbott Biotech Ventures, Arresto was acquired by Gilead Sciences for $225 million; the deal was announced December 20, 2010 and had closed by February 2011. The company no longer operates as an independent entity, publishes no developer or API surface, and its former domain (arrestobio.com) no longer resolves.

providers.name: Cambridge Cancer Genomics
providers.description: Cambridge Cancer Genomics (CCG.ai) was a Cambridge, UK precision-oncology company founded in 2015 out of the University of Cambridge, building OncOS, an AI/machine-learning platform that analyzed genomic data from liquid biopsies (circulating tumor DNA) to help oncologists track tumor evolution and personalize cancer treatment. The company was a Y Combinator alumnus in the digital-biology sector and was acquired by Dante Labs in June 2021, after which OncOS was folded into Dante Labs' genomics platform. As of this enrichment pass the CCG.ai domain redirects to a domain-sale marketplace and the company operates no independent public developer or API surface; its historical first-party code lives only in the ccgenomics GitHub organization (research repositories, not published API SDKs).

providers.name: PRA Health Sciences
providers.description: PRA Health Sciences was a global contract research organization (CRO) headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, providing outsourced clinical development services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. On July 1, 2021 ICON plc completed its acquisition of PRA Health Sciences in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $12 billion, forming one of the world's largest healthcare research organizations. Following the acquisition the PRA Health Sciences brand has been fully retired and operations were merged into ICON. The legacy prahs.com domain redirects to iconplc.com / icongroup.com and no PRA-branded developer programs, public APIs, SDKs, or technical documentation remain.

providers.name: Vineti
providers.description: Vineti was an enterprise software company for cell and gene therapy supply chain management, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 2016. Its Personalized Therapy Management (PTM) platform — sold as PTM Enterprise and PTM Essentials — orchestrated the patient-centric supply chain behind autologous and allogeneic cell therapies, gene therapies and personalized cancer vaccines: chain of identity, chain of custody, apheresis and manufacturing scheduling, clinical-site workflows, and regulatory reporting. PTM was delivered as a configurable aPaaS on AWS, with HIPAA compliance certified by Avertium and GAMP-aligned validation. Vineti was named a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and raised a $35M Series C in 2020. The PTM software was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2023 to continue supporting its commercial therapy rollouts and clinical trials, and Vineti ceased to operate as an independent company: vineti.com no longer resolves and the domain now sits on Johnson & Johnson name servers. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Alphina Therapeutics
providers.description: Alphina Therapeutics is a New Haven, Connecticut precision-oncology biotechnology company founded by experts in DNA repair and metabolic lethality. It develops next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that deliver potent NAMPT inhibitor payloads directly to tumors, designed to kill both dividing and non-dividing cancer cells, and pairs them with a proprietary companion diagnostic that identifies the patients most likely to respond. The company is venture-backed by Canaan Partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation, so no API artifacts apply at this time.

providers.name: General Proximity
providers.description: General Proximity is a biotechnology company pioneering next-generation "proximity medicines" that control biological processes by inducing proximity between molecular targets. Its multi-target OMNITAC platform is used to discover and advance novel therapeutics, including an oncology collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo. The company is backed by investors including Felicis and Y Combinator, and has drawn investment from Freemind and Daewoong Pharmaceutical. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; General Proximity is a drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Gilead Sciences
providers.description: Gilead Sciences is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and commercializes innovative therapeutics in areas of unmet medical need including HIV, viral hepatitis, oncology, and inflammatory diseases.

providers.name: Grove Biopharma
providers.description: Grove Biopharma is a Chicago-based biopharmaceutical company developing therapeutics that target intracellular protein-protein interactions implicated in cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and rare disorders. The company pioneered Bionic Biologics, hybrid biomolecules that integrate principles of biologic and synthetic design to achieve cell permeability with customizable, modular construction that can disrupt or degrade disease-causing proteins. Grove has demonstrated proof-of-concept against targets including AR/AR-V7, SHOC2, MYC, TAU, and KEAP1/NRF2. Founded in 2025 and led by CEO Geoffrey Duyk, the company raised a $30M Series A in April 2025 and is backed by DCVC. Grove is a therapeutics company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Terragia
providers.description: Terragia is a cellulosic biofuel company developing technology to convert cellulosic biomass such as agricultural crop residues into ethanol and other low-carbon fuels at a cost competitive with petroleum. The company uses consolidated bioprocessing (CBP) with co-treatment, employing engineered thermophilic bacteria to reduce the capital expense and number of steps in bioprocessing, targeting difficult-to-electrify transportation sectors like aviation and maritime shipping. Founded on decades of research led by Dr. Lee Lynd and supported by the US Department of Energy's Center for Bioenergy Innovation, Terragia spun out of Enchi in 2022 and is based in Lebanon, New Hampshire. It is backed by General Catalyst. Terragia is a biotech and energy company and publishes no public developer, API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: VectorY
providers.description: VectorY Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel genetic medicines for neurodegenerative diseases using its proprietary Vectorized Antibody Platform, which combines AAV-based gene delivery with antibody engineering to express therapeutic antibodies directly in the central nervous system. Its pipeline targets amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with VTx-002 and VTx-001 and Huntington's disease with VTx-003. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics research organization, VectorY publishes a corporate website, pipeline, scientific publications, news, and careers, but operates no public developer API, documentation portal, or programmatic interface surface.

providers.name: Vitalgen
providers.description: Shanghai Vitalgen BioPharma Co., Ltd. (Vitalgen), founded in March 2020 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, translates cutting-edge gene delivery and gene editing techniques into clinically effective treatments for patients with unmet medical needs. Vitalgen operates a GMP-compliant commercial production platform built on its proprietary ViCas CRISPR/Cas editing tools, ViLNP lipid nanoparticles, and ViVec AAV capsids, developing gene therapies for hereditary diseases and neurodegenerative disorders across a pipeline that includes Bietti Crystalline Dystrophy (VGR-R01), AADC Deficiency, Parkinson's Disease, Gaucher Disease, and Glutaric Acidemia Type I. Several candidates have entered clinical trials and secured U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designations and an EMA PRIME designation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a corporate marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Exact Sciences
providers.description: Exact Sciences is a molecular diagnostics company and a Fortune 1000 firm best known for the Cologuard colorectal cancer screening test and the Oncotype DX family of cancer tests. The company develops, manufactures, and markets laboratory-based screening and precision oncology tests delivered to patients and providers through its Exact Labs operations. Exact Sciences does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Abata Therapeutics
providers.description: Abata Therapeutics was a biotechnology company developing engineered regulatory T cell (Treg) therapies aimed at restoring immune tolerance in tissue-specific autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, with lead programs directed at progressive multiple sclerosis and type 1 diabetes. Founded in 2021 and based in the Boston/Cambridge area (Watertown, Massachusetts), the company was launched by Third Rock Ventures and counted Lightspeed Venture Partners among its backers. As a therapeutics developer it operated no public developer program, API, or documentation surface. As of this enrichment pass its corporate domains (abatatx.com and abatatherapeutics.com) resolve to a WP Engine host but serve an unconfigured "Site Not Configured" 404, indicating the public website has been deprovisioned and the company appears to have wound down.

providers.name: Advanced Biohealing
providers.description: Advanced BioHealing, Inc. was a regenerative medicine company best known for Dermagraft, a cryopreserved human fibroblast-derived dermal substitute used to treat diabetic foot ulcers. The company acquired the Dermagraft assets from Smith & Nephew in 2006, was backed by Canaan Partners and other venture investors, and was acquired by Shire plc for $750 million in cash in June 2011 to seed Shire's regenerative medicine business unit. Dermagraft was later sold to Organogenesis in 2014. Advanced BioHealing no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer portal, API, or programmatic surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company record.

providers.name: Agenovir
providers.description: Agenovir Corporation was a biotechnology company founded in 2014 to develop a novel class of human therapeutics targeting diseases caused by latent or persistent viral reservoirs. Built on CRISPR/Cas9 and other nuclease technology from the Stephen Quake lab at Stanford, it designed and simulated nucleases in silico at scale to disrupt intracellular viral DNA. It raised a $10.6M Series A led by DCVC (Data Collective) with Celgene and Lightspeed Venture Partners, and was acquired by Vir Biotechnology in 2018. It is a therapeutics company with no public developer, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Ai Vivo
providers.description: AI VIVO (AIVIVO LTD) is a Cambridge, England based drug-discovery company that combines systems pharmacology with artificial intelligence to accelerate the identification and de-risking of therapeutic candidates. Its "Organome" platform simulates biological processes at the target, cell, organ, and organism levels and ranks drug candidates by their phenotypic effects at the tissue level, without relying on prior knowledge of the disease or compounds. The approach gained recognition in 2020 when the platform ranked roughly 90,000 compounds for COVID-19 and surfaced dexamethasone as a top candidate weeks before its clinical benefit was widely reported. AI VIVO is backed by DCVC and other life-science and applied-AI investors. As of this profile the company publishes a minimal public web presence (a home and contact page) and exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: Ancora Biotech
providers.description: Ancora Biotech is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing breakthrough biotherapeutics for B cell cancers, metabolic diseases, and chronic hepatitis B infection. Formed by former Teneobio executives and venture investors, it oversees three therapeutic programs across separate spinoffs — TeneoTwo (TNB-486, a T cell engager in Phase I for B-cell malignancies), TeneoFour (TNB-738, an anti-CD38 antibody for inflammatory and metabolic disorders), and TeneoTen (an anti-HBV T cell engager for hepatitis B). It is a drug-development company with no public developer API or platform surface.

providers.name: Applied Biosystems
providers.description: Applied Biosystems is a life-sciences instrumentation brand now part of Thermo Fisher Scientific, known for genetic analysis and applied genomics platforms including real-time and end-point PCR (QuantStudio, StepOne, ViiA 7, ProFlex), Sanger capillary-electrophoresis sequencing (SeqStudio, 3500/3730 Genetic Analyzers), and mass spectrometry. Its software surface is delivered through Thermo Fisher Connect, a cloud platform for storing, analyzing, and sharing instrument data with Applied Biosystems qPCR and Sanger secondary-analysis modules, the Cloud Connect Utility for uploading data from non-cloud-enabled instruments, and the Instrument Connect remote-monitoring app. Applied Biosystems does not publish a standalone public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its programmatic footprint is instrument-connectivity and cloud analysis rather than a hosted web API. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity only.

providers.name: ARMO BioSciences *
providers.description: ARMO BioSciences was a clinical-stage immuno-oncology biopharmaceutical company based in Redwood City, California, developing biologic therapeutics that activate a patient's own immune system to fight cancer. Its lead candidate was pegilodecakin (AM0010), a PEGylated recombinant human interleukin-10 (IL-10) evaluated across solid tumors. Backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins, the company IPO'd on NASDAQ in 2018 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company that same year for approximately $1.6 billion; its former web domain now redirects to lilly.com. As a life-sciences therapeutics developer it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Arsanis *
providers.description: Arsanis was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in the life-sciences sector, focused on developing monoclonal antibody immunotherapies to prevent and treat serious infectious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. Arsanis operated as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider, and the company no longer exists as an independent entity; its public web presence at arsanis.com is no longer served. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph lead with no active developer, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Babylon Bio
providers.description: Babylon Bio (Babylon Biosciences) is a San Francisco-based drug discovery and development company founded in 2023 and backed by Lux Capital. Staffed by experienced medicinal chemists and biologists with a track record of discovering FDA-approved medicines, the company develops therapeutics that rescue essential functions in the brain rather than clearing emergent pathology, leveraging a proprietary high-throughput assay platform with an early focus on neurodegenerative disease including Alzheimer's. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private, pre-commercial biotech it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Bestcomm
providers.description: Bestcomm (Bestcomm Pharmaceutical) is a China-based pharmaceutical company backed by IDG Capital, surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates in the healthcare / life-sciences sector and raised venture funding alongside IDG Capital and regional investors. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer it has no known public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or programmatic API surface; this profile remains a company lead rather than an API provider. It is distinct from the unrelated BestComm Networks wireless-LAN company.

providers.name: Biophero
providers.description: BioPhero is a Danish agricultural biotechnology company that engineers microbes to produce synthetic insect pheromones via microbial fermentation, providing low-cost, bio-based pest control that disrupts insect mating cycles on major row crops without toxic insecticides. Founded as a spin-out from the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), BioPhero raised a DCVC Bio-led Series A (with FMC Ventures, Syngenta Group Ventures, and Novo Holdings) and was subsequently acquired by FMC Corporation. The company is a DCVC portfolio holding surfaced in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a research and product organization in synthetic biology and crop protection and publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or agent-facing surface.

providers.name: bioscience-tj
providers.description: Bioscience (Tianjin) Diagnostic Technology Co., Ltd. (博奥赛斯) is a Chinese in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company that integrates R&D, manufacturing, marketing, and technical support for diagnostic instruments and reagents. Its product lines span chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) and point-of-care testing (POCT) analyzers together with the supporting reagent kits used in clinical laboratories and hospitals. The company is headquartered in Tianjin, China and is a healthcare portfolio company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It manufactures medical diagnostic devices and consumables rather than publishing a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead, and no public API, developer portal, documentation, or specification surface has been found at this time.

providers.name: Bipar Sciences
providers.description: BiPar Sciences was a Brisbane, California biopharmaceutical company developing a tumor-selective class of PARP (poly ADP-ribose polymerase) inhibitors for cancer therapy. Its lead candidate, BSI-201 (iniparib), was in mid-stage trials for advanced breast, ovarian, and other tumors. Backed by Canaan Partners, Vulcan Capital, PolyTechnos, Asset Management Company, and Quantum Technology Partners, BiPar was acquired by Sanofi-Aventis for roughly $500 million in April 2009 and no longer operates as an independent company. It was surfaced as a Canaan Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment finds no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Calixa Therapeutics
providers.description: Calixa Therapeutics was a privately held, San Diego-based biopharmaceutical company focused on developing antibiotics to treat serious infections caused by multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens. Its lead compound, CXA-201 (later ceftolozane/tazobactam), was an intravenous therapy for serious hospital-acquired Gram-negative infections. Calixa was acquired by Cubist Pharmaceuticals in December 2009 for approximately $92.5 million (plus up to $310 million in milestone payments) and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer or API surface. This profile exists in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub associated with canaan-partners; there are no API artifacts to enrich because it is a defunct pharmaceutical company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Cell Design Labs
providers.description: Cell Design Labs, Inc. was a biotherapeutics company based at 5858 Horton Street, Emeryville, California, that engineered immune cells into "smart, living therapies" for cancer and other diseases. Its platform was a toolkit of proprietary molecular modules — including synthetic Notch (synNOTCH) receptors and programmable, combinatorial-antigen CAR-T circuits developed out of Wendell Lim's lab at UCSF — deployed inside an immune cell to program its specificity and control its killing force, so a therapy recognizes a disease signature and neutralizes it without harming adjacent tissue. The company ran an exclusive research collaboration with Kite Pharma (announced June 2016) on molecular on/off switches for CAR T-cell immunotherapies, and was acquired by Gilead Sciences, announced 7 December 2017. Cell Design Labs no longer operates as an independent company: celldesignlabs.com is dead (DNS resolves to a parked address, HTTP times out; the archived site shows an expired Squarespace subscription). It published no developer program, API, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, and none exists to enrich.

providers.name: Cell Pathways
providers.description: Cell Pathways, Inc. (CPI) was a development-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at 702 Electronic Drive, Horsham, Pennsylvania, focused on the research and development of products to treat and prevent cancer. Incorporated in Delaware in July 1998 (as Cell Pathways Holdings, Inc., renamed Cell Pathways, Inc. in February 2001), it developed a class of compounds it called selective apoptotic anti-neoplastic drugs (SAANDs), designed to induce selective apoptosis — programmed cell death — in precancerous and cancerous cells without affecting normal cells. Its lead candidate was Aptosyn (exisulind), studied in precancerous lesions such as colonic polyps and cervical dysplasia and later in prostate, lung, and breast cancer; the company also imported, promoted, and sold Gelclair Concentrated Oral Gel into oncology and dental markets, and had previously marketed Nilandron. It traded on the Nasdaq National Market (Commission File No. 000-24889) and employed approximately 34 people full-time as of March 1, 2003. In February 2003 Cell Pathways signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger to be acquired by OSI Pharmaceuticals, Inc. in a stock-for-stock exchange; stockholders approved the merger on June 10, 2003, and the company filed a Form 15-12G on June 12, 2003 terminating its Exchange Act registration with one holder of record. OSI Pharmaceuticals was itself acquired by Astellas Pharma and deregistered on June 18, 2010. Cell Pathways predates the API economy entirely, never operated a developer program or public API surface, and no longer exists as an operating entity. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cellular Research
providers.description: Cellular Research, Inc. was a single-cell genomics company backed by Canaan Partners that developed molecular-indexing (its "Precise" assay) technology for high-throughput single-cell gene expression analysis. The company was acquired by Becton Dickinson (BD) in 2015 and its technology became the foundation of the BD Rhapsody single-cell analysis platform. As a life-sciences instrument and reagent company folded into BD, it exposes no independent public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead identity record only.

providers.name: Civitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Civitas Therapeutics was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 (Chelsea/Cambridge, Massachusetts) that developed inhaled therapeutics using the proprietary ARCUS dry-powder pulmonary delivery platform. Its lead program, CVT-301, was an inhaled levodopa therapy for the rapid relief of OFF episodes in Parkinson's disease patients. The company was acquired by Acorda Therapeutics in 2014 for approximately $525 million and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a life-sciences / drug-development company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or technical integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and retained in the API Evangelist network for provenance.

providers.name: Combinatorx
providers.description: CombinatoRx, Inc. was a Cambridge/Boston, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (SEC CIK 0001135906, SIC 2834 Pharmaceutical Preparations, incorporated in Delaware) that pursued combination drug discovery — screening pairs of approved drugs for synergistic therapeutic effects. It registered with the SEC in 2002 and traded publicly following its 2005 IPO. The company was renamed Zalicus Inc. in September 2010 after its combination with Neuromed Pharmaceuticals, and renamed again to EPIRUS Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. in July 2014 after merging with EPIRUS. EPIRUS was delisted in September 2016 (Form 25-NSE) and its SEC registration was formally revoked on 2024-05-14. The company is defunct: it operated no developer program and published no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, and combinatorx.com is now a parked NameBright listing unrelated to the original company. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Canaan Partners portfolio company and has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Comprehend
providers.description: Comprehend Systems, Inc. was a clinical-trials software company that built SaaS analytics for the life-sciences industry. Its flagship product, Comprehend Clinical, let clinical data managers and executives monitor studies and make real-time decisions across multiple source systems without moving the underlying data. The company raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series B in 2014 and was acquired by Saama Technologies in 2019, after which the standalone Comprehend product and the comprehend.com domain were retired. This API Evangelist profile is a Lightspeed portfolio lead; the company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no live developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: coremed
providers.description: CoreMed (Beijing) Biomedical Research Co., Ltd. is a China-based contract research organization (CRO) founded in 2013 that provides clinical professional services for innovative cardiovascular medical devices and structural-heart products. Its services span animal testing, human clinical trials, data management, statistical analysis, and independent core-laboratory imaging analysis, and it was among the first domestic providers in China to run trials for interventional heart valves, LAA occluders, and bioresorbable scaffolds. Headquartered in Beijing with branches in Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Chengdu, CoreMed is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. This is a services/CRO company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface; its site (coremed.com.cn) was unreachable at enrichment time (connection refused, expired TLS cert).

providers.name: Crescendo Bioscience
providers.description: Crescendo Bioscience was a molecular-diagnostics company based in South San Francisco, known for Vectra DA (later Vectra), a multi-biomarker blood test that measures disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and other venture investors, it was acquired by Myriad Genetics in 2014 and its diagnostic product now sits within Myriad. It has no independent public developer surface: no API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, and its former domains no longer resolve. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Dermira
providers.description: Dermira was a biopharmaceutical company focused on medical dermatology, developing and commercializing treatments for chronic skin conditions such as primary axillary hyperhidrosis (Qbrexza / glycopyrronium) and atopic dermatitis (lebrikizumab). Headquartered in Menlo Park, California and originally backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, the company went public on NASDAQ (DERM) in 2014 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company in 2020. Its assets and operations are now part of Eli Lilly; the dermira.com domain redirects to lilly.com. Dermira did not operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity only and has no API artifacts to enrich.
